verses.text:
स तां पुष्करिणीं गत्वा पद्मोत्पलझषाकुलाम्।
रामः सौमित्रिसहितो विललापाकुलेन्द्रियः॥ १॥
verses.m: Reaching alongwith Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) the aforesaid pond abounding in lotuses, lilies and fishes, Śrī Rāma, whose mind was troubled, burst into a wail. (1)

verses.text:
तत्र दृष्ट्वैव तां हर्षादिन्द्रियाणि चकम्पिरे।
स कामवशमापन्नः सौमित्रिमिदमब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Immediately on seeing the pond there the senses of Śrī Rāma felt excited through delight. Fallen a prey to love, he spoke as follows to Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) : (2)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे शोभते पम्पा वैदूर्यविमलोदका।
फुल्लपद्मोत्पलवती शोभिता विविधैर्द्रुमैः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Containing full-blown lotuses and lilies and adorned with trees of every description, and with its water transparent as a cat’s-eye gem, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), Pampā looks charming. (3)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाः काननं शुभदर्शनम्।
यत्र राजन्ति शैला वा द्रुमाः सशिखरा इव॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the woodland surrounding Pampā, so pleasant to the sight, the trees looking as though crested with their towering boughs, spread their charm like mountains. (4)

verses.text:
मां तु शोकाभिसंतप्तमाधयः पीडयन्ति वै।
भरतस्य च दुःखेन वैदेह्या हरणेन च॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Agonies of various kinds for their part undoubtedly afflict me, sore-stricken as I already am with grief caused by Bharata’s sad plight and the abduction of Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory. (5)

verses.text:
शोकार्तस्यापि मे पम्पा शोभते चित्रकानना।
व्यवकीर्णा बहुविधैः पुष्पैः शीतोदका शिवा॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The delightful Pampā, which is lined by a picturesque woodland and interspersed with flowers of various kinds and is known for its cool water, fascinates me, stricken though I am with grief. (6)

verses.text:
नलिनैरपि संछन्ना ह्यत्यर्थशुभदर्शना।
सर्पव्यालानुचरिता मृगद्विजसमाकुला॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Though thickly covered with lotuses, infested with serpents and beasts of prey and surrounded by deer and birds, it actually wears an exceedingly pleasant aspect. (7)

verses.text:
अधिकं प्रविभात्येतन्नीलपीतं तु शाद्वलम्।
द्रुमाणां विविधैः पुष्पैः परिस्तोमैरिवार्पितम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Scattered with blossoms of various kinds dropped from trees, this turf, which presents a blue and yellow hue, looks extremely charming, overspread, as it were, with carpets. (8)

verses.text:
पुष्पभारसमृद्धानि शिखराणि समन्ततः।
लताभिः पुष्पिताग्राभिरुपगूढानि सर्वतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Enriched by loads of flowers on all sides, the tree-tops stand entwined all-round by climbers with blossomed ends. (9)

verses.text:
सुखानिलोऽयं सौमित्रे कालः प्रचुरमन्मथः।
गन्धवान् सुरभिर्मासो जातपुष्पफलद्रुमः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “This month of Caitra (the first month of the vernal season, roughly corresponding to the month of March), O Lakṣmaṇa, represents a period of agreeable breezes, awakening deep love and full of pride (on this achievement), when trees blossom and bear fruit. (10)

verses.text:
पश्य रूपाणि सौमित्रे वनानां पुष्पशालिनाम्।
सृजतां पुष्पवर्षाणि वर्षं तोयमुचामिव॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the scenery of these woods adorned with flowers and raining volumes of flowers like clouds discharging showers. (11)

verses.text:
प्रस्तरेषु च रम्येषु विविधाः काननद्रुमाः।
वायुवेगप्रचलिताः पुष्पैरवकिरन्ति गाम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Nay, shaken by the tempo of blasts, forest trees of every description standing in the midst of pleasing flat rocks cover the ground with flowers. (12)

verses.text:
पतितैः पतमानैश्च पादपस्थैश्च मारुतः।
कुसुमैः पश्य सौमित्रे क्रीडतीव समन्ततः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “See how the breeze is sporting as it were on all sides with the flowers that have fallen, are falling and are still on the trees, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (13)

verses.text:
विक्षिपन् विविधाः शाखां नगानां कुसुमोत्कटाः।
मारुतश्चलितस्थानैः षट्पदैरनुगीयते॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Violently shaking the various branches, richly endowed with blossom of trees, the breeze is being celebrated in song by black bees which have shifted from their position (on the flowers, dislodged as they were by the breeze). (14)

verses.text:
मत्तकोकिलसंनादैर्नर्तयन्निव पादपान्।
शैलकंदरनिष्क्रान्तः प्रगीत इव चानिलः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Emerging from mountain-caves and as though making the trees dance by the dulcet notes of cuckoos in heat, the breeze has started singing, as it were. (15)

verses.text:
तेन विक्षिपतात्यर्थं पवनेन समन्ततः।
अमी संसक्तशाखाग्रा ग्रथिता इव पादपाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “With the tips of their branches united on all sides by the aforesaid breeze, which was violently shaking them, those trees appear as though strung together. (16)

verses.text:
स एव सुखसंस्पर्शो वाति चन्दनशीतलः।
गन्धमभ्यवहन् पुण्यं श्रमापनयनोऽनिलः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Delightful to the touch and rendered cool by the touch of sandalwood and hence relieving fatigue, and wafting its pleasing fragrance, the aforesaid breeze moves along. (17)

verses.text:
अमी पवनविक्षिप्ता विनदन्तीव पादपाः।
षट्पदैरनुकूजद्भिर्वनेषु मधुगन्धिषु॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Violently shaken by the blast, those trees in the groves, fragrant with honey, are singing as it were through the black bees continuously humming. (18)

verses.text:
गिरिप्रस्थेषु रम्येषु पुष्पवद्भिर्मनोरमैः।
संसक्तशिखराः शैला विराजन्ति महाद्रुमैः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The mountains look exceptionally charming with their peaks joined together by large trees laden with blossom and hence pleasing to the mind, standing on their lovely plateaus. (19)

verses.text:
पुष्पसंछन्नशिखरा मारुतोत्क्षेपचञ्चलाः।
अमी मधुकरोत्तंसाः प्रगीता इव पादपाः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “With their tops thickly covered with blossom, the yonder trees, unsteady due to the shaking given by the wind and crested with black bees, are singing, as it were. (20)

verses.text:
सुपुष्पितांस्तु पश्यैतान् कर्णिकारान् समन्ततः।
हाटकप्रतिसंछन्नान् नरान् पीताम्बरानिव॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Behold these Karṇikāra trees laden with flowers on all sides and looking like men heavily adorned with gold ornaments and clad in yellow. (21)

verses.text:
अयं वसन्तः सौमित्रे नानाविहगनादितः।
सीतया विप्रहीणस्य शोकसंदीपनो मम॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Made noisy by birds of different species, this vernal season, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), fully awakens my grief, disunited as I am once for all from Sītā. (22)

verses.text:
मां हि शोकसमाक्रान्तं संतापयति मन्मथः।
हृष्टं प्रवदमानश्च समाह्वयति कोकिलः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Indeed love torments me, overwhelmed as I am with grief; and engaging in a quarrel (with me), the cuckoo merrily challenges me. (23)

verses.text:
एष दात्यूहको हृष्टो रम्ये मां वननिर्झरे।
प्रणदन्मन्मथाविष्टं शोचयिष्यति लक्ष्मण॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Joyously cackling near the wild lovely cascade, O Lakṣmaṇa, this water-fowl fills me with grief, possessed as I am with love, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (24)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वैतस्य पुरा शब्दमाश्रमस्था मम प्रिया।
मामाहूय प्रमुदिताः परमं प्रत्यनन्दत॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Overjoyed to hear its cry in the past, and calling me, my darling Sītā, when present in the hermitage, hailed me with excessive joy. (25)

verses.text:
एवं विचित्राः पतगा नानारावविराविणः।
वृक्षगुल्मलताः पश्य सम्पतन्ति समन्ततः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “See how, uttering notes of various kinds, birds of every description descend on trees, bushes and climbers on all sides. (26)

verses.text:
विमिश्रा विहगाः पुंभिरात्मव्यूहाभिनन्दिताः।
भृङ्गराजप्रमुदिताः सौमित्रे मधुरस्वराः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “When united with male birds, female birds, feeling rejoiced in the midst of their own kind, and female bees too are uttering sweet notes, overjoyed as they are at the sight of drones, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (27)

verses.text:
अस्याः कूले प्रमुदिताः सङ्घशः शकुनास्त्विह।
दात्यूहरतिविक्रन्दैः पुंस्कोकिलरुतैरपि॥ २८॥
स्वनन्ति पादपाश्चेमे ममानङ्गप्रदीपकाः।
अशोकस्तबकाङ्गारः षट्पदस्वननिःस्वनः॥ २९॥
मां हि पल्लवताम्रार्चिर्वसन्ताग्निः प्रधक्ष्यति।
नहि तां सूक्ष्मपक्ष्माक्षीं सुकेशीं मृदुभाषिणीम्॥ ३०॥
अपश्यतो मे सौमित्रे जीवितेऽस्ति प्रयोजनम्।
अयं हि रुचिरस्तस्याः कालो रुचिरकाननः॥ ३१॥
कोकिलाकुलसीमान्तो दयिताया ममानघ।
मन्मथायाससम्भूतो वसन्तगुणवर्धितः॥ ३२॥
अयं मां धक्ष्यति क्षिप्रं शोकाग्निर्नचिरादिव।
अपश्यतस्तां वनितां पश्यतो रुचिरान् द्रुमान्॥ ३३॥
ममायमात्मप्रभवो भूयस्त्वमुपयास्यति।
अदृश्यमाना वैदेही शोकं वर्धयतीह मे॥ ३४॥
दृश्यमानो वसन्तश्च स्वेदसंसर्गदूषकः।
मां हि सा मृगशावाक्षी चिन्ताशोकबलात्कृतम्॥ ३५॥
संतापयति सौमित्रे क्रूरश्चैत्रवनानिलः।
अमी मयूराः शोभन्ते प्रनृत्यन्तस्ततस्ततः॥ ३६॥
स्वैः पक्षैः पवनोद्धूतैर्गवाक्षैः स्फाटिकैरिव।
शिखिनीभिः परिवृतास्त एते मदमूर्च्छिताः॥ ३७॥
मन्मथाभिपरीतस्य मम मन्मथवर्धनाः।
पश्य लक्ष्मण नृत्यन्तं मयूरमुपनृत्यति॥ ३८॥
शिखिनी मन्मथार्तैषा भर्तारं गिरिसानुनि।
तामेव मनसा रामां मयूरोऽप्यनुधावति॥ ३९॥
वितत्य रुचिरौ पक्षौ रुतैरुपहसन्निव।
मयूरस्य वने नूनं रक्षसा न हृता प्रिया॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Living in flocks, birds for their part feel highly rejoiced on this strand of Pampā. Nay, through the notes of the water-fowls uttered during their amorous sports as well as through the shrill notes of male cuckoos these trees themselves sing, fully kindling (the fire of) love in me. Fire in the shape of the vernal season, which has bunches of crimson flowers of Aśoka trees for its live embers, the humming of bees for its crackle and the fresh leaves for its coppery tongues will undoubtedly consume me. Surely there is no purpose in my surviving, O Lakṣmaṇa, unable as I am to see that lady, Sītā, with lovely locks, eyes having fine eye-lashes and gentle speech. Surely the present season, in which woodlands look charming and their boundaries are thronged with cuckoos, was delightful to that darling of mine, O sinless one! This fire of grief, which has its source in the pangs of love and has been augmented by the charms of Spring will forthwith consume me without delay, as it were. This longing of my heart to meet her will reach its climax even as I am unable to perceive that beloved one and look on the charming trees. Being out of sight, Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, intensifies my grief in this forest, and so does Spring, which is discernible at present and shuts out all contact with sweat due to cool and delightful breezes. That fawn-eyed lady, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), unquestionably torments me, overpowered as I already am by worry and grief, and so does the cruel breeze from the woods characteristic of the month of Caitra. Dancing here and there with their wings, resembling crystal windows, shaken by the wind, the yonder peacocks spread their charm. Surrounded by peahens and intoxicated with joy, these peacocks intensify my longing to meet Sītā, overwhelmed as I already am with love. Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa, how this love-lorn peahen is dancing by the side of her mate, the dancing peacock, on the top of the hill. Spreading his charming wings and mocking me, as it were, by his cries, the peacock too is mentally following the aforesaid beloved one. Surely the beloved of the peacock has not been stolen away by a demon in the forest. (28—40)

verses.text:
तस्मान्नृत्यति रम्येषु वनेषु सह कान्तया।
मम त्वयं विना वासः पुष्पमासे सुदुःसहः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Hence it is that he is dancing with his beloved peahen in the delightful groves. For me, however, it is most unbearable to live in desolation in this vernal month of abundant flowers. (41)

verses.text:
पश्य लक्ष्मण संरागस्तिर्यग्योनिगतेष्वपि।
यदेषा शिखिनी कामाद् भर्तारमभिवर्तते॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “See, O Lakṣmaṇa, how intense love is found even among those belonging to the sub-human creation, as is clear from the fact that this peahen approaches her mate through love. (42)

verses.text:
ममाप्येवं विशालाक्षी जानकी जातसम्भ्रमा।
मदनेनाभिवर्तेत यदि नापहृता भवेत्॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “The large-eyed Sītā (daughter of Janaka) too would approach me through love in a flurry, had she not been borne away by the demon. (43)

verses.text:
पश्य लक्ष्मण पुष्पाणि निष्फलानि भवन्ति मे।
पुष्पभारसमृद्धानां वनानां शिशिरात्यये॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “See, O Lakṣmaṇa, how the blossoms of the forests, rich in their load of flowers, are proving of no use to me in the absence of Sītā, at the close of winter. (44)

verses.text:
रुचिराण्यपि पुष्पाणि पादपानामतिश्रिया।
निष्फलानि महीं यान्ति समं मधुकरोत्करैः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “The blossom of the trees, though lovely due to their surpassing charm, fall to the ground alongwith the swarms of black bees, being of no use to me. (45)

verses.text:
नदन्ति कामं शकुना मुदिताः सङ्घशः कलम्।
आह्वयन्त इवान्योन्यं कामोन्मादकरा मम॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “Full of joy the birds carol at will in flocks, calling to one another, as it were, and intoxicating me with love. (46)

verses.text:
वसन्तो यदि तत्रापि यत्र मे वसति प्रिया।
नूनं परवशा सीता सापि शोचत्यहं यथा॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “If spring has set in even in that region where my darling, Sītā is living, fallen as she is under the sway of others, undoubtedly she too is pining as I do. (47)

verses.text:
नूनं न तु वसन्तस्तं देशं स्पृशति यत्र सा।
कथं ह्यसितपद्माक्षी वर्तयेत् सा मया विना॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Surely Spring will never touch the fringe of that region where Sītā dwells. Even then how can that lady with dark lotus-like eyes survive without me? (48)

verses.text:
अथवा वर्तते तत्र वसन्तो यत्र मे प्रिया।
किं करिष्यति सुश्रोणी सा तु निर्भर्त्सिता परैः॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Or, Spring does prevail where my darling dwells. But, scolded, as she is, by enemies, what will that fair-limbed lady do?(49)

verses.text:
श्यामा पद्मपलाशाक्षी मृदुभाषा च मे प्रिया।
नूनं वसन्तमासाद्य परित्यक्ष्यति जीवितम्॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “Surely on crossing the threshold of Spring my juvenescent darling, who has eyes resembling lotus petals and is gentle of speech, will forthwith give up the ghost. (50)

verses.text:
दृढं हि हृदये बुद्धिर्मम सम्परिवर्तते।
नालं वर्तयितुं सीता साध्वी मद्विरहं गता॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “The thought steadily revolves in my heart that, having fallen a prey to separation from me, the virtuous Sītā is unable to survive. (51)

verses.text:
मयि भावो हि वैदेह्यास्तत्त्वतो विनिवेशितः।
ममापि भावः सीतायां सर्वथा विनिवेशितः॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “The affection of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) is undoubtedly and truly riveted on me and my affection too is riveted wholly on Sītā. (52)

verses.text:
एष पुष्पवहो वायुः सुखस्पर्शो हिमावहः।
तां विचिन्तयतः कान्तां पावकप्रतिमो मम॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “This breeze carrying the fragrance of flowers, which is delightful to the touch and brings coolness to the body, is like fire to me even as I think deeply of my darling. (53)

verses.text:
सदा सुखमहं मन्ये यं पुरा सह सीतया।
मारुतः स विना सीतां शोकसंजननो मम॥ ५४॥
verses.m: “The selfsame breeze which I considered as ever agreeable at one time in the company of Sītā is causing grief to me, bereft, as I am, of Sītā. (54)

verses.text:
तां विनाथ विहङ्गोऽसौ पक्षी प्रणदितस्तदा।
वायसः पादपगतः प्रहृष्टमभिकूजति॥ ५५॥
verses.m: “In the past the yonder bird (which is a crow) emitted a hoarse cry while flying through the air (thereby foreboding the abduction of Sītā). Now, in the absence of Sītā, the crow is crying most delightfully while remaining perched on the tree (thereby predicting her return). (55)

verses.text:
एष वै तत्र वैदेह्या विहगः प्रतिहारकः।
पक्षी मां तु विशालाक्ष्याः समीपमुपनेष्यति॥ ५६॥
verses.m: “While this bird, viz.,a crow, proved at that time (viz., during the presence of Sītā) instrumental (by foreboding evil) in bringing about the abduction of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), the bird will this time lead me to the presence of Sītā, a lady with large eyes. (56)

verses.text:
पश्य लक्ष्मण संनादं वने मदविवर्धनम्।
पुष्पिताग्रेषु वृक्षेषु द्विजानामवकूजताम्॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “Know the chorus in the forest of the birds warbling on the trees crested with flowers to be instrumental in heightening my joy beyond measure, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (57)

verses.text:
विक्षिप्तां पवनेनैतामसौ तिलकमञ्जरीम्।
षट्पदः सहसाभ्येति मदोद्धूतामिव प्रियाम्॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “The yonder bee suddenly approaches this flower-stalk of a Tilaka tree, shaken by the wind, even as a lover would approach his loved one thrilled with joy. (58)

verses.text:
कामिनामयमत्यन्तमशोकः शोकवर्धनः।
स्तबकैः पवनोत्क्षिप्तैस्तर्जयन्निव मां स्थितः॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “Accentuating beyond measure the grief of lovers, this Aśoka tree (which is supposed to rid those who approach it of their grief) stands threatening me, as it were, through its plumes of flowers shaken by the wind. (59)

verses.text:
अमी लक्ष्मण दृश्यन्ते चूताः कुसुमशालिनः।
विभ्रमोत्सिक्तमनसः साङ्गरागा नरा इव॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “Adorned with blossom, the yonder mango trees, O Lakṣmaṇa, look like human beings anointed with cosmetics, their mind distracted through love. (60)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पायाश्चित्रासु वनराजिषु।
किंनरा नरशार्दूल विचरन्ति यतस्ततः॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “See, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), how Kinnaras (a species of demigods) range hither and thither through the picturesque rows of forest trees standing on the brink of Pampā, O tiger among men ! (61)

verses.text:
इमानि शुभगन्धीनि पश्य लक्ष्मण सर्वशः।
नलिनानि प्रकाशन्ते जले तरुणसूर्यवत्॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa, how these fragrant red lotuses shine on all sides on the water like the rising sun reflected in every ripple of the Pampā. (62)

verses.text:
एषा प्रसन्नसलिला पद्मनीलोत्पलायुता।
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णा पम्पा सौगन्धिकायुता॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “Here is Pampā distinguished by its placid water, nay covered all over with lotuses and blue water-lilies, thronged with swans and water-fowl and overspread with Saugandhika flowers (a species of Kalhāra). (63)

verses.text:
जले तरुणसूर्याभैः षट्पदाहतकेसरैः।
पङ्कजैः शोभते पम्पा समन्तादभिसंवृता॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “Covered on all sides with lotuses shining like the rising sun reflected in water, their pollen having been scattered by black bees, Pampā spreads its charm. (64)

verses.text:
चक्रवाकयुता नित्यं चित्रप्रस्थवनान्तरा।
मातङ्गमृगयूथैश्च शोभते सलिलार्थिभिः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: “Inhabited by Cakravākas (ruddy geese) all the year, the woodlands about it consisting of wonderful glades, the lake looks charming with herds of elephants and deer seeking its water. (65)

verses.text:
पवनाहतवेगाभिरूर्मिभिर्विमलेऽम्भसि।
पङ्कजानि विराजन्ते ताड्यमानानि लक्ष्मण॥ ६६॥
verses.m: “Being lashed, O Lakṣmaṇa, by the waves which have gained velocity through the impact of winds, the lotuses shine brightly on the limpid water of the lake. (66)

verses.text:
पद्मपत्रविशालाक्षीं सततं प्रियपङ्कजाम्।
अपश्यतो मे वैदेहीं जीवितं नाभिरोचते॥ ६७॥
verses.m: “Life no longer attracts me, unable as I am to see Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), who has eyes large as lotus petals and who is ever fond of lotuses. (67)

verses.text:
अहो कामस्य वामत्वं यो गतामपि दुर्लभाम्।
स्मारयिष्यति कल्याणीं कल्याणतरवादिनीम्॥ ६८॥
verses.m: “Oh, the crookedness of Cupid, who puts me in mind of the blessed Sītā, who spoke highly agreeable words, nay, who has disappeared and is difficult to recover. (68)

verses.text:
शक्यो धारयितुं कामो भवेदभ्यागतो मया।
यदि भूयो वसन्तो मां न हन्यात् पुष्पितद्रुमः॥ ६९॥
verses.m: “The longing to meet her that has appeared in me may yet be restrained by me if Spring, marked by blossomed trees, were not to smite me in addition. (69)

verses.text:
यानि स्म रमणीयानि तया सह भवन्ति मे।
तान्येवारमणीयानि जायन्ते मे तया विना॥ ७०॥
verses.m: “Those very things which were delightful to me in her company have grown unattractive to me in her absence. (70)

verses.text:
पद्मकोशपलाशानि द्रष्टुं दृष्टिर्हि मन्यते।
सीताया नेत्रकोशाभ्यां सदृशानीति लक्ष्मण॥ ७१॥
verses.m: “My eyes love to see the petals of lotus cups in that they are akin to Sītā’s bud-like eyes, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (71)

verses.text:
पद्मकेसरसंसृष्टो वृक्षान्तरविनिःसृतः।
निःश्वास इव सीताया वाति वायुर्मनोहरः॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “The soul-ravishing breeze brought into contact with the filaments of lotuses and emerged through other trees blows like the breath of Sītā. (72)

verses.text:
सौमित्रे पश्य पम्पाया दक्षिणे गिरिसानुषु।
पुष्पितां कर्णिकारस्य यष्टिं परमशोभिताम्॥ ७३॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the trunk of the blossomed Karṇikāra tree invested with supreme charm on the mountain-peaks to the south of Pampā. (73)

verses.text:
अधिकं शैलराजोऽयं धातुभिस्तु विभूषितः।
विचित्रं सृजते रेणुं वायुवेगविघट्टितम्॥ ७४॥
verses.m: “Specially adorned in a large measure by minerals, this Ṛṣyamūka (a king of mountains) for its part is discharging a dust of various colours and odours wafted by force of winds. (74)

verses.text:
गिरिप्रस्थास्तु सौमित्रे सर्वतः सम्प्रपुष्पितैः।
निष्पत्रैः सर्वतो रम्यैः प्रदीप्ता इव किंशुकैः॥ ७५॥
verses.m: “With their lovely Kiṁśuka trees richly endowed with flowers and shorn of leaves, the peaks of this mountain for their part, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), appear ignited on all sides. (75)

verses.text:
पम्पातीररुहाश्चेमे संसिक्ता मधुगन्धिनः।
मालतीमल्लिकापद्मकरवीराश्च पुष्पिताः॥ ७६॥
verses.m: “Here are Mālatī, Mallikā, Padma and Karavīra trees in blossom, that have grown on the edge of the Pampā and have been nurtured by it and emit a sweet aroma. (76)

verses.text:
केतक्यः सिन्दुवाराश्च वासन्त्यश्च सुपुष्पिताः।
माधव्यो गन्धपूर्णाश्च कुन्दगुल्माश्च सर्वशः॥ ७७॥
verses.m: “There are Ketakī and Sinduvāra trees and climbers named Vāsantī in full blossom as also climbers named Mādhavī and jasmine shrubs, all full of fragrance on every side. (77)

verses.text:
चिरिबिल्वा मधूकाश्च वञ्जुला बकुलास्तथा।
चम्पकास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः॥ ७८॥
verses.m: “Nay, here are Ciribilva and Madhūka, Vañjula, Bakula, Campaka and Tilaka as well as Nāga trees, all in blossom. (78)

verses.text:
पद्मकाश्चैव शोभन्ते नीलाशोकाश्च पुष्पिताः।
लोध्राश्च गिरिपृष्ठेषु सिंहकेसरपिञ्जराः॥ ७९॥
verses.m: “On hill-tops Padmaka and blue Aśoka trees in blossom and also Lodhra trees, tawny as the manes of a lion, spread their charm. (79)

verses.text:
अङ्कोलाश्च कुरण्टाश्च चूर्णकाः पारिभद्रकाः।
चूताः पाटलयश्चापि कोविदाराश्च पुष्पिताः॥ ८०॥
मुचुकुन्दार्जुनाश्चैव दृश्यन्ते गिरिसानुषु।
केतकोद्दालकाश्चैव शिरीषाः शिंशपा धवाः॥ ८१॥
शाल्मल्यः किंशुकाश्चैव रक्ताः कुरवकास्तथा।
तिनिशा नक्तमालाश्च चन्दनाः स्यन्दनास्तथा॥ ८२॥
हिन्तालास्तिलकाश्चैव नागवृक्षाश्च पुष्पिताः।
पुष्पितान् पुष्पिताग्राभिर्लताभिः परिवेष्टितान्॥ ८३॥
द्रुमान् पश्येह सौमित्रे पम्पाया रुचिरान् बहून्।
वातविक्षिप्तविटपान् यथासन्नान् द्रुमानिमान्॥ ८४॥
लताः समनुवर्तन्ते मत्ता इव वरस्त्रियः।
पादपात् पादपं गच्छन् शैलाच्छैलं वनाद् वनम्॥ ८५॥
वाति नैकरसास्वादसम्मोदित इवानिलः।
केचित् पर्याप्तकुसुमाः पादपा मधुगन्धिनः॥ ८६॥
केचिन्मुकुलसंवीताः श्यामवर्णा इवाबभुः।
इदं मृष्टमिदं स्वादु प्रफुल्लमिदमित्यपि॥ ८७॥
रागरक्तो मधुकरः कुसुमेष्वेव लीयते।
निलीय पुनरुत्पत्य सहसान्यत्र गच्छति।
मधुलुब्धो मधुकरः पम्पातीरद्रुमेष्वसौ॥ ८८॥
verses.m: “Aṅkola, Kuraṇṭa, Cūrṇaka and Pāribhadraka trees, mango, Pāṭali and Kovidāra trees as also Mucukunda and Arjuna trees are seen in blossom on mountain-peaks. Here are Ketaka as also Uddālaka, Śirīṣa, Śiṁśapā, Dhava, Śālmalī and Kiṁśuka trees as well as red Kurabaka trees, Tiniśa and Naktamāla, sandalwood and Syandana, Hintāla and Tilaka as well as Nāga trees, all in blossom. Behold here, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), the numerous lovely trees in blossom entwined by climbers crested with blossom on the edge of the Pampā. Like pretty women drunk with love, the climbers embrace these trees, whose branches are tossed by the wind and which are bent so low as to appear quite at hand. Passing from tree to tree, from crag to crag and from wood to wood, the wind blows gently as though enraptured by enjoying diverse tastes from diverse flowers. Some trees are in full blossom and emit the fragrance of honey; while others are covered all over with buds and appear dark-brown of hue because of these buds. ‘How sweet is this ! How delicious is that ! How full-blown is that (the other) !’ Reflecting thus, the black bee steeped in love for the flowers remains buried in flowers alone. Remaining hidden (in flowers for some time) and then flying off, the black bee, covetous of honey, suddenly moves to other trees on the margin of the Pampā. (80—88)

verses.text:
इयं कुसुमसंघातैरुपस्तीर्णा सुखाकृता।
स्वयं निपतितैर्भूमिः शयनप्रस्तरैरिव॥ ८९॥
verses.m: “Strewn with heaps of flowers, fallen off themselves, this plot looks as if made smug by bedsheets. (89)

verses.text:
विविधा विविधैः पुष्पैस्तैरेव नगसानुषु।
विस्तीर्णाः पीतरक्ताभाः सौमित्रे प्रस्तराः कृताः॥ ९०॥
verses.m: “Extensive beds of a mixed yellow and red colour and of various sizes and designs have been made, as it were, with those flowers of different kinds on tops of the mountain, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā). (90)

verses.text:
हिमान्ते पश्य सौमित्रे वृक्षाणां पुष्पसम्भवम्।
पुष्पमासे हि तरवः संघर्षादिव पुष्पिताः॥ ९१॥
verses.m: “Behold the wealth of flowers on the trees at the close of winter, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) ! Indeed in the month of Caitra (a month of flowers) the trees stand clothed with blossom as if in a spirit of rivalry. (91)

verses.text:
आह्वयन्त इवान्योन्यं नगाः षट्पदनादिताः।
कुसुमोत्तंसविटपाः शोभन्ते बहु लक्ष्मण॥ ९२॥
verses.m: “Rendered noisy by the humming of bees and as such challenging one another as it were, and their boughs crowned with flowers, the trees, O Lakṣmaṇa, look very charming. (92)

verses.text:
एष कारण्डवः पक्षी विगाह्य सलिलं शुभम्।
रमते कान्तया सार्धं काममुद्दीपयन्निव॥ ९३॥
verses.m: “Diving into the limpid water this bird of the Kāraṇḍava species (a kind of water-fowl) is sporting with its beloved mate, thereby inspiring love as it were (in me, who have been torn away from my beloved). (93)

verses.text:
मन्दाकिन्यास्तु यदिदं रूपमेतन्मनोरमम्।
स्थाने जगति विख्याता गुणास्तस्या मनोरमाः॥ ९४॥
verses.m: “Since this beauty of Pampā, which looks like the Mandākinī, is so soul-ravishing, it is but proper that its soul-enchanting excellences are famed throughout the world. (94)

verses.text:
यदि दृश्येत सा साध्वी यदि चेह वसेमहि।
स्पृहयेयं न शक्राय नायोध्यायै रघूत्तम॥ ९५॥
verses.m: “If that pious lady comes to view and if we live in this forest, I shall not look with envy on Indra, the ruler of gods, nor long to be at Ayodhyā, O jewel among the Raghus ! (95)

verses.text:
न ह्येवं रमणीयेषु शाद्वलेषु तया सह।
रमतो मे भवेच्चिन्ता न स्पृहान्येषु वा भवेत्॥ ९६॥
verses.m: “If I sport with her on such lovely lawns, no worry will ever seize me, nor any craving for other pleasures. (96)

verses.text:
अमी हि विविधैः पुष्पैस्तरवो विविधच्छदाः।
काननेऽस्मिन् विना कान्तां चिन्तामुत्पादयन्ति मे॥ ९७॥
verses.m: “Clothed with leaves of various kinds and laden with flowers of every description, the yonder trees in this forest cause worry to Me, bereft as I am of Sītā. (97)

verses.text:
पश्य शीतजलां चेमां सौमित्रे पुष्करायुताम्।
चक्रवाकानुचरितां कारण्डवनिषेविताम्॥ ९८॥
प्लवैः क्रौञ्चैश्च सम्पूर्णां महामृगनिषेविताम्।
अधिकं शोभते पम्पा विकूजद्भिर्विहंगमैः॥ ९९॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), this lake full of cool water, covered all over with lotuses, frequented by Cakravākas (red geese), nay, inhabited by water-fowls, teeming with ducks and herons and visited by large deer. Pampā looks very charming with birds singing melodiously. (98-99)

verses.text:
दीपयन्तीव मे कामं विविधा मुदिता द्विजाः।
श्यामां चन्द्रमुखीं स्मृत्वा प्रियां पद्मनिभेक्षणाम्॥ १००॥
verses.m: “Putting me in mind of my youthful darling, whose countenance resembles the full moon and who has lotus-like eyes, the merry birds of different species intensely inflame my love, as it were. (100)

verses.text:
पश्य सानुषु चित्रेषु मृगीभिः सहितान् मृगान्।
मां पुनर्मृगशावाक्ष्या वैदेह्या विरहीकृतम्।
व्यथयन्तीव मे चित्तं संचरन्तस्ततस्ततः॥ १०१॥
verses.m: “Behold, on the one hand, the deer O Lakṣmaṇa, accompanied by female deer, on the picturesque peaks and on the other hand, myself, who stand disunited from the fawn-eyed Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory); moving freely here and there they afflict my mind, as it were. (101)

verses.text:
अस्मिन् सानुनि रम्ये हि मत्तद्विजगणाकुले।
पश्येयं यदि तां कान्तां ततः स्वस्ति भवेन्मम॥ १०२॥
verses.m: “Happiness will come to me then only if I am able to behold that beloved one on this delightful peak thronged with flocks of birds in heat. (102)

verses.text:
जीवेयं खलु सौमित्रे मया सह सुमध्यमा।
सेवेत यदि वैदेही पम्पायाः पवनं शुभम्॥ १०३॥
verses.m: “I should certainly survive, O Lakṣmaṇa, if Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) of charming limbs enjoys with me the pleasant breeze coming from the Pampā. (103)

verses.text:
पद्मसौगन्धिकवहं शिवं शोकविनाशनम्।
धन्या लक्ष्मण सेवन्ते पम्पाया वनमारुतम्॥ १०४॥
verses.m: “Only blessed souls drink, O Lakṣmaṇa, the delightful breeze from the woodlands surrounding Pampā, carrying as it does the fragrance of lotuses and Saugandhika flowers (the white water-lilies) and uprooting all grief. (104)

verses.text:
श्यामा पद्मपलाशाक्षी प्रिया विरहिता मया।
कथं धारयति प्राणान् विवशा जनकात्मजा॥ १०५॥
verses.m: “How, I wonder, does the beloved and youthful Sītā (Janaka’s daughter), who has eyes resembling lotus petals, preserve her life, disunited as she is from me and helpless as such? (105)

verses.text:
किं नु वक्ष्यामि धर्मज्ञं राजानं सत्यवादिनम्।
जनकं पृष्टसीतं तं कुशलं जनसंसदि॥ १०६॥
verses.m: “How, I wonder, shall I tell the celebrated King Janaka, who knows what is right and always speaks the truth, when he asks me about Sītā in an assemblage of men, that all is well with her? (106)

verses.text:
या मामनुगता मन्दं पित्रा प्रस्थापितं वनम्।
सीता धर्मं समास्थाय क्व नु सा वर्तते प्रिया॥ १०७॥
verses.m: “Where on earth is that beloved Sītā, who, clinging fast as she did to the principles of virtue, followed me when I was exiled to the forest by my father, unlucky as I was? (107)

verses.text:
तया विहीनः कृपणः कथं लक्ष्मण धारये।
या मामनुगता राज्याद् भ्रष्टं विहतचेतसम्॥ १०८॥
verses.m: “How, O Lakṣmaṇa, shall I survive, miserable as I am because bereft of Sītā, who followed me even when I was deprived of my sovereignty and dispirited? (108)

verses.text:
तच्चार्वाञ्चितपद्माक्षं सुगन्धि शुभमव्रणम्।
अपश्यतो मुखं तस्याः सीदतीव मतिर्मम॥ १०९॥
verses.m: “My mind is indeed troubled as I fail to behold her comely and bright face with graceful lotus-like eyes, free from scars and emitting a sweet fragrance. (109)

verses.text:
स्मितहास्यान्तरयुतं गुणवन्मधुरं हितम्।
वैदेह्या वाक्यमतुलं कदा श्रोष्यामि लक्ष्मण॥ ११०॥
verses.m: When shall I hear, O Lakṣmaṇa, the incomparable speech of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), excellent, sweet and wholesome and interspersed with smiles and fun? (110)

verses.text:
प्राप्य दुःखं वने श्यामा मां मन्मथविकर्शितम्।
नष्टदुःखेव हृष्टेव साध्वी साध्वभ्यभाषत॥ १११॥
verses.m: “Even though undergoing suffering in the forest, the youthful and virtuous lady spoke lovingly to me, sore stricken as I was with love, as though she were happy and as though she had no suffering. (111)

verses.text:
किं नु वक्ष्याम्ययोध्यायां कौसल्यां हि नृपात्मज।
क्व सा स्नुषेति पृच्छन्तीं कथं चापि मनस्विनीम्॥ ११२॥
verses.m: “What on earth shall I actually tell the lofty-minded Kausalyā (my mother) when she puts the following question to me in Ayodhyā (on my return from exile): ‘Where and also how is that princess, my daughter-in-law?’ (112)

verses.text:
गच्छ लक्ष्मण पश्य त्वं भरतं भ्रातृवत्सलम्।
नह्यहं जीवितुं शक्तस्तामृते जनकात्मजाम्॥ ११३॥
verses.m: “Depart, O Lakṣmaṇa, and see you Bharata, who is so fond of his brothers; for I am no longer able to survive without the said daughter of Janaka.” (113)

verses.text:
इति रामं महात्मानं विलपन्तमनाथवत्।
उवाच लक्ष्मणो भ्राता वचनं युक्तमव्ययम्॥ ११४॥
verses.m: Brother Lakṣmaṇa made the following judicious and flawless reply to the high-souled Śrī Rāma, who was lamenting like a forlorn creature : (114)

verses.text:
संस्तम्भ राम भद्रं ते मा शुचः पुरुषोत्तम।
नेदृशानां मतिर्मन्दा भवत्यकलुषात्मनाम्॥ ११५॥
verses.m: “Have fortitude, O Rāma! May prosperity attend on you. Pray, do not grieve, O jewel among men ! The intellect of such people as you, whose mind is free from sin, never gets languid. (115)

verses.text:
स्मृत्वा वियोगजं दुःखं त्यज स्नेहं प्रिये जने।
अतिस्नेहपरिष्वङ्गाद् वर्तिरार्द्रापि दह्यते॥ ११६॥
verses.m: “Bearing in mind the grief born of desolation, give up your fondness for the beloved ones. Even a wet wick begins to burn through contact with excessive oil (the word used here to denote oil is ‘Sneha’, which also means love). (116)

verses.text:
यदि गच्छति पातालं ततोऽभ्यधिकमेव वा।
सर्वथा रावणस्तात न भविष्यति राघव॥ ११७॥
verses.m: “Rāvaṇa, O dear brother, will not survive at all even if he descends into Pātāla (the nethermost subterranean region) or a still darker region than that, O scion of Raghu. (117)

verses.text:
प्रवृत्तिर्लभ्यतां तावत् तस्य पापस्य रक्षसः।
ततो हास्यति वा सीतां निधनं वा गमिष्यति॥ ११८॥
verses.m: “Let the whereabouts of that sinful ogre be ascertained first. He will then either yield up Sītā or meet his end. (118)

verses.text:
यदि याति दितेर्गर्भं रावणं सह सीतया।
तत्राप्येनं हनिष्यामि न चेद् दास्यति मैथिलीम्॥ ११९॥
verses.m: “If Rāvaṇa enters with Sītā the womb of Diti (the mother of the demon race), I shall kill him even there in case he refuses to yield up Sītā (a princess of Mithilā). (119)

verses.text:
स्वास्थ्यं भद्रं भजस्वार्य त्यज्यतां कृपणा मतिः।
अर्थो हि नष्टकार्यार्थैरयत्नेनाधिगम्यते॥ १२०॥
verses.m: “Have recourse to blessed forbearance which is your normal state, O noble sir, and let the abject mentality of despondency be given up. For, the object of pursuit cannot be attained without exertion by those whose endeavour has been foiled and purpose thwarted. (120)

verses.text:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात् परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किंचिदपि दुर्लभम्॥ १२१॥
verses.m: “Strenuous effort alone is powerful, O worthy Sir ! There is no might greater than exertion. Indeed nothing whatsoever is difficult to attain in all the worlds for a man given to endeavour. (121)

verses.text:
उत्साहवन्तः पुरुषा नावसीदन्ति कर्मसु।
उत्साहमात्रमाश्रित्य प्रतिलप्स्याम जानकीम्॥ १२२॥
verses.m: “Men of endeavour do not get disheartened when faced with hardest duties. Falling back upon bare exertion we shall be able to recover Sītā (Janaka’s daughter). (122)

verses.text:
त्यजतां कामवृत्तत्वं शोकं संन्यस्य पृष्ठतः।
महात्मानं कृतात्मानमात्मानं नावबुध्यसे॥ १२३॥
verses.m: “Casting grief to the background, abandon the behaviour of one dominated by concupiscence. It is a pity you no longer recognize yourself to be an exalted soul who has disciplined his mind.” (123)

verses.text:
एवं सम्बोधितस्तेन शोकोपहतचेतनः।
त्यज्य शोकं च मोहं च रामो धैर्यमुपागमत्॥ १२४॥
verses.m: Shaking off grief and infatuation too, when admonished thus by Lakṣmaṇa, Śrī Rāma, whose understanding had been clouded by grief, regained his firmness. (124)

verses.text:
सोऽभ्यतिक्रामदव्यग्रस्तामचिन्त्यपराक्रमः।
रामः पम्पां सुरुचिरां रम्यां पारिप्लवद्रुमाम्॥ १२५॥
verses.m: The celebrated Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of inconceivable prowess and was now unruffled, passed clearly beyond the aforesaid Pampā, which was exceedingly charming and delightful and was hemmed on all sides with waving trees. (125)

verses.text:
निरीक्षमाणः सहसा महात्मा
सर्वं वनं निर्झरकन्दरं च।
उद्विग्नचेताः सह लक्ष्मणेन
विचार्य दुःखोपहतः प्रतस्थे॥ १२६॥
verses.m: Having deliberated with Lakṣmaṇa and surveying the entire forest as well as the cascades and caves comprised in it, the exalted soul, who was feeling perturbed in mind and was overwhelmed with sorrow, precipitately sallied forth in quest of Sītā. (126)

verses.text:
तं मत्तमातङ्गविलासगामी
गच्छन्तमव्यग्रमना महात्मा।
स लक्ष्मणो राघवमिष्टचेष्टो
ररक्ष धर्मेण बलेन चैव॥ १२७॥
verses.m: Walking with the sportful gait of an elephant in rut, the celebrated and high-souled Lakṣmaṇa, whose mind was unruffled and whose movements were agreeable to his eldest brother, protected Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), who was walking ahead, by showing him his duty and describing his own might too. (127)

verses.text:
तावृष्यमूकस्य समीपचारी
चरन् ददर्शाद्भुतदर्शनीयौ।
शाखामृगाणामधिपस्तरस्वी
वितत्रसे नैव विचेष्ट चेष्टाम्॥ १२८॥
verses.m: Moving about on the verge of Pampā, one day, the mighty Sugrīva (the overlord of monkeys), who used to ramble in the vicinity of Mount Ṛṣyamūka, espied the two princes, who were marvellously good-looking, and got so much frightened that he did not even move to take his food (which was coveted by him). (128)

verses.text:
स तौ महात्मा गजमन्दगामी
शाखामृगस्तत्र चरंश्चरन्तौ।
दृष्ट्वा विषादं परमं जगाम
चिन्तापरीतो भयभारभग्नः॥ १२९॥
verses.m: Overwhelmed with anxiety and weighed down with a load of fear to see while rambling the two princes moving about in that area, that high-souled monkey, who walked with the slow gait of an elephant, fell a victim to supreme despondency. (129)

verses.text:
तमाश्रमं पुण्यसुखं शरण्यं
सदैव शाखामृगसेवितान्तम्।
त्रस्ताश्च दृष्ट्वा हरयोऽभिजग्मु-
र्महौजसौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ तौ॥ १३०॥
verses.m: Frightened to see the aforesaid Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) and Lakṣmaṇa, who were possessed of great bodily strength, and whom they suspected to be allies of Vālī, the other monkeys too, who had cast their lot with Sugrīva and lived with him, retired for safety to the hermitage, referred to above, (of Sage Mataṅga, which had been rendered a forbidden land for Vālī due to an imprecation uttered by the sage) and hence was capable of affording protection to them, nay, which was sacred and pleasant and whose interior was permanently inhabited by monkeys. (130)

verses.text:
तौ तु दृष्ट्वा महात्मानौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
वरायुधधरौ वीरौ सुग्रीवः शङ्कितोऽभवत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Sugrīva was seized with apprehension to see the two aforesaid gallant brothers, the high-souled Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who for their part carried excellent weapons on their person. (1)

verses.text:
उद्विग्नहृदयः सर्वा दिशः समवलोकयन्।
न व्यतिष्ठत कस्मिंश्चिद् देशे वानरपुंगवः॥ २॥
verses.m: Glancing round on all sides, perturbed at heart as he was, Sugrīva (the foremost of monkeys) could not find rest at any one place. (2)

verses.text:
नैव चक्रे मनः स्थातुं वीक्षमाणौ महाबलौ।
कपेः परमभीतस्य चित्तं व्यवससाद ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Perceiving the two princes of extraordinary might, Sugrīva did not feel inclined to stay at his own place. The mind of the monkey who was extremely frightened, gave way to despondency: so the tradition goes. (3)

verses.text:
चिन्तयित्वा स धर्मात्मा विमृश्य गुरुलाघवम्।
सुग्रीवः परमोद्विग्नः सर्वैस्तैर्वानरैः सह॥ ४॥
verses.m: Pondering himself and considering with his ministers the superiority of the enemy’s strength and his own weakness, the celebrated Sugrīva, whose mind was set on virtue, felt extremely perturbed with all the aforesaid monkeys. (4)

verses.text:
ततः स सचिवेभ्यस्तु सुग्रीवः प्लवगाधिपः।
शशंस परमोद्विग्नः पश्यंस्तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ ५॥
verses.m: Beholding the said Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the celebrated Sugrīva, the overlord of monkeys, for his part, who was extremely sad, thereupon pointed out the two princes to his ministers in the following words : (5)

verses.text:
एतौ वनमिदं दुर्गं वालिप्रणिहितौ ध्रुवम्।
छद्मना चीरवसनौ प्रचरन्ताविहागतौ॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Undoubtedly sent by Vālī (my elder brother), these two princes, who are clad in the bark of trees by way of disguise, have come roaming about to this forest here, which is difficult of access.” (6)

verses.text:
ततः सुग्रीवसचिवा दृष्ट्वा परमधन्विनौ।
जग्मुर्गिरितटात् तस्मादन्यच्छिखरमुत्तमम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Seeing the two great bowmen, the counsellors of Sugrīva moved from that mountain-side to another excellent peak. (7)

verses.text:
ते क्षिप्रमभिगम्याथ यूथपा यूथपर्षभम्।
हरयो वानरश्रेष्ठं परिवार्योपतस्थिरे॥ ८॥
verses.m: Reaching the peak in no time, the monkeys, who were all leaders of troops, stood surrounding Sugrīva (the foremost of monkeys), the leader of those leaders. (8)

verses.text:
एवमेकायनगताः प्लवमाना गिरेर्गिरिम्।
प्रकम्पयन्तो वेगेन गिरीणां शिखराणि च॥ ९॥
verses.m: Leaping from crag to crag, and violently shaking the hill-tops with their vehemence, the monkeys thus reached a common track. (9)

verses.text:
ततः शाखामृगाः सर्वे प्लवमाना महाबलाः।
बभञ्जुश्च नगांस्तत्र पुष्पितान् दुर्गमाश्रितान्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Nay, while leaping (from crag to crag), the monkeys, who were all possessed of extraordinary might, thereupon broke down the trees in blossom standing on the hill at that time. (10)

verses.text:
आप्लवन्तो हरिवराः सर्वतस्तं महागिरिम्।
मृगमार्जारशार्दूलांस्त्रासयन्तो ययुस्तदा॥ ११॥
verses.m: Jumping on that great mountain from all sides and scaring the deer, wild cats and leopards (living on that hill), the foremost of monkeys then moved on. (11)

verses.text:
ततः सुग्रीवसचिवाः पर्वतेन्द्रे समाहिताः।
संगम्य कपिमुख्येन सर्वे प्राञ्जलयः स्थिताः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Coming together with Sugrīva (the chief of monkeys), all the ministers of Sugrīva then stood attentive on the Ṛṣyamūka hill (the lord of mountains) with joined palms. (12)

verses.text:
ततस्तु भयसंत्रस्तं वालिकिल्बिषशङ्कितम्।
उवाच हनुमान् वाक्यं सुग्रीवं वाक्यकोविदः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Thereupon Hanumān, for his part, who was an adept in expression, spoke as follows to Sugrīva, who was distracted through fear and was apprehensive of some mischief on the part of Vālī: (13)

verses.text:
सम्भ्रमस्त्यज्यतामेष सर्वैर्वालिकृते महान्।
मलयोऽयं गिरिवरो भयं नेहास्ति वालिनः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Let this great flurry on account of Vālī be given up by all. This jewel among mountains is no other than Malaya (otherwise known as Ṛṣyamūka); there is no fear here from Vālī. (14)

verses.text:
यस्मादुद्विग्नचेतास्त्वं विद्रुतो हरिपुङ्गव।
तं क्रूरदर्शनं क्रूरं नेह पश्यामि वालिनम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I do not see here that cruel Vālī of ferocious aspect, because of whom you have run away, perturbed in mind, O bull among monkeys ! (15)

verses.text:
यस्मात् तव भयं सौम्य पूर्वजात् पापकर्मणः।
स नेह वाली दुष्टात्मा न ते पश्याम्यहं भयम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “That Vālī of wicked mind, your elder brother of sinful deeds, from whom there is danger to you, O gentle one, is not here. I, therefore, see no cause of fear to you. (16)

verses.text:
अहो शाखामृगत्वं ते व्यक्तमेव प्लवङ्गम।
लघुचित्ततयाऽऽत्मानं न स्थापयसि यो मतौ॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Oh, too evident is the ape in you, O bull among monkeys, who due to light-mindedness, are not able to keep yourself fixed on a particular conclusion. (17)

verses.text:
बुद्धिविज्ञानसम्पन्न इङ्गितैः सर्वमाचर।
नह्यबुदिं्ध गतो राजा सर्वभूतानि शास्ति हि॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Reading the mind of others through their gestures, richly endowed as you are with intelligence and wisdom, do everything needful in the proper way. Surely a king who has taken recourse to thoughtlessness cannot effectively rule over all his subjects.” (18)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवस्तु शुभं वाक्यं श्रुत्वा सर्वं हनूमतः।
ततः शुभतरं वाक्यं हनूमन्तमुवाच ह॥ १९॥
verses.m: Hearing the brilliant speech of Hanumān in its entirety, Sugrīva for his part addressed to Hanumān the following observation, which was more brilliant than the former (that of Hanumān) : (19)

verses.text:
दीर्घबाहू विशालाक्षौ शरचापासिधारिणौ।
कस्य न स्याद् भयं दृष्ट्वा ह्येतौ सुरसुतोपमौ॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Who will not be actually seized with fear to see these two warriors possessed of unusually long arms and large eyes, nay, carrying a bow, sword and arrow on their person and looking like the offspring of gods? (20)

verses.text:
वालिप्रणिहितावेव शङ्केऽहं पुरुषोत्तमौ।
राजानो बहुमित्राश्च विश्वासो नात्र हि क्षमः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “I suspect these two jewels among men to have been sent by Vālī alone; for kings have many friends and no reliance should be placed in them. (21)

verses.text:
अरयश्च मनुष्येण विज्ञेयाश्छद्मचारिणः।
विश्वस्तानामविश्वस्ताश्छिद्रेषु प्रहरन्त्यपि॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Enemies moving in disguise ought to be recognized by a clever man. For remaining distrustful themselves, they instil, trust in their enemies and then go the length of assailing the vulnerable points of their trustful adversaries. (22)

verses.text:
कृत्येषु वाली मेधावी राजानो बहुदर्शिनः।
भवन्ति परहन्तारस्ते ज्ञेयाः प्राकृतैर्नरैः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Vālī is shrewd in his state affairs; nay, kings are well-versed in many expedients and destroy their enemies. They should be known (in their true colours) with the help of spies clad as ordinary men. (23)

verses.text:
तौ त्वया प्राकृतेनेव गत्वा ज्ञेयौ प्लवंगम।
इङ्गितानां प्रकारैश्च रूपव्याभाषणेन च॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Making a move to them like one unconcerned, the aforesaid two strangers ought to be truly known by you, O monkey hero, through the nature of their gestures, as also through their facial expression and mutual talks. (24)

verses.text:
लक्षयस्व तयोर्भावं प्रहृष्टमनसौ यदि।
विश्वासयन् प्रशंसाभिरिङ्गितैश्च पुनः पुनः॥ २५॥
ममैवाभिमुखं स्थित्वा पृच्छ त्वं हरिपुङ्गव।
प्रयोजनं प्रवेशस्य वनस्यास्य धनुर्धरौ॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Find out their intentions and, inspiring confidence in them again and again by means of my praises and gestures (corroborating them), if they are highly rejoiced in mind, and standing with your face turned towards me, inquire of the two bowmen the purpose of their entry into this forest, O bull among monkeys ! (25-26)

verses.text:
शुद्धात्मानौ यदि त्वेतौ जानीहि त्वं प्लवङ्गम।
व्याभाषितैर्वा रूपैर्वा विज्ञेया दुष्टतानयोः॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Even if you conclude them to be honest of purpose, O monkey hero, their wickedness should be discovered by means of their talks as well as by their facial expression.” (27)

verses.text:
इत्येवं कपिराजेन संदिष्टो मारुतात्मजः।
चकार गमने बुदिं्ध यत्र तौ रामलक्ष्मणौ॥ २८॥
verses.m: Instructed thus by Sugrīva (a king of monkeys), Hanumān, son of wind-god, made up his mind to proceed to the spot where the aforesaid Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa were. (28)

verses.text:
तथेति सम्पूज्य वचस्तु तस्य
कपेः सुभीतस्य दुरासदस्य।
महानुभावो हनुमान् ययौ तदा
स यत्र रामोऽतिबली सलक्ष्मणः॥ २९॥
verses.m: Bowing with the words “So be it” to the command of Sugrīva, who felt dismayed, though otherwise difficult to approach, that high-souled monkey, Hanumān, then left for the place where Śrī Rāma, who was possessed of extraordinary might, was with Lakṣmaṇa. (29)

verses.text:
वचो विज्ञाय हनुमान् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
पर्वतादृष्यमूकात् तु पुप्लुवे यत्र राघवौ॥ १॥
verses.m: Receiving respectfully the bidding of the high-souled Sugrīva, Hanumān for his part jumped from (the top of) the Ṛṣyamūka hill to the spot where stood Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two scions of Raghu. (1)

verses.text:
कपिरूपं परित्यज्य हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः।
भिक्षुरूपं ततो भेजे शठबुद्धितया कपिः॥ २॥
verses.m: Concealing the form of a monkey, because of his having a suspicious mind, a monkey as he was, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, thereupon assumed the form of a mendicant (recluse). (2)

verses.text:
ततश्च हनुमान् वाचा श्लक्ष्णया सुमनोज्ञया।
विनीतवदुपागम्य राघवौ प्रणिपत्य च॥ ३॥
आबभाषे च तौ वीरौ यथावत् प्रशशंस च।
सम्पूज्य विधिवद् वीरौ हनुमान् वानरोत्तमः॥ ४॥
उवाच कामतो वाक्यं मृदु सत्यपराक्रमौ।
राजर्षिदेवप्रतिमौ तापसौ संशितव्रतौ॥ ५॥
देशं कथमिमं प्राप्तौ भवन्तौ वरवर्णिनौ।
त्रासयन्तौ मृगगणानन्यांश्च वनचारिणः॥ ६॥
पम्पातीररुहान् वृक्षान् वीक्षमाणौ समन्ततः।
इमां नदीं शुभजलां शोभयन्तौ तरस्विनौ॥ ७॥
verses.m: Approaching the two scions of Raghu like a humble man and falling prostrate before them, Hanumān then accosted the aforesaid two heroes in a soft and most pleasing language and duly extolled them. Offering due homage to the two heroes according to the scriptural ordinance, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, addressed the following gentle words to them according to the desire of Sugrīva: “How have you two ascetics of remarkable vigour, unfailing prowess, most austere vows and excellent appearance and resembling a couple of royal sages or gods, come to this region, causing fright to the herds of deer and other denizens of the forest, nay, surveying the trees growing on all sides on the brink of Pampā and lending charm as you do to this lake of sparkling water? (3—7)

verses.text:
धैर्यवन्तौ सुवर्णाभौ कौ युवां चीरवाससौ।
निःश्वसन्तौ वरभुजौ पीडयन्ताविमाः प्रजाः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Who are you of charming arms and remarkable fortitude, clad in the bark of trees and possessing a charming complexion and lustre, sighing and causing discomfort to these creatures by your very august presence? (8)

verses.text:
सिंहविप्रेक्षितौ वीरौ महाबलपराक्रमौ।
शक्रचापनिभे चापे गृहीत्वा शत्रुनाशनौ॥ ९॥
श्रीमन्तौ रूपसम्पन्नौ वृषभश्रेष्ठविक्रमौ।
हस्तिहस्तोपमभुजौ द्युतिमन्तौ नरर्षभौ॥ १०॥
प्रभया पर्वतेन्द्रोऽसौ युवयोरवभासितः।
राज्यार्हावमरप्रख्यौ कथं देशमिहागतौ॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Wielding a pair of bows shining brightly like rainbows, how have you, two heroic jewels among men, visited this region—you, who are endowed with the gaze of a lion and are possessed of extraordinary might and prowess, are capable of destroying the foes, are full of glory and splendour and rich in comeliness, who are distinguished by the noble gait of a bull and arms resembling the proboscis of an elephant, who are worthy of sovereignty and shine brightly like gods? The yonder Ṛṣyamūka (a king of mountains) stands illumined by your effulgence. (9—11)

verses.text:
पद्मपत्रेक्षणौ वीरौ जटामण्डलधारिणौ।
अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरौ देवलोकादिहागतौ॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Having eyes resembling the petals of a lotus and wearing a rounded mass of matted locks, you two gallant men match each other and are heroes come down to this earth from the celestial world. (12)

verses.text:
यदृच्छयेव सम्प्राप्तौ चन्द्रसूर्यौ वसुंधराम्।
विशालवक्षसौ वीरौ मानुषौ देवरूपिणौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Endowed with a broad chest, you two heroic men possess the exterior of gods. It appears as if the moon-god and the sun-god have duly reached the earth by the will of Providence. (13)

verses.text:
सिंहस्कन्धौ महोत्साहौ समदाविव गोवृषौ।
आयताश्च सुवृत्ताश्च बाहवः परिघोपमाः॥ १४॥
सर्वभूषणभूषार्हाः किमर्थं न विभूषिताः।
उभौ योग्यावहं मन्ये रक्षितुं पृथिवीमिमाम्॥ १५॥
ससागरवनां कृत्स्नां विन्ध्यमेरुविभूषिताम्।
इमे च धनुषी चित्रे श्लक्ष्णे चित्रानुलेपने॥ १६॥
प्रकाशेते यथेन्द्रस्य वज्रे हेमविभूषिते।
सम्पूर्णाश्च शितैर्बाणैस्तूणाश्च शुभदर्शनाः॥ १७॥
जीवितान्तकरैर्घोरैर्ज्वलद्भिरिव पन्नगैः।
महाप्रमाणौ विपुलौ तप्तहाटकभूषणौ॥ १८॥
खड्गावेतौ विराजेते निर्मुक्तभुजगाविव।
एवं मां परिभाषन्तं कस्माद् वै नाभिभाषतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Having shoulders resembling those of a lion and, possessed of extraordinary vigour, you look like a pair of bulls in heat. Wherefore have these arms of yours, long and perfectly round and resembling a pair of clubs, have not been artistically adorned, even though they deserve to be embellished with all kinds of jewels? I consider you both as fit to protect this entire earth with its oceans and forests and richly adorned with the Vindhya and Meru mountains. Nay, these wonderful, charming and strangely gilded bows of yours shine like Indra’s thunderbolts decorated with gold. Besides, filled to capacity with blazing sharp-pointed shafts, capable of ending one’s life and dreadful like serpents, these quivers of yours look so charming. These swords of considerable length and enormous size and decorated with refined gold, shine brightly like a pair of serpents that have shed their slough. But wherefore do you not answer me even though I am uttering your praises, as I have done? (14—19)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवो नाम धर्मात्मा कश्चिद् वानरपुङ्गवः।
वीरो विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा जगद्भ्रमति दुःखितः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “A gallant jewel among monkeys, Sugrīva by name, whose mind is set on virtue, roams the earth, afflicted as he is, having been banished by his elder brother. (20)

verses.text:
प्राप्तोऽहं प्रेषितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण महात्मना।
राज्ञा वानरमुख्यानां हनुमान् नाम वानरः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Sent by that high-minded Sugrīva, king of the leaders of monkeys, I, a monkey, Hanumān by name, have sought you. (21)

verses.text:
युवाभ्यां स हि धर्मात्मा सुग्रीवः सख्यमिच्छति।
तस्य मां सचिवं वित्तं वानरं पवनात्मजम्॥ २२॥
भिक्षुरूपप्रतिच्छन्नं सुग्रीवप्रियकारणात्।
ऋष्यमूकादिह प्राप्तं कामगं कामचारिणम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “The said pious-minded Sugrīva actually seeks your friendship. Know me to be his minister, a monkey sprung from the loins of the wind-god and arrived here from Ṛṣyamūka in order to serve the cause of Sugrīva and disguised in the form of a recluse, capable as I am of going wherever I please and assuming any form as I please.”(22-23)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु हनुमांस्तौ वीरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यकुशलः पुनर्नोवाच किंचन॥ २४॥
verses.m: Having spoken thus to the aforesaid heroes, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, Hanumān, for his part, who understood the true meaning of words and was an adept in expression, said nothing further. (24)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य रामो लक्ष्मणमब्रवीत्।
प्रहृष्टवदनः श्रीमान् भ्रातरं पार्श्वतः स्थितम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Hearing the foregoing speech of Hanumān, the glorious Rāma, who wore a most cheerful countenance, spoke as follows to his brother, Lakṣmaṇa, standing by his side : (25)

verses.text:
सचिवोऽयं कपीन्द्रस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
तमेव कांक्षमाणस्य ममान्तिकमिहागतः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “He who has arrived here in my presence is a minister of Sugrīva, the high-minded chief of monkeys, whom alone I was seeking. (26)

verses.text:
तमभ्यभाष सौमित्रे सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम्।
वाक्यज्ञं मधुरैर्वाक्यैः स्नेहयुक्तमरिंदमम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Answer in sweet words with affection the aforesaid monkey, who is a minister of Sugrīva, knows how to speak and is a tamer of foes, O Lakṣmaṇa ! (27)

verses.text:
नानृग्वेदविनीतस्य नायजुर्वेदधारिणः।
नासामवेदविदुषः शक्यमेवं विभाषितुम्॥ २८॥
verses.m: “To speak in the way he has done is not possible for one who has not studied Ṛgveda with an eye to its meaning, not memorized Yajurveda and has no knowledge of Sāmaveda either. (28)

verses.text:
नूनं व्याकरणं कृत्स्नमनेन बहुधा श्रुतम्।
बहु व्याहरतानेन न किंचिदपशब्दितम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Surely the entire range of Sanskrit grammar has been studied by him in many ways, as is clear from the fact that nothing has been wrongly worded by him even though speaking a good deal. (29)

verses.text:
न मुखे नेत्रयोश्चापि ललाटे च भ्रुवोस्तथा।
अन्येष्वपि च सर्वेषु दोषः संविदितः क्वचित्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “No fault of expression was noticed anywhere in his face nor even in his eyes, nor again in his forehead nor in his eyebrows nor in anyone of his other limbs. (30)

verses.text:
अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्।
उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “The speech emanating from his bosom and articulated by his throat is marked by absence of prolixity, is unambiguous and unfaltering and does not make a grating impression on one’s ears, uttered as it is in a modulated tone. (31)

verses.text:
संस्कारक्रमसम्पन्नामद्भुतामविलम्बिताम्।
उच्चारयति कल्याणीं वाचं हृदयहर्षिणीम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “He utters a wholesome, distinct and remarkable speech, which is grammatically correct, fluent and delightful to the mind. (32)

verses.text:
अनया चित्रया वाचा त्रिस्थानव्यञ्जनस्थया।
कस्य नाराध्यते चित्तमुद्यतासेररेरपि॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Whose mind will not be rendered favourable by this wonderful speech, which has its seat in three articulating organs, viz., the bosom, throat and head. To say nothing of others, the mind even of an enemy with his sword uplifted will be made friendly thereby. (33)

verses.text:
एवंविधो यस्य दूतो न भवेत् पार्थिवस्य तु।
सिद्ध्यन्ति हि कथं तस्य कार्याणां गतयोऽनघ॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “How can the progress of undertakings of a king in whose service no such envoy exists actually meet with success, O sinless brother? (34)

verses.text:
एवंगुणगणैर्युक्ता यस्य स्युः कार्यसाधकाः।
तस्य सिद्ध्यन्ति सर्वेऽर्था दूतवाक्यप्रचोदिताः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “By the very pleading of an envoy, all the objects of a sovereign in whose service there happen to be agents adorned with hosts of such virtues are surely accomplished.” (35)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सौमित्रिः सुग्रीवसचिवं कपिम्।
अभ्यभाषत वाक्यज्ञो वाक्यज्ञं पवनात्मजम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these words by Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) for his part, who knew how to speak, replied as follows to the monkey, Hanumān (son of the wind-god), a minister of Sugrīva, who also knew how to speak : (36)

verses.text:
विदिता नौ गुणा विद्वन् सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
तमेव चावां मार्गावः सुग्रीवं प्लवगेश्वरम्॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “The virtues of the high-minded Surgrīva are known to us, O learned monkey ! We too are looking for the self same Sugrīva, a ruler of monkeys. (37)

verses.text:
यथा ब्रवीषि हनुमन् सुग्रीववचनादिह।
तत् तथा हि करिष्यावो वचनात् तव सत्तम॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “O excellent Hanumān, as desired by Sugrīva, we are prepared for an alliance with him.” (38)

verses.text:
तत् तस्य वाक्यं निपुणं निशम्य
प्रहृष्टरूपः पवनात्मजः कपिः।
मनः समाधाय जयोपपत्तौ
सख्यं तदा कर्तुमियेष ताभ्याम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Having carefully heard the aforesaid reply of Lakṣmaṇa, and setting his heart on the consummation of Sugrīva’s truimph, Hanumān (the monkey sprung from the loins of the wind-god), who wore a most cheerful countenance, sought then and there to negotiate an alliance with the two princes.(39)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहृष्टो हनुमान् कृत्यवानिति तद्वचः।
श्रुत्वा मधुरभावं च सुग्रीवं मनसा गतः॥ १॥
verses.m: Highly rejoiced to hear the aforesaid speech of Śrī Rāma as well as of Śrī Rāma’s friendly feeling towards Sugrīva and to learn that Śrī Rāma too had some purpose in meeting him, Hanumān then mentally sought the presence of Sugrīva. (1)

verses.text:
भाव्यो राज्यागमस्तस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
यदयं कृत्यवान् प्राप्तः कृत्यं चैतदुपागतम्॥ २॥
verses.m: He said to himself, ‘Attainment of sovereignty on the part of that high-souled Sugrīva is sure to come about as is clear from the fact that Śrī Rāma has come here with a purpose and the duty of accomplishing it has devolved on Sugrīva.’ (2)

verses.text:
ततः परमसंहृष्टो हनूमान् प्लवगोत्तमः।
प्रत्युवाच ततो वाक्यं रामं वाक्यविशारदः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Supremely rejoiced at the thought, Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, thereupon replied as follows to Śrī Rāma, who was an adept in expression : (3)

verses.text:
किमर्थं त्वं वनं घोरं पम्पाकाननमण्डितम्।
आगतः सानुजो दुर्गं नानाव्यालमृगायुतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “What for have you come with your younger brother to this dreadful forest of Daṇḍaka, which is so difficult of access and is infested with birds of prey and deer of every description, though adorned with the woodland encompassing Pampā?” (4)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा लक्ष्मणो रामचोदितः।
आचचक्षे महात्मानं रामं दशरथात्मजम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid question of Hanumān, Lakṣmaṇa, as urged by Śrī Rāma (by means of gestures), spoke as follows about the high-souled Śrī Rāma, son of Emperor Daśaratha : (5)

verses.text:
राजा दशरथो नाम द्युतिमान् धर्मवत्सलः।
चातुर्वर्ण्यं स्वधर्मेण नित्यमेवाभिपालयन्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Ruling all the four grades of society from day to day according to the code of conduct prescribed for himself, there was a king, Daśaratha by name, who was full of splendour and fond of virtue. (6)

verses.text:
न द्वेष्टा विद्यते तस्य स तु द्वेष्टि न कंचन।
स तु सर्वेषु भूतेषु पितामह इवापरः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “None was inimical to him nor did he for his part hate anyone. He was in fact another Brahmā (the grandfather of the entire creation) to all created beings. (7)

verses.text:
अग्निष्टोमादिभिर्यज्ञैरिष्टवानाप्तदक्षिणैः।
तस्यायं पूर्वजः पुत्रो रामो नाम जनैः श्रुतः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “He propitiated the Lord by means of sacrificial performances such as Agniṣṭoma, in which handsome fees were paid to the priests officiating in them. This prince is his first-born son, called by the people by the name of Śrī Rāma. (8)

verses.text:
शरण्यः सर्वभूतानां पितुर्निर्देशपारगः।
ज्येष्ठो दशरथस्यायं पुत्राणां गुणवत्तरः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Fit to protect all created beings, he has fully carried out the commands of his father. He is the eldest of all Daśaratha’s sons and is more qualified than all of them. (9)

verses.text:
राजलक्षणसंयुक्तः संयुक्तो राज्यसम्पदा।
राज्याद् भ्रष्टो मया वस्तुं वने सार्धमिहागतः॥ १०॥
भार्यया च महाभाग सीतयानुगतो वशी।
दिनक्षये महातेजाः प्रभयेव दिवाकरः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Endowed with the bodily marks of a king, he was just going to be invested by his father with royal fortune (in the shape of the office of Prince Regent) when he was suddenly disinherited of his sovereignty and came here to live in the forest with me, followed by his consort, Sītā too—even as the sun sinks below horizon with its splendour at the close of the day—possessed as he was of extraordinary brilliance and had fully controlled himself. (10-11)

verses.text:
अहमस्यावरो भ्राता गुणैर्दास्यमुपागतः।
कृतज्ञस्य बहुज्ञस्य लक्ष्मणो नाम नामतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I am his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa by name, who was lovingly drawn by his virtues to become his servant, appreciating as he does the services, rendered to him and making much of even small services. (12)

verses.text:
सुखार्हस्य महार्हस्य सर्वभूतहितात्मनः।
ऐश्वर्येण विहीनस्य वनवासे रतस्य च॥ १३॥
रक्षसापहृता भार्या रहिते कामरूपिणा।
तच्च न ज्ञायते रक्षः पत्नी येनास्य वा हृता॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The spouse of my aforesaid brother, who is worthy of all comforts, who deserves to be adored even by the trio adored by all (viz., Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva) and whose mind is set on the good of all created beings, nay, who is now totally bereft of all lordship and is devoted to a forest life, was carried off at a place where none was beside her, by an ogre who is capable of assuming any form at will. That ogre, however, by whom his consort has been stolen away is not known. (13-14)

verses.text:
दनुर्नाम दितेः पुत्रः शापाद् राक्षसतां गतः।
आख्यातस्तेन सुग्रीवः समर्थो वानराधिपः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “There was a son of Diti, Danu (Kabandha) by name, who had by virtue of an imprecation assumed the state of an ogre. Sugrīva, the powerful overlord of monkeys, was mentioned to us by him. (15)

verses.text:
स ज्ञास्यति महावीर्यस्तव भार्यापहारिणम्।
एवमुक्त्वा दनुः स्वर्गं भ्राजमानो दिवं गतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘That exceptionally powerful monkey will find out the ogre who stole away your consort !’ Saying so, and emitting light (all-round), Danu rose to the skies on his way to heaven. (16)

verses.text:
एतत् ते सर्वमाख्यातं याथातथ्येन पृच्छतः।
अहं चैव च रामश्च सुग्रीवं शरणं गतौ॥ १७॥
verses.m: “All this has been narrated in all sincerity to you, who inquired about it. Now Śrī Rāma as well as myself have sought Sugrīva as our refuge. (17)

verses.text:
एष दत्त्वा च वित्तानि प्राप्य चानुत्तमं यशः।
लोकनाथः पुरा भूत्वा सुग्रीवं नाथमिच्छति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Having given away all his riches to beggars while leaving Ayodhyā for the forest and earned unsurpassed glory, and having been in the past the protector of the world, Śrī Rāma desires to have Sugrīva as his benefactor. (18)

verses.text:
सीता यस्य स्नुषा चासीच्छरण्यो धर्मवत्सलः।
तस्य पुत्रः शरण्यश्च सुग्रीवं शरणं गतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Himself affording shelter to others and fond of virtues, the son of King Daśaratha, (who was fit to protect others and), whose daughter-in-law was Sītā, has sought Sugrīva as his refuge. (19)

verses.text:
सर्वलोकस्य धर्मात्मा शरण्यः शरणं पुरा।
गुरुर्मे राघवः सोऽयं सुग्रीवं शरणं गतः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “The selfsame Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), my eldest brother, whose mind is set on virtue and who was once not only fit to protect, but the actual protector of the whole world, has sought Sugrīva as his asylum. (20)

verses.text:
यस्य प्रसादे सततं प्रसीदेयुरिमाः प्रजाः।
स रामो वानरेन्द्रस्य प्रसादमभिकांक्षते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “That Rāma, on whose being propitious all these created beings remain constantly pleased, seeks the favour of Sugrīva, king of monkeys ! (21)

verses.text:
येन सर्वगुणोपेताः पृथिव्यां सर्वपार्थिवाः।
मानिताः सततं राज्ञा सदा दशरथेन वै॥ २२॥
तस्यायं पूर्वजः पुत्रस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः।
सुग्रीवं वानरेन्द्रं तु रामः शरणमागतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Śrī Rāma, the first-born son, well-known through all the three worlds, of King Daśaratha—by whom in reality all the kings on earth, endowed with all kinds of virtues, were unceasingly honoured everyday, has for his part sought Sugrīva, the lord of monkeys, as his refuge. (22-23)

verses.text:
शोकाभिभूते रामे तु शोकार्ते शरणं गते।
कर्तुमर्हति सुग्रीवः प्रसादं सह यूथपैः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Sugrīva alongwith his troop-leaders ought in his turn to show his grace to Śrī Rāma, who is overwhelmed and stricken with grief and has sought Sugrīva as his refuge.” (24)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवाणं सौमित्रिं करुणं साश्रुपातनम्।
हनूमान् प्रत्युवाचेदं वाक्यं वाक्यविशारदः॥ २५॥
verses.m: To Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā), speaking as aforesaid in a pathetic tone accompanied by a flow of tears, Hanumān, who was an adept in expression, replied as follows : (25)

verses.text:
ईदृशा बुद्धिसम्पन्ना जितक्रोधा जितेन्द्रियाः।
द्रष्टव्या वानरेन्द्रेण दिष्ट्या दर्शनमागताः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Through good luck people like you, who are rich in wisdom, have subdued their anger and mastered their senses, and who deserve to be seen by Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys), have fallen within the range of our sight. (26)

verses.text:
स हि राज्याश्च विभ्रष्टः कृतवैरश्च वालिना।
हृतदारो वने त्रस्तो भ्रात्रा विनिकृतो भृशम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Antagonized and deposed from his throne, nay, actually deprived of his spouse and exiled by his elder brother, Vālī, Sugrīva lives in the forest greatly alarmed. (27)

verses.text:
करिष्यति स साहाय्यं युवयोर्भास्करात्मजः।
सुग्रीवः सह चास्माभिः सीतायाः परिमार्गणे॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Alongwith us (monkeys) the said Sugrīva, sprung from the loins of the sun-god, will render help to you in tracing out Sītā.” (28)

verses.text:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा हनुमान् श्लक्ष्णं मधुरया गिरा।
बभाषे साधु गच्छामः सुग्रीवमिति राघवम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having spoken thus in a sweet tone, Hanumān softly said to Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, “Well, let us proceed to meet Sugrīva.” (29)

verses.text:
एवं ब्रुवन्तं धर्मात्मा हनूमन्तं स लक्ष्मणः।
प्रतिपूज्य यथान्यायमिदं प्रोवाच राघवम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: Having honoured according to the rules of propriety Hanumān, who was speaking thus, the celebrated Lakṣmaṇa, whose mind was set on virtue, submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) : (30)

verses.text:
कपिः कथयते हृष्टो यथायं मारुतात्मजः।
कृत्यवान् सोऽपि सम्प्राप्तः कृतकृत्योऽसि राघव॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Full of joy, this son of the wind-god speaks aright. Sugrīva too has some end to be achieved (through you). Having arrived here at the right time, you have your object accomplished, O scion of Raghu ! (31)

verses.text:
प्रसन्नमुखवर्णश्च व्यक्तं हृष्टश्च भाषते।
नानृतं वक्ष्यते वीरो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Full of delight, Hanumān speaks unambiguously and with a cheerful glow on his face. The gallant son of the wind-god would not tell a lie.” (32)

verses.text:
ततः स सुमहाप्राज्ञो हनूमान् मारुतात्मजः।
जगामादाय तौ वीरौ हरिराजाय राघवौ॥ ३३॥
verses.m: Taking Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, the two heroic scions of Raghu, the aforesaid Hanumān, the extremely wise son of the wind-god, thereupon sallied forth to meet Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys). (33)

verses.text:
भिक्षुरूपं परित्यज्य वानरं रूपमास्थितः।
पृष्ठमारोप्य तौ वीरौ जगाम कपिकुञ्जरः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: Having abandoned the guise of a mendicant (recluse) and resumed the form of a monkey, and placing the aforesaid two heroes on his shoulders, Hanumān (a veritable elephant among monkeys) departed for Ṛṣyamūka. (34)

verses.text:
स तु विपुलयशाः कपिप्रवीरः
पवनसुतः कृतकृत्यवत् प्रहृष्टः।
गिरिवरमुरुविक्रमः प्रयातः
स शुभमतिः सह रामलक्ष्मणाभ्याम्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Overjoyed like one whose object has been accomplished, that great hero among the monkeys, the noble-minded son of the wind-god, for his part, who had earned an extensive fame and was possessed of extraordinary prowess, proceeded alongwith Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Ṛṣyamūka (the foremost of mountains). (35)

verses.text:
ऋष्यमूकात् तु हनुमान् गत्वा तं मलयं गिरिम्।
आचचक्षे तदा वीरौ कपिराजाय राघवौ॥ १॥
verses.m: Springing to the celebrated Mount Malaya (an offshoot of Ṛṣyamūka) from the Ṛṣyamūka hill, Hanumān for his part forthwith announced Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa (the two scions of Raghu) to Sugrīva (the king of monkeys). (1)

verses.text:
अयं रामो महाप्राज्ञ सम्प्राप्तो दृढविक्रमः।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा रामोऽयं सत्यविक्रमः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Here is Rāma duly arrived with Lakṣmaṇa, his younger brother, O highly wise king of unbending prowess ! The aforesaid Rāma is possessed of unfailing prowess. (2)

verses.text:
इक्ष्वाकूणां कुले जातो रामो दशरथात्मजः।
धर्मे निगदितश्चैव पितुर्निर्देशकारकः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Born in the line of Ikṣwākus, Śrī Rāma is sprung from the loins of King Daśaratha, and is well-known for his devotion to duty. He has come to the forest in obedience to the behest of his father. (3)

verses.text:
राजसूयाश्वमेधैश्च वह्निर्येनाभितर्पितः।
दक्षिणाश्च तथोत्सृष्टा गावः शतसहस्रशः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma is a son of the same King Daśaratha by whom the god of fire was fully propitiated by means of Rājasūya and Aśwamedha sacrifices and liberal fees were given away as well as cows in hundreds of thousands. (4)

verses.text:
तपसा सत्यवाक्येन वसुधा येन पालिता।
स्त्रीहेतोस्तस्य पुत्रोऽयं रामोऽरण्यं समागतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Nay, the earth was ruled by him by recourse to truthful words and asceticism. Because of the plighted word given by the aforesaid king to his wife (Kaikeyī, Rāma’s stepmother) Śrī Rāma has come to (live in) the forest. (5)

verses.text:
तस्यास्य वसतोऽरण्ये नियतस्य महात्मनः।
रावणेन हृता भार्या स त्वां शरणमागतः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The spouse of the same high-souled Śrī Rāma was carried off by Rāvaṇa while the former was leading a disciplined life in the forest. He has accordingly sought you as his refuge. (6)

verses.text:
भवता सख्यकामौ तौ भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
प्रगृह्य चार्चयस्वैतौ पूजनीयतमावुभौ॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Receiving and accepting as your own the aforesaid two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who seek friendship with you and are most deserving of homage, pray, offer (formal) worship to both these princes.” (7)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा हनूमतो वाक्यं सुग्रीवो वानराधिपः।
दर्शनीयतमो भूत्वा प्रीत्योवाच च राघवम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Hearing the submission of Hanumān and appearing most good-looking, Sugrīva, the overlord of monkeys, lovingly approached and submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) : (8)

verses.text:
भवान् धर्मविनीतश्च सुतपाः सर्ववत्सलः।
आख्याता वायुपुत्रेण तत्त्वतो मे भवद्गुणाः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “You have been trained in the practice of righteousness, and are highly ascetic and fond of all; your virtues have already been recounted by Hanumān, son of the wind-god, in their reality. (9)

verses.text:
तन्ममैवैष सत्कारो लाभश्चैवोत्तमः प्रभो।
यत्त्वमिच्छसि सौहार्दं वानरेण मया सह॥ १०॥
verses.m: “It is an honour to myself and my foremost gain too, my lord, that you seek amity with me, a monkey. (10)

verses.text:
रोचते यदि मे सख्यं बाहुरेष प्रसारितः।
गृह्यतां पाणिना पाणिर्मर्यादा बध्यतां ध्रुवा॥ ११॥
verses.m: “If my friendship is acceptable to you, here is my hand extended before you. Let this hand be clasped with yours and an abiding pact entered into with me.” (11)

verses.text:
एतत् तु वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य सुभाषितम्।
सम्प्रहृष्टमना हस्तं पीडयामास पाणिना॥ १२॥
verses.m: Extremely delighted at heart to hear this beautifully-worded submission of Sugrīva, Śrī Rāma for his part pressed his hand with his own. (12)

verses.text:
हृष्टः सौहृदमालम्ब्य पर्यष्वजत पीडितम्।
ततो हनूमान् संत्यज्य भिक्षुरूपमरिंदमः॥ १३॥
काष्ठयोः स्वेन रूपेण जनयामास पावकम्।
दीप्यमानं ततो वह्निं पुष्पैरभ्यर्च्य सत्कृतम्॥ १४॥
तयोर्मध्ये तु सुप्रीतो निदधौ सुसमाहितः।
ततोऽग्निं दीप्यमानं तौ चक्रतुश्च प्रदक्षिणम्॥ १५॥
सुग्रीवो राघवश्चैव वयस्यत्वमुपागतौ।
ततः सुप्रीतमनसौ तावुभौ हरिराघवौ॥ १६॥
अन्योन्यमभिवीक्षन्तौ न तृप्तिमभिजग्मतुः।
त्वं वयस्योऽसि हृद्यो मे ह्येकं दुःखं सुखं च नौ॥ १७॥
सुग्रीवो राघवं वाक्यमित्युवाच प्रहृष्टवत्।
ततः सुपर्णबहुलां भङ्क्त्वा शाखां सुपुष्पिताम्॥ १८॥
सालस्यास्तीर्य सुग्रीवो निषसाद सराघवः।
लक्ष्मणायाथ संहृष्टो हनुमान् मारुतात्मजः॥ १९॥
शाखां चन्दनवृक्षस्य ददौ परमपुष्पिताम्।
ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवः श्लक्ष्णं मधुरया गिरा॥ २०॥
प्रत्युवाच तदा रामं हर्षव्याकुललोचनः।
अहं विनिकृतो राम चरामीह भयार्दितः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Nay, adopting a friendly attitude, he joyously embraced Sugrīva, who had been subjected to oppression. Giving up the form of a mendicant (recluse), and appearing in his own native form, Hanumān, the tamer of his foes, thereupon lighted a fire out of a pair of logs of wood. Highly pleased and fully composed, Hanumān for his part thereupon placed the fire, after it had been honoured by being worshipped with flowers, between Śrī Rāma and Sugrīva. Having contracted friendship (with each other), the aforesaid Sugrīva and Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) too then went round the inflamed fire clockwise. Highly delighted in mind, both the aforesaid friends, Sugrīva (a monkey) and Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) did not experience satiety while gazing on each other. Full of excessive joy, Sugrīva spoke as follows to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) : “Since you are now a friend beloved of my heart, our woe and joy are one.” Breaking a bough of a sal tree, laden with flowers and thick with beautiful leaves, and laying it down, Sugrīva then sat down on it with Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). Highly rejoiced, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, now offered to Lakṣmaṇa a fully blossomed bough of a sandalwood tree. Highly rejoiced, Sugrīva thereupon gently submitted forthwith in a sweet tone as follows to Śrī Rāma, his eyes bedimmed with joy : “Having been exiled (by my elder brother, Vālī), I move about in this forest, oppressed as I am with fear, O Rāma ! (13—21)

verses.text:
हृतभार्यो वने त्रस्तो दुर्गमेतदुपाश्रितः।
सोऽहं त्रस्तो वने भीतो वसाम्युद्भ्रान्तचेतनः॥ २२॥
वालिना निकृतो भ्रात्रा कृतवैरश्च राघव।
वालिनो मे महाभाग भयार्तस्याभयं कुरु॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Alarmed as I am, my spouse too having been taken away, I have sought shelter for my protection in this mountain, which is difficult of access for Vālī. Having been banished and antagonized by my brother, (Vālī), O scion of Raghu, I live in the forest perturbed and alarmed, my mind being confused. Therefore, grant me security, O highly blessed one, from Vālī, stricken with fear as I am. (22-23)

verses.text:
कर्तुमर्हसि काकुत्स्थ भयं मे न भवेद् यथा।
एवमुक्तस्तु तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्मवत्सलः॥ २४॥
प्रत्यभाषत काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीवं प्रहसन्निव।
उपकारफलं मित्रं विदितं मे महाकपे॥ २५॥
verses.m: “You ought to ensure, O scion of Kākutstha, that no fear may linger in me.” Implored thus, the glorious Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kākutstha), for his part, who knew what is right and was fond of righteousness, replied (as follows) to Sugrīva as though heartily laughing : “It is known to me that service is the fruit yielded by a friend, O mighty monkey ! (24-25)

verses.text:
वालिनं तं वधिष्यामि तव भार्यापहारिणम्।
अमोघाः सूर्यसंकाशा ममेमे निशिताः शराः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I shall dispose of the notorious Vālī, who has wrested your wife. Infallible are these sharpened shafts of mine, glorious as the sun. (26)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् वालिनि दुर्वृत्ते निपतिष्यन्ति वेगिताः।
कङ्कपत्रप्रतिच्छन्ना महेन्द्राशनिसंनिभाः॥ २७॥
तीक्ष्णाग्रा ऋजुपर्वाणः सरोषा भुजगा इव।
तमद्य वालिनं पश्य तीक्ष्णैराशीविषोपमैः॥ २८॥
शरैर्विनिहतं भूमौ प्रकीर्णमिव पर्वतम्।
स तु तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्यात्मनो हितम्।
सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतः परमं वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Covered at the end with the feathers of a buzzard and provided with a momentum, and shining brightly like the thunderbolt of the mighty Indra (the lord of paradise), these arrows with pointed heads and straight joints will descend like angry serpents on that Vālī of immoral conduct. See Vālī struck down today on the earth like a scattered mountain with pointed shafts resembling venomous serpents.” Supremely rejoiced to hear the aforesaid assurance, favourable to him, of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the celebrated Sugrīva for his part uttered the following excellent words : (27—29)

verses.text:
तव प्रसादेन नृसिंह वीर
प्रियां च राज्यं च समाप्नुयामहम्।
तथा कुरु त्वं नरदेव वैरिणं
यथा न हिंस्यात् स पुनर्ममाग्रजम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “By your goodwill, O lion among men, I hope to recover my darling as well as my sovereignty. Pray, handle my hostile elder brother in such a way, O heroic prince, that he may not persecute me any more.” (30)

verses.text:
सीताकपीन्द्रक्षणदाचराणां
राजीवहेमज्वलनोपमानि।
सुग्रीवरामप्रणयप्रसङ्गे
वामानि नेत्राणि समं स्फुरन्ति॥ ३१॥
verses.m: On the occasion of the friendship concluded between Sugrīva and Śrī Rāma the left eyes of Sītā, Vālī (the king of monkeys) and Rāvaṇa (an ogre, lit., a night-stalker)—which were lotus-like, gold-like and fire-like, respectively, synchronously throbbed.* (31)

verses.text:
पुनरेवाब्रवीत् प्रीतो राघवं रघुनन्दनम्।
अयमाख्याति ते राम सचिवो मन्त्रिसत्तमः॥ १॥
हनुमान् यन्निमित्तं त्वं निर्जनं वनमागतः।
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वसतश्च वने तव॥ २॥
रक्षसापहृता भार्या मैथिली जनकात्मजा।
त्वया वियुक्ता रुदती लक्ष्मणेन च धीमता॥ ३॥
अन्तरं प्रेप्सुना तेन हत्वा गृध्रं जटायुषम्।
भार्यावियोगजं दुःखं प्रापितस्तेन रक्षसा॥ ४॥
verses.m: Sugrīva once more lovingly submitted as follows to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the delight of the Raghus : “This Hanumān, a veritable jewel among my counsellors and your servant, has revealed to me the purpose for which you have sought this lonely forest, O Rāma ! He has told me how while you were living in the forest with your brother, Lakṣmaṇa, your consort, Sītā (a princess of Mithilā), daughter of Janaka, was carried off, wailing at a time when she was disunited from you as well as from the talented Lakṣmaṇa, after killing the vulture, Jaṭāyu, by that ogre Rāvaṇa, who had (all along) been seeking an opportune moment (to lay his violent hands on her), and how you have been subjected by that ogre to the agony of separation from your spouse. (1—4)

verses.text:
भार्यावियोगजं दुःखं नचिरात् त्वं विमोक्ष्यसे।
अहं तामानयिष्यामि नष्टां वेदश्रुतीमिव॥ ५॥
verses.m: “You will cast away before long the agony of separation from your consort; for I will bring her back even as the Lord (in His descent as the Divine Fish) recovered the Veda (the Divine Revelation) that had vanished out of sight. (5)

verses.text:
रसातले वा वर्तन्तीं वर्तन्तीं वा नभस्तले।
अहमानीय दास्यामि तव भार्यामरिंदम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Recovering your consort, O tamer of foes, no matter whether she exists in the bowels of the earth or is living in the vaults of heaven, I shall deliver her to you. (6)

verses.text:
इदं तथ्यं मम वचस्त्वमवेहि च राघव।
न शक्या सा जरयितुमपि सेन्द्रैः सुरासुरैः॥ ७॥
तव भार्या महाबाहो भक्ष्यं विषकृतं यथा।
त्यज शोकं महाबाहो तां कान्तामानयामि ते॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Know this statement of mine to be true, O mighty-armed scion of Raghu, that the aforesaid consort of yours cannot be absorbed (with impunity) even by gods and demons including Indra, any more than food cooked with poison. Cast away grief, O mighty-armed prince, I shall surely bring back that darling of yours. (7-8)•

verses.text:
अनुमानात् तु जानामि मैथिली सा न संशयः।
ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रक्षसा रौद्रकर्मणा॥ ९॥
क्रोशन्ती रामरामेति लक्ष्मणेति च विस्वरम्।
स्फुरन्ती रावणस्याङ्के पन्नगेन्द्रवधूर्यथा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “By surmise on my part I conclude that the aforesaid princess of Mithilā was seen by me while being carried off by Rāvaṇa (the ogre) of terrible deeds, crying in a husky voice “Rāma, Rāma !” and “Lakṣmaṇa !” and wriggling like a female serpent in the arms of Rāvaṇa—there is no doubt about it. (9-10)

verses.text:
आत्मना पञ्चमं मां हि दृष्ट्वा शैलतले स्थितम्।
उत्तरीयं तया त्यक्तं शुभान्याभरणानि च॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Seeing me standing at the foot of Mount Malaya (in the company of four others) with myself as the fifth, a wrapper was actually dropped by her as also shining jewels. (11)

verses.text:
तान्यस्माभिर्गृहीतानि निहितानि च राघव।
आनयिष्याम्यहं तानि प्रत्यभिज्ञातुमर्हसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “They were collected by us and have been preserved, O scion of Raghu ! I shall presently bring them; you ought to (be able to) recognize them (as belonging to Sītā).” (12)

verses.text:
तमब्रवीत् ततो रामः सुग्रीवं प्रियवादिनम्।
आनयस्व सखे शीघ्रं किमर्थं प्रविलम्बसे॥ १३॥
verses.m: Śrī Rāma thereupon said to the celebrated Sugrīva, who had spoken agreeable words to him, “Bring them soon, my friend; wherefore do you tarry !” (13)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवः शैलस्य गहनां गुहाम्।
प्रविवेश ततः शीघ्रं राघवप्रियकाम्यया॥ १४॥
verses.m: Urged in these words, Sugrīva for his part then quickly penetrated deep into a cavern in the mountain, which was difficult of access, with intent to sooth Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). (14)

verses.text:
उत्तरीयं गृहीत्वा तु स तान्याभरणानि च।
इदं पश्येति रामाय दर्शयामास वानरः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Taking hold of the wrapper as well as of the aforesaid jewels, the said monkey, Sugrīva, for his part showed them to Śrī Rāma, saying : “Look here !” (15)

verses.text:
ततो गृहीत्वा वासस्तु शुभान्याभरणानि च।
अभवद् बाष्पसंरुद्धो नीहारेणेव चन्द्रमाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: Then holding the raiment as well as the sparkling jewels, Śrī Rāma for his part was fully covered up with tears even as the moon is with fog. (16)

verses.text:
सीतास्नेहप्रवृत्तेन स तु बाष्पेण दूषितः।
हा प्रियेति रुदन् धैर्यमुत्सृज्य न्यपतत् क्षितौ॥ १७॥
