verses.m: Stained with tears that gushed forth due to his affection for Sītā, and losing his presence of mind, Śrī Rāma for his part toppled down to the ground crying “Ah my darling !” (17)

verses.text:
हृदि कृत्वा स बहुशस्तमलंकारमुत्तमम्।
निशश्वास भृशं सर्पो बिलस्थ इव रोषितः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Pressing that excellent jewel to his bosom repeatedly, he violently hissed like a serpent provoked in its hole. (18)

verses.text:
अविच्छिन्नाश्रुवेगस्तु सौमित्रिं प्रेक्ष्य पार्श्वतः।
परिदेवयितुं दीनं रामः समुपचक्रमे॥ १९॥
verses.m: Perceiving Lakṣmaṇa (son of Sumitrā) by his side, Śrī Rāma for his part duly began to wail piteously as follows, the stream of his tears remaining unbroken : (19)

verses.text:
पश्य लक्ष्मण वैदेह्या संत्यक्तं ह्रियमाणया।
उत्तरीयमिदं भूमौ शरीराद् भूषणानि च॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Behold, O Lakṣmaṇa, this wrapper as well as the jewels consciously dropped on the ground from her person by Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) while being borne away by the ogre. (20)

verses.text:
शाद्वलिन्यां ध्रुवं भूम्यां सीतया ह्रियमाणया।
उत्सृष्टं भूषणमिदं तथा रूपं हि दृश्यते॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Surely this jewel was dropped on a grassy ground by Sītā while being borne away as is evident from the fact that it looks just the same in appearance.” (21)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु रामेण लक्ष्मणो वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
नाहं जानामि केयूरे नाहं जानामि कुण्डले॥ २२॥
नूपुरे त्वभिजानामि नित्यं पादाभिवन्दनात्।
ततस्तु राघवो वाक्यं सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्॥ २३॥
verses.m: Spoken to as aforesaid by Śrī Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa for his part replied as follows : “Neither do I recognize the armlets nor do I know the earrings, I only recognize the anklets due to my bowing at her feet everyday.” Thereupon Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) for his part spoke as follows to Sugrīva : (22-23)

verses.text:
ब्रूहि सुग्रीव कं देशं ह्रियन्ती लक्षिता त्वया।
रक्षसा रौद्ररूपेण मम प्राणप्रिया हृता॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Pray, point out, O Sugrīva, to which land Sītā (who is dearer to me than my life) was borne away by the ogre of terrible aspect as she was perceived by you while being carried off. (24)

verses.text:
क्व वा वसति तद् रक्षो महद् व्यसनदं मम।
यन्निमित्तमहं सर्वान् नाशयिष्यामि राक्षसान्॥ २५॥
हरता मैथिलीं येन मां च रोषयता ध्रुवम्।
आत्मनो जीवितान्ताय मृत्युद्वारमपावृतम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Also, let me know where dwells that ogre, who has inflicted enormous suffering on me and on whose account I shall exterminate all the ogres, and by whom the portals of Death have undoubtedly been opened for the termination of his own life, carrying off (as he did) Sītā (the princess of Mithilā) and provoking me. (25-26)

verses.text:
मम दयिततमा हृता वनाद्
रजनिचरेण विमथ्य येन सा।
कथय मम रिपुं तमद्य वै
प्लवगपते यमसंनिधिं नयामि॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Point out to me, O lord of monkeys, the ranger of the night, my enemy, by whom my most beloved spouse was borne away from the forest after being put off the scent. I shall surely despatch him to the presence of Death today.” (27)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवो रामेणार्तेन वानरः।
अब्रवीत् प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं सबाष्पं बाष्पगद्गदः॥ १॥
verses.m: Spoken to as aforesaid by Śrī Rāma in distress, the monkey chief, Sugrīva, for his part, replied as follows to Śrī Rāma (who had tears in his eyes) with joined palms and in a voice choked with tears : (1)

verses.text:
न जाने निलयं तस्य सर्वथा पापरक्षसः।
सामर्थ्यं विक्रमं वापि दौष्कुलेयस्य वा कुलम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “I do not know at all the abode or strength or prowess or even the pedigree of that sinful ogre of vile birth. (2)

verses.text:
सत्यं तु प्रतिजानामि त्यज शोकमरिंदम।
करिष्यामि तथा यत्नं यथा प्राप्स्यसि मैथिलीम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Cast away grief, O tamer of foes ! I for my part make an unfailing promise to you : I will strive in such a way that you will be able to recover Sītā (a princess of Mithilā). (3)

verses.text:
रावणं सगणं हत्वा परितोष्यात्मपौरुषम्।
तथास्मि कर्ता नचिराद् यथा प्रीतो भविष्यसि॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Having killed Rāvaṇa with his followers and given satisfaction to you (thereby), I will exert my strength before long in such a way that you will get pleased with me. (4)

verses.text:
अलं वैक्लव्यमालम्ब्य धैर्यमात्मगतं स्मर।
त्वद्विधानां न सदृशमीदृशं बुद्धिलाघवम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Cease giving way to mental weakness and call to mind your native fortitude. Such littleness of mind is not becoming of people like you. (5)

verses.text:
मयापि व्यसनं प्राप्तं भार्याविरहजं महत्।
नाहमेवं हि शोचामि धैर्यं न च परित्यजे॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Great adversity born of separation from my spouse has been met with by me too. I, however, neither grieve nor lose courage thus. (6)

verses.text:
नाहं तामनुशोचामि प्राकृतो वानरोऽपि सन्।
महात्मा च विनीतश्च किं पुनर्धृतिमान् महान्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “A common monkey though I am, I do not grieve for her; how much less should you, a great man, high-souled and cultured and endowed with courage as you are? (7)

verses.text:
बाष्पमापतितं धैर्यान्निग्रहीतुं त्वमर्हसि।
मर्यादां सत्त्वयुक्तानां धृतिं नोत्स्रष्टुमर्हसि॥ ८॥
verses.m: “By recourse to fortitude you ought to restrain the tears which have appeared in your eyes. You ought not to abandon propriety of conduct and fortitude, characteristic of those possessed of resolution. (8)

verses.text:
व्यसने वार्थकृच्छ्रे वा भये वा जीवितान्तगे।
विमृशंश्च स्वया बुद्ध्या धृतिमान् नावसीदति॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Deliberating by recourse to his own faculty of judgment as to what remedy be adopted in suffering, caused by separation from one’s object of love or in a financial crisis or in a danger leading to the end of one’s life, a man of fortitude does not come to grief. (9)

verses.text:
बालिशस्तु नरो नित्यं वैक्लव्यं योऽनुवर्तते।
स मज्जत्यवशः शोके भाराक्रान्तेव नौर्जले॥ १०॥
verses.m: “A foolish man, however, who always gives way to mental weakness, is helplessly plunged in grief, even as a boat loaded with excessive weight sinks in water. (10)

verses.text:
एषोऽञ्जलिर्मया बद्धः प्रणयात् त्वां प्रसादये।
पौरुषं श्रय शोकस्य नान्तरं दातुमर्हसि॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Here are palms joined by me (in supplication) and I beseech you through love: pray, have recourse to manliness; you ought not to allow grief a passage to enter your mind. (11)

verses.text:
ये शोकमनुवर्तन्ते न तेषां विद्यते सुखम्।
तेजश्च क्षीयते तेषां न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Happiness does not dwell in them who yield to grief; their strength too diminishes. Hence you should not grieve. (12)

verses.text:
शोकेनाभिप्रपन्नस्य जीविते चापि संशयः।
स शोकं त्यज राजेन्द्र धैर्यमाश्रय केवलम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “There is danger even to the life of a man, who is overwhelmed with grief. Therefore, cast away grief, O king of kings, and have recourse to fortitude alone. (13)

verses.text:
हितं वयस्यभावेन ब्रूहि नोपदिशामि ते।
वयस्यतां पूजयन्मे न त्वं शोचितुमर्हसि॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I tender a salutary advice to you in a spirit of friendship and do not moralize. Honouring my friendship you should not grieve.” (14)

verses.text:
मधुरं सान्त्वितस्तेन सुग्रीवेण स राघवः।
मुखमश्रुपरिक्लिन्नं वस्त्रान्तेन प्रमार्जयत्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Sweetly comforted in these words by the aforesaid Sugrīva, the celebrated Śrī Rāma wiped his face, which had been bathed in tears, with an end of his loin-cloth. (15)

verses.text:
प्रकृतिस्थस्तु काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीवचनात् प्रभुः।
सम्परिष्वज्य सुग्रीवमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Closely embracing Sugrīva, when he (Śrī Rāma) had returned to his normal condition, as a result of the former’s words of consolation, Lord Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) for his part replied as follow : (16)

verses.text:
कर्तव्यं यद् वयस्येन स्निग्धेन च हितेन च।
अनुरूपं च युक्तं च कृतं सुग्रीव तत् त्वया॥ १७॥
verses.m: “That which ought to be done by a loving and benevolent friend, nay, that which is worthy of you as well as proper has been done by you, O Sugrīva ! (17)

verses.text:
एष च प्रकृतिस्थोऽहमनुनीतस्त्वया सखे।
दुर्लभो हीदृशो बन्धुरस्मिन् काले विशेषतः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Counselled by you, my friend, I have returned to normalcy now. Such a friend as you are, is indeed difficult to get, particularly at this time of adversity. (18)

verses.text:
किं तु यत्नस्त्वया कार्यो मैथिल्याः परिमार्गणे।
राक्षसस्य च रौद्रस्य रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Endeavour should, however, be made by you in the direction of tracing out Sītā (the princess of Mithilā) as well as the terrible and evil-minded ogre, Rāvaṇa. (19)

verses.text:
मया च यदनुष्ठेयं विस्रब्धेन तदुच्यताम्।
वर्षास्विव च सुक्षेत्रे सर्वं सम्पद्यते तव॥ २०॥
verses.m: “It may also be pointed out by you unreservedly what should be done by me. All your desire will be accomplished even as all seeds sown in a good field during the rains bear fruit. (20)

verses.text:
मया च यदिदं वाक्यमभिमानात् समीरितम्।
तत्त्वया हरिशार्दूल तत्त्वमित्युपधार्यताम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “The assurance (to the effect that I shall kill Vālī) that has been duly given by me out of self-confidence should be taken by you to be a bare truth, O tiger among monkeys! (21)

verses.text:
अनृतं नोक्तपूर्वं मे न च वक्ष्ये कदाचन।
एतत्ते प्रतिजानामि सत्येनैव शपाम्यहम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Never before has a falsehood been uttered by me nor shall I ever utter it. I solemnly affirm this to you and swear by truth alone.” (22)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवो वानरैः सचिवैः सह।
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा प्रतिज्ञातं विशेषतः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Sugrīva alongwith his counsellors, who were all monkeys felt immensely delighted to hear the words of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), particularly the promise made by him. (23)

verses.text:
एवमेकान्तसम्पृक्तौ ततस्तौ नरवानरौ।
उभावन्योन्यसदृशं सुखं दुःखमभाषताम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: United thus in a lonely retreat, both the aforesaid friends, a human being and a monkey, thereupon spoke each about his joys and sorrows, which were akin to those of the other. (24)

verses.text:
महानुभावस्य वचो निशम्य
हरिर्नृपाणामधिपस्य तस्य।
कृतं स मेने हरिवीरमुख्य-
स्तदा च कार्यं हृदयेन विद्वान्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Hearing the assurance of Śrī Rāma, the king of kings, who was possessed of great might, the wise Sugrīva, the foremost of monkey heroes, forthwith took his object mentally accomplished. (25)

verses.text:
परितुष्टस्तु सुग्रीवस्तेन वाक्येन हर्षितः।
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रजं शूरमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Much gratified at the aforesaid assurance of Śrī Rāma, Sugrīva for his part joyfully submitted as follows to the gallant eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa : (1)

verses.text:
सर्वथाहमनुग्राह्यो देवतानां न संशयः।
उपपन्नो गुणोपेतः सखा यस्य भवान् मम॥ २॥
verses.m: “I am undoubtedly deserving in everyway of the grace of gods in that you, who are rich in all natural endowments and endowed with virtues, are my friend. (2)

verses.text:
शक्यं खलु भवेद् राम सहायेन त्वयानघ।
सुरराज्यमपि प्राप्तुं स्वराज्यं किमुत प्रभो॥ ३॥
verses.m: “With you as my ally, O sinless Rāma, it should indeed be possible for me to secure even the kingdom of gods, to say nothing of regaining my own lost sovereignty, O lord ! (3)

verses.text:
सोऽहं सभाज्यो बन्धूनां सुहृदां चैव राघव।
यस्याग्निसाक्षिकं मित्रं लब्धं राघववंशजम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “As such, O scion of Raghu, I deserve to be adored by my kinsmen and friends, in that a friend born in the line of Raghu has been secured by me with fire as a witness. (4)

verses.text:
अहमप्यनुरूपस्ते वयस्यो ज्ञास्यसे शनैः।
न तु वक्तुं समर्थोऽहं त्वयि आत्मगतान् गुणान्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “You will gradually come to know that I too am a friend worthy of you. I am, however, not able to make known to you the virtues inhering in me. (5)

verses.text:
महात्मनां तु भूयिष्ठं त्वद्विधानां कृतात्मनाम्।
निश्चला भवति प्रीतिर्धैर्यमात्मवतां वर॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The love of exalted souls like you, who have mastered their Self, is of course steady and their fortitude infinite, O jewel among masters of their Self ! (6)

verses.text:
रजतं वा सुवर्णं वा शुभान्याभरणानि च।
अविभक्तानि साधूनामवगच्छन्ति साधवः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Friends look upon their own silver or gold or even shining jewels as undivided with their friends. (7)

verses.text:
आढ्योवापि दरिद्रो वा दुःखितः सुखितोऽपि वा।
निर्दोषश्च सदोषश्च वयस्यः परमा गतिः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Rich or even poor, nay, afflicted or even happy, and faultless as well as full of faults, a friend is the supreme asylum to a friend. (8)

verses.text:
धनत्यागः सुखत्यागो देशत्यागोऽपि वानघ।
वयस्यार्थे प्रवर्तन्ते स्नेहं दृष्ट्वा तथाविधम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Renunciation of wealth, renunciation of comforts and renunciation even of one’s country follow in the interests of a friend on seeing love of a category evoking such a sacrifice, O sinless one !” (9)

verses.text:
तत् तथेत्यब्रवीद् रामः सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्।
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो लक्ष्म्या वासवस्येव धीमतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: In the presence of the wise Lakṣmaṇa, who vied with Indra in splendour, Śrī Rāma said to Sugrīva of pleasing aspect, “It is as you say.” (10)

verses.text:
ततो रामं स्थितं दृष्ट्वा लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।
सुग्रीवः सर्वतश्चक्षुर्वने लोलमपातयत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Seeing Śrī Rāma as well as Lakṣmaṇa, who was possessed of great strength, Sugrīva thereupon cast his restless eyes all around in the forest. (11)

verses.text:
स ददर्श ततः सालमविदूरे हरीश्वरः।
सुपुष्पमीषत्पत्राढ्यं भ्रमरैरुपशोभितम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, presently sighted not far from that spot a sal tree of charming flowers, nay, clothed with a scanty foliage and adorned with black bees. (12)

verses.text:
तस्यैकां पर्णबहुलां शाखां भङ्क्त्वा सुशोभिताम्।
रामस्यास्तीर्य सुग्रीवो निषसाद सराघवः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Breaking for the sake of Śrī Rāma one most lovely bough, thick with leaves, off that tree and laying it on the ground, Sugrīva sat on it alongwith Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu). (13)

verses.text:
तावासीनौ ततो दृष्ट्वा हनूमानपि लक्ष्मणम्।
शालशाखां समुत्पाट्य विनीतमुपवेशयत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Seeing them seated and duly tearing one more bough off the sal tree, Hanumān prevailed on the meek Lakṣmaṇa too to sit on it. (14)

verses.text:
सुखोपविष्टं रामं तु प्रसन्नमुदधिं यथा।
सालपुष्पावसंकीर्णे तस्मिन् गिरिवरोत्तमे॥ १५॥
ततः प्रहृष्टः सुग्रीवः श्लक्ष्णया शुभया गिरा।
उवाच प्रणयाद् रामं हर्षव्याकुलिताक्षरम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: Then out of affection Sugrīva for his part most joyfully submitted in a soft and attractive tone and in words rendered indistinct through joy to Śrī Rāma, the delighter of all, comfortably seated and calm like an unruffled ocean on that jewel among the best of mountains, which was strewn with blossoms of sal. (15-16)

verses.text:
अहं विनिकृतो भ्रात्रा चराम्येष भयार्दितः।
ऋष्यमूकं गिरिवरं हृतभार्यः सुदुःखितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Exiled by my elder brother, Vālī, and deprived of my spouse, I range on this Ṛṣyamūka, the best of mountains, stricken with fear and sore afflicted. (17)

verses.text:
सोऽहं त्रस्तो भये मग्नो वने सम्भ्रान्तचेतनः।
वालिना निकृतो भ्रात्रा कृतवैरश्च राघव॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Having been exiled and antagonized by my elder brother, Vālī, O scion of Raghu, I dwell in this forest alarmed and submerged in fear, my mind being utterly confused. (18)

verses.text:
वालिनो मे भयार्तस्य सर्वलोकाभयंकर।
ममापि त्वमनाथस्य प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि॥ १९॥
verses.m: “You ought to show favour to me as well, forlorn as I am and stricken with fear from Vālī, O prince ridding all people of fear !” (19)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्मवत्सलः।
प्रत्युवाच स काकुत्स्थः सुग्रीवं प्रहसन्निव॥ २०॥
verses.m: Requested thus by Sugrīva, the glorious Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kakutstha, for his part, who knew what is right and was fond of righteousness, replied to Sugrīva as follows, as though heartily laughing : (20)

verses.text:
उपकारफलं मित्रमपकारोऽरिलक्षणम्।
अद्यैव तं वधिष्यामि तव भार्यापहारिणम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Service is the fruit yielded by a friend and an enemy is known by disservice (that he renders). I will this very day dispose of Vālī, who has wrested your spouse. (21)

verses.text:
इमे हि मे महाभाग पत्रिणस्तिग्मतेजसः।
कार्तिकेयवनोद्भूताः शरा हेमविभूषिताः॥ २२॥
कङ्कपत्रपरिच्छन्ना महेन्द्राशनिसंनिभाः।
सुपर्वाणः सुतीक्ष्णाग्राः सरोषा भुजगा इव॥ २३॥
verses.m: “Here indeed are my winged shafts of dazzling brilliance sprung from a thicket of reeds (the birth-place of Lord Skanda), decked with gold and adorned with the feathers of buzzards, endowed with smooth joints and exceptionally sharp points, nay, resembling the great Indra’s thunderbolt and looking like angry serpents, O highly blessed one ! (22-23)

verses.text:
वालिसंज्ञममित्रं ते भ्रातरं कृतकिल्बिषम्।
शरैर्विनिहतं पश्य विकीर्णमिव पर्वतम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “See your hostile brother, known by the name of Vālī, who has done you wrong, struck down with arrows like a cleft mountain.” (24)

verses.text:
राघवस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवो वाहिनीपतिः।
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे साधु साध्विति चाब्रवीत्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Sugrīva, who was the leader of an army, derived incomparable joy on hearing the assurance of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) and said, “Excellent ! Bravo !! (25)

verses.text:
राम शोकाभिभूतोऽहं शोकार्तानां भवान् गतिः।
वयस्य इति कृत्वा हि त्वय्यहं परिदेवये॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I am overwhelmed with grief, while you are the refuge of those stricken with grief. I ventilate my grievance to you, knowing you as I do to be my friend. (26)

verses.text:
त्वं हि पाणिप्रदानेन वयस्यो मेऽग्निसाक्षिकम्।
कृतः प्राणैर्बहुमतः सत्येन च शपाम्यहम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “By offering my hand of friendship to you, we have been made friends, with fire as a witness and you are more highly esteemed than my very life. I swear by truth. (27)

verses.text:
वयस्य इति कृत्वा च विस्रब्धः प्रवदाम्यहम्।
दुःखमन्तर्गतं तन्मे मनो हरति नित्यशः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Nay, recognizing you to be my friend, I have revealed to you in confidence the sorrow residing in my heart, which distracts my mind from day to day.” (28)

verses.text:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं बाष्पदूषितलोचनः।
बाष्पदूषितया वाचा नोच्चैः शक्नोति भाषितुम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: Having spoken words to the extent noted above, his eyes bedimmed with tears, he could not speak aloud any more due to his voice getting choked with tears. (29)

verses.text:
बाष्पवेगं तु सहसा नदीवेगमिवागतम्।
धारयामास धैर्येण सुग्रीवो रामसंनिधौ॥ ३०॥
verses.m: By recourse to firmness in the presence of Śrī Rāma, Sugrīva, however, controlled the stream of his tears that had precipitately welled up like a river in spate. (30)

verses.text:
स निगृह्य तु तं बाष्पं प्रमृज्य नयने शुभे।
विनिःश्वस्य च तेजस्वी राघवं पुनरूचिवान्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Restraining those tears, nay, wiping his charming eyes and drawing a deep breath, the strong-willed monkey for his part submitted to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) once more as follows : (31)

verses.text:
पुराहं वालिना राम राज्यात् स्वादवरोपितः।
परुषाणि च संश्राव्य निर्धूतोऽस्मि बलीयसा॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “In the past, O Rāma, I was deposed by Vālī from my throne (which I had ascended under his instruction and with his concurrence) and, addressing pungent words, was exiled by him, mightier as he was. (32)

verses.text:
हृता भार्या च मे तेन प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी।
सुहृदश्च मदीया ये संयता बन्धनेषु ते॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “My spouse too, who was more precious than my very life, was wrested (from me) by him and those who were my near and dear ones were bound with chains. (33)

verses.text:
यत्नवांश्च स दुष्टात्मा मद्विनाशाय राघव।
बहुशस्तप्रयुक्ताश्च वानरा निहता मया॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Nay, that malevolent fellow is endeavouring to bring about my destruction, O scion of Raghu ! Monkeys employed by him for this purpose on many occasions have been killed by me. (34)

verses.text:
शङ्कया त्वेतयाहं च दृष्ट्वा त्वामपि राघव।
नोपसर्पाम्यहं भीतो भये सर्वे हि बिभ्यति॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “Nay, dismayed through this fear alone I could not have courage to approach you even on seeing you, O scion of Raghu; for in the face of danger all get nervous. (35)

verses.text:
केवलं हि सहाया मे हनुमत्प्रमुखास्त्विमे।
अतोऽहं धारयाम्यद्य प्राणान् कृच्छ्रगतोऽपि सन्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “These monkeys with Hanumān as their leader for their part have in fact been my only companions. Hence I am able to preserve my life today, though reduced to straits. (36)

verses.text:
एते हि कपयः स्निग्धा मां रक्षन्ति समन्ततः।
सह गच्छन्ति गन्तव्ये नित्यं तिष्ठन्ति चास्थिते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “These loving monkeys actually protect me on all sides. They accompany me wherever I have to go and ever remain by my side when I have to stay. (37)

verses.text:
संक्षेपस्त्वेष मे राम किमुक्त्वा विस्तरं हि ते।
स मे ज्येष्ठो रिपुर्भ्राता वाली विश्रुतपौरुषः॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “This in brief is all my story, O Rāma! Of what use is it to give you details? Vālī, that hostile elder brother of mine, is well-known for his valour. (38)

verses.text:
तद्विनाशेऽपि मे दुःखं प्रमृष्टं स्यादनन्तरम्।
सुखं मे जीवितं चैव तद्विनाशनिबन्धनम्॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “My suffering can be immediately wiped out only after his destruction. My happiness, nay, my life itself hinges on his destruction. (39)

verses.text:
एष मे राम शोकान्तः शोकार्तेन निवेदितः।
दुःखितः सुखितो वापि सख्युर्नित्यं सखा गतिः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “In this way has the means of ending my suffering been submitted by me, stricken as I am with grief, O Rāma ! Afflicted or happy, a friend alone is the refuge of a friend at any time.” (40)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वैतच्च वचो रामः सुग्रीवमिदमब्रवीत्।
किं निमित्तमभूद् वैरं श्रोतुमिच्छामि तत्त्वतः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: Hearing this submission, Śrī Rāma once more spoke as follows to Sugrīva : “What was the occasion for Vālī’s hostility (with you)? I wish to hear this truly. (41)

verses.text:
सुखं हि कारणं श्रुत्वा वैरस्य तव वानर।
आनन्तर्याद् विधास्यामि सम्प्रधार्य बलाबलम्॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “After duly ascertaining the relative strength and weakness of you both, on hearing the cause of this antagonism, O monkey, I shall forthwith provide relief to you (in the shape of Vālīs destruction). (42)

verses.text:
बलवान् हि ममामर्षः श्रुत्वा त्वामवमानितम्।
वर्धते हृदयोत्कम्पी प्रावृड्वेग इवाम्भसः॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Like the onrush of water (flowing in streams) during the monsoon, my indignation, which is already strong and shakes my heart, grows hearing about your being insulted. (43)

verses.text:
हृष्टः कथय विस्रब्धो यावदारोप्यते धनुः।
सृष्टश्च हि मया बाणो निरस्तश्च रिपुस्तव॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “Speak joyfully and with confidence till the bow is strung by me. Your adversary (Vālī) will be killed as soon as an arrow is discharged by me.” (44)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्तु सुग्रीवः काकुत्स्थेन महात्मना।
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः॥ ४५॥
verses.m: Reassured in these words by the high-souled Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha), Sugrīva for his part derived incomparable joy alongwith the four monkeys (who accompanied him). (45)

verses.text:
ततः प्रहृष्टवदनः सुग्रीवो लक्ष्मणाग्रजे।
वैरस्य कारणं तत्त्वमाख्यातुमुपचक्रमे॥ ४६॥
verses.m: With his face extremely delighted, Sugrīva thereupon proceeded to relate to Śrī Rāma (the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa) the cause of their hostility, which constituted the reality. (46)

verses.text:
वाली नाम मम भ्राता ज्येष्ठः शत्रुनिषूदनः।
पितुर्बहुमतो नित्यं मम चापि तथा पुरा॥ १॥
verses.m: “Vālī by name is my elder brother, capable of exterminating his foes. He was held in great esteem by our father and likewise made much of by me too in the past. (1)

verses.text:
पितर्युपरते तस्मिन् ज्येष्ठोऽयमिति मन्त्रिभिः।
कपीनामीश्वरो राज्ये कृतः परमसम्मतः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Our aforesaid father having died, Vālī, who was supremely honoured by all, was installed by the ministers on the throne of Kiṣkindhā as the ruler of monkeys, on the ground of his being the elder prince. (2)

verses.text:
राज्यं प्रशासतस्तस्य पितृपैतामहं महत्।
अहं सर्वेषु कालेषु प्रणतः प्रेष्यवत् स्थितः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “While he justly ruled over his big ancestral kingdom, I remained submissive to him at all times and stood like his servant. (3)

verses.text:
मायावी नाम तेजस्वी पूर्वजो दुन्दुभेः सुतः।
तेन तस्य महद्वैरं वालिनः स्त्रीकृतं पुरा॥ ४॥
verses.m: “There was a glorious son of the demon Maya, elder than Dundubhi. The said Vālī formerly had a bitter enmity with him on account of a woman. (4)

verses.text:
स तु सुप्ते जने रात्रौ किष्किन्धाद्वारमागतः।
नर्दति स्म सुसंरब्धो वालिनं चाह्वयद् रणे॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Arrived at the gates of Kiṣkindhā at dead of night, when people were asleep, he for his part thundered and challenged Vālī to a duel, highly enraged as he was. (5)

verses.text:
प्रसुप्तस्तु मम भ्राता नर्दतो भैरवस्वनम्।
श्रुत्वा न ममृषे वाली निष्पपात जवात् तदा॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Hearing the frightful roar of the thundering Māyāvī, my brother, Vālī, who was fast asleep, did not brook his challenge and briskly sallied forth at once. (6)

verses.text:
स तु वै निःसृतः क्रोधात् तं हन्तुमसुरोत्तमम्।
वार्यमाणस्ततः स्त्रीभिर्मया च प्रणतात्मना॥ ७॥
verses.m: Emerged in fury to kill Māyāvī, the foremost of demons, Vālī for his part was actually restrained from that daring act by the women of his gynaeceum as well as by me, whose body was bent low with submission. (7)

verses.text:
स तु निर्धूय सर्वान् नो निर्जगाम महाबलः।
ततोऽहमपि सौहार्दान्निःसृतो वालिना सह॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Repelling us all, Vālī, however, who was possessed of extraordinary might, went forth. Out of affection I too thereupon sallied forth with Vālī. (8)

verses.text:
स तु मे भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा मां च दूरादवस्थितम्।
असुरो जातसंत्रासः प्रदुद्राव तदा भृशम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Seized with terror to see from a distance my elder brother, Vālī, stationed in a firm position to give battle, as well as myself, Māyāvī forthwith ran quickly for life. (9)

verses.text:
तस्मिन् द्रवति संत्रस्ते ह्यावां द्रुततरं गतौ।
प्रकाशोऽपि कृतो मार्गश्चन्द्रेणोद्गच्छता तदा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “While he was fleeing alarmed for life, we two followed faster; the road was illumined at that time by the moon appearing in the horizon. (10)

verses.text:
स तृणैरावृतं दुर्गं धरण्या विवरं महत्।
प्रविवेशासुरो वेगादावामासाद्य विष्ठितौ॥ ११॥
verses.m: “The aforesaid demon entered with expedition a large hole in the earth, which was covered with grass and hence difficult of access; while we two stood rooted on reaching the spot. (11)

verses.text:
तं प्रविष्टं रिपुं दृष्ट्वा बिलं रोषवशं गतः।
मामुवाच ततो वाली वचनं क्षुभितेन्द्रियः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Fallen a prey to anger on seeing his aforesaid adversary having penetrated deep into a hole, Vālī thereupon spoke to me as follows, his mind being agitated : (12)

verses.text:
इह तिष्ठाद्य सुग्रीव बिलद्वारि समाहितः।
यावदत्र प्रविश्याहं निहन्मि समरे रिपुम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Remain alert at the mouth of this hole today, O Sugrīva, till I, penetrating deep into the hole, make short work of my enemy in the course of a duel.’ (13)

verses.text:
मया त्वेतद् वचः श्रुत्वा याचितः स परंतपः।
शापयित्वा च मां पद्भ्यां प्रविवेश बिलं ततः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Though implored by me to take myself alongwith him on hearing this command, Vālī, for his part, the scorcher of his foes, thereupon penetrated deep into the hole, binding me on oath in the name of his own person to remain outside. (14)

verses.text:
तस्य प्रविष्टस्य बिलं साग्रः संवत्सरो गतः।
स्थितस्य च बिलद्वारि स कालो व्यत्यवर्तत॥ १५॥
verses.m: “More than a year slipped away since he penetrated deep into the hole and the same period elapsed even as I remained stationed at the mouth of the hole. (15)

verses.text:
अहं तु नष्टं तं ज्ञात्वा स्नेहादागतसम्भ्रमः।
भ्रातरं न प्रपश्यामि पापशङ्कि च मे मनः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Since I did not perceive my elder brother with my own eyes all these long months, my mind began to apprehend his death. Nay, concluding him to have been killed by the demon, I for my part was overcome by a feeling of misgiving through affection. (16)

verses.text:
अथ दीर्घस्य कालस्य बिलात् तस्माद् विनिःसृतम्।
सफेनं रुधिरं दृष्ट्वा ततोऽहं भृशदुःखितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Then, on seeing after a long time blood mixed with foam emerged from the aforesaid hole, I felt extremely distressed because of that. (17)

verses.text:
नर्दतामसुराणां च ध्वनिर्मे श्रोत्रमागतः।
न रतस्य च संग्रामे क्रोशतोऽपि स्वनो गुरोः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “The yell of thundering demons too reached my ears, while the noise of my elder brother, even though he was roaring while engaged in the encounter, did not fall on my ears. (18)

verses.text:
अहं त्ववगतो बुद्ध्या चिह्नैस्तैर्भातरं हतम्।
पिधाय च बिलद्वारं शिलया गिरिमात्रया॥ १९॥
शोकार्तश्चोदकं कृत्वा किष्किन्धामागतः सखे।
गूहमानस्य मे तत् त्वं यत्नतो मन्त्रिभिः श्रुतम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “By recourse to reason on the strength of the aforesaid indications, I, for my part, concluded my elder brother to have been killed. Nay, blocking up the mouth of the hole with a rock as big as a hillock, and offering water to the spirit of the deceased, stricken as I was with grief, I returned to Kiṣkindhā, O friend ! Although I concealed the truth, the secret was learnt by the ministers with effort. (19-20)

verses.text:
ततोऽहं तैः समागम्य समेतैरभिषेचितः।
राज्यं प्रशासतस्तस्य न्यायतो मम राघव॥ २१॥
आजगाम रिपुं हत्वा दानवं स तु वानरः।
अभिषिक्तं तु मां दृष्ट्वा क्रोधात् संरक्तलोचनः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “Having met together and deliberated with one another, I was thereupon installed on the throne of Kiṣkindhā by the ministers in a body. Having got rid of his adversary, the demon (Māyāvī), the aforesaid monkey, my elder brother, Vālī, for his part came home while I was ruling his kingdom with justice, O scion of Raghu! Seeing me installed on the throne he had his eyes actually turned crimson due to anger. (21-22)

verses.text:
मदीयान् मन्त्रिणो बद्ध्वा परुषं वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
निग्रहे च समर्थस्य तं पापं प्रति राघव॥ २३॥
न प्रावर्तत मे बुद्धिर्भ्रातृगौरवयन्त्रिता।
हत्वा शत्रुं स मे भ्राता प्रविवेश पुरं तदा॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Nay, binding my ministers in chains, he spoke harsh words to them. Even though I was capable of restraining that sinful monkey, Vālī, O scion of Raghu, my mind, which was weighed down by a feeling of reverence for my elder brother, did not feel inclined to do so. Having killed his adversary, the said brother of mine forthwith entered the capital in due course. (23-24)

verses.text:
मानयंस्तं महात्मानं यथावच्चाभिवादयम्।
उक्ताश्च नाशिषस्तेन प्रहृष्टेनान्तरात्मना॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Holding as I did the high-minded Vālī in esteem, I greeted him with due reverence: benedictions, however, were not pronounced by him with a highly rejoiced mind. (25)

verses.text:
नत्वा पादावहं तस्य मुकुटेनास्पृशं प्रभो।
अपि वाली मम क्रोधान्न प्रसादं चकार सः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Bowing down to him I touched his feet with my crown, O lord ! Due to anger, however, the said Vālī did not relent.” (26)

verses.text:
ततः क्रोधसमाविष्टं संरब्धं तमुपागतम्।
अहं प्रसादयांचक्रे भ्रातरं हितकाम्यया॥ १॥
verses.m: “With intent to do him good I then sought to placate in the following words my elder brother Vālī, who came possessed of anger and was excited : (1)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्यासि कुशली प्राप्तो निहतश्च त्वया रिपुः।
अनाथस्य हि मे नाथस्त्वमेकोऽनाथनन्दन॥ २॥
verses.m: “ ‘By good luck you have returned home safe and the enemy has been killed by you. You are my only protector, protectorless as I was, O the delight of the forlorn ! (2)

verses.text:
इदं बहुशलाकं ते पूर्णचन्द्रमिवोदितम्।
छत्रं सवालव्यजनं प्रतीच्छस्व मया धृतम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Here is your canopy supported on many ribs and resembling the full moon appeared above horizon, held by me alongwith a pair of whisks; pray, accept it and allow it to be held over your head and the whisks to be waved on both sides of you. (3)

verses.text:
आर्तस्तत्र बिलद्वारि स्थितः संवत्सरं नृप।
दृष्ट्वा च शोणितं द्वारि बिलाच्चापि समुत्थितम्॥ ४॥
शोकसंविग्नहृदयो भृशं व्याकुलितेन्द्रियः।
अपिधाय बिलद्वारं शैलशृङ्गेण तत् तदा॥ ५॥
तस्माद् देशादपाक्रम्य किष्किन्धां प्राविशं पुनः।
विषादात्त्विह मां दृष्ट्वा पौरैर्मन्त्रिभिरेव च॥ ६॥
अभिषिक्तो न कामेन तन्मे क्षन्तुं त्वमर्हसि।
त्वमेव राजा मानार्हः सदा चाहं यथा पुरा॥ ७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having waited at the mouth of that hole for a full year, O monarch, even though I felt distressed over your entry into the hole, I felt agitated at heart through grief to see blood welled up from the hole and collected at its mouth, my mind being distracted. Closing the aforesaid mouth of the hole with the top of a cliff and withdrawing from that area, I then entered Kiṣkindhā again through despondency. Seeing me forlorn, without you for a year, I, for my part, was installed on the throne by the citizens as well as the ministers and not through covetousness on my part. You ought, therefore, to forgive the aforesaid offence on my part, unintentional as it was. You alone are the sovereign deserving of honour, while I am ever your servant as heretofore. (4—7)

verses.text:
राजभावे नियोगोऽयं मम त्वद्विरहात् कृतः।
सामात्यपौरनगरं स्थितं निहतकण्टकम्॥ ८॥
न्यासभूतमिदं राज्यं तव निर्यातयाम्यहम्।
मा च रोषं कृथाः सौम्य मम शत्रुनिषूदन॥ ९॥
verses.m: “ ‘This installation of mine on the throne of Kiṣkindhā was brought about due to your absence. I hereby restore to you your kingdom including ministers, citizens and the city of Kiṣkindhā, which vested in me as a sacred trust and which has been rid of all thorns. Therefore, O gentle brother do not give vent to anger towards me, O exterminator of foes ! (8-9)

verses.text:
याचे त्वां शिरसा राजन् मया बद्धोऽयमञ्जलिः।
बलादस्मिन् समागम्य मन्त्रिभिः पुरवासिभिः॥ १०॥
राजभावे नियुक्तोऽहं शून्यदेशजिगीषया।
स्निग्धमेवं ब्रुवाणं मां स विनिर्भर्त्स्य वानरः॥ ११॥
धिक्त्वामिति च मामुक्त्वा बहु तत्तदुवाच ह।
प्रकृतीश्च समानीय मन्त्रिणश्चैव सम्मतान्॥ १२॥
मामाह सुहृदां मध्ये वाक्यं परमगर्हितम्।
विदितं वो मया रात्रौ मायावी स महासुरः॥ १३॥
मां समाह्वयत क्रुद्धो युद्धाकांक्षी तदा पुरा।
तस्य तद् भाषितं श्रुत्वा निःसृतोऽहं नृपालयात्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘I solicit you, O sovereign, with my head bent low to get pleased with me and here stand my palms joined together in supplication. I was forcibly installed on this throne by your ministers and the citizens in a body lest a rulerless state should tempt others to conquer it.’ “Censuring me, even though I spoke such loving words, and saying ‘Fie upon you !’ the said monkey, Vālī, actually uttered many abusive words. Nay, calling together (accredited representatives of) the people as well as ministers who were held in high esteem, he spoke to me most contemptible words in the midst of my near and dear ones as follows : “ ‘It is known to you how that mighty demon, Māyāvī, who sought a trial of arms with me, angrily challenged me to a duel the other day at dead of night. Hearing his aforesaid challenge, I sallied forth from my royal residence. (10—14)

verses.text:
अनुयातश्च मां तूर्णमयं भ्राता सुदारुणः।
स तु दृष्ट्वैव मां रात्रौ सद्वितीयं महाबलः॥ १५॥
प्राद्रवद् भयसंत्रस्तो वीक्ष्यावां समुपागतौ।
अभिद्रुतस्तु वेगेन विवेश स महाबिलम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘This most cruel younger brother of mine too followed me apace. The moment the demon saw me followed by another at night, the fellow, even though possessed of great might, fled for life, distracted as he was through fear. Nay, put to flight with greater speed on perceiving us arrived very near, he entered a big hole with impetuosity. (15-16)

verses.text:
तं प्रविष्टं विदित्वा तु सुघोरं सुमहद्बिलम्।
अयमुक्तोऽथ मे भ्राता मया तु क्रूरदर्शनः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘Knowing him to have entered a most fearful and very large hole, this younger brother of mine of cruel aspect for his part was then spoken to by me as follows : (17)

verses.text:
अहत्वा नास्ति मे शक्तिः प्रतिगन्तुमितः पुरीम्।
बिलद्वारि प्रतीक्ष त्वं यावदेनं निहन्म्यहम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Power is lacking in me to return from this place to the city of Kiṣkindhā without disposing of this demon. Therefore, wait you at the mouth of the gate till I get rid of him. (18)

verses.text:
स्थितोऽयमिति मत्वाहं प्रविष्टस्तु दुरासदम्।
तं मे मार्गयतस्तत्र गतः संवत्सरस्तदा॥ १९॥
स तु दृष्टो मया शत्रुरनिर्वेदाद् भयावहः।
निहतश्च मया सद्यः स सर्वैः सह बन्धुभिः॥ २०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Presuming that my brother will remain standing there, I for my part penetrated deep into the cave, which was difficult of access. While I remained hunting the demon in that cave a whole year rolled by. Then that dreadful enemy for his part was seen by me without causing any despondency (in me because of his not having been seen for a whole year) and the demon was killed by me then and there with all his kinsmen. (19-20)

verses.text:
तस्यास्यात्तु प्रवृत्तेन रुधिरौघेण तद्बिलम्।
पूर्णमासीद् दुराक्रामं स्तनतस्तस्य भूतले॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘While he was thundering in the bowels of the earth, the said cave was for its part filled with a stream of blood which gushed forth from his mouth and consequently rendered difficult to pass through. (21)

verses.text:
सूदयित्वा तु तं शत्रुं विकान्तं तमहं सुखम्।
निष्क्रामं नैव पश्यामि बिलस्य पिहितं मुखम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having killed with ease my powerful enemy, the notorious Māyāvī, I would not find my way out of the cave as its entrance was closed. (22)

verses.text:
विक्रोशमानस्य तु मे सुग्रीवेति पुनः पुनः।
यतः प्रतिवचो नास्ति ततोऽहं भृशदुःखितः॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Since no response whatever came from outside even though I cried out loudly ‘O Sugrīva ! again and again, hence I felt sore afflicted. (23)

verses.text:
पादप्रहारैस्तु मया बहुभिः परिपातितम्।
ततोऽहं तेन निष्क्रम्य पथा पुरमुपागतः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘The rock was, however, pushed back by me with many a kick. Emerging through that outlet I then returned to the city. (24)

verses.text:
तत्रानेनास्मि संरुद्धो राज्यं मृगयताऽऽत्मनः।
सुग्रीवेण नृशंसेन विस्मृत्य भ्रातृसौहृदम्॥ २५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Disregarding brotherly affection, I was thus shut up in that cave by this cruel Sugrīva, who sought rulership for himself.’ (25)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु मां तत्र वस्त्रेणैकेन वानरः।
तदा निर्वासयामास वाली विगतसाध्वसः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Saying so, the monkey, Vālī, for his part, from whom all sense of shame had departed, banished me then and there with a single piece of cloth, stripping me of all my possessions. (26)

verses.text:
तेनाहमपविद्धश्च हृतदारश्च राघव।
तद्भयाच्च महीं सर्वां क्रान्तवान् सवनार्णवाम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Expelled by him and deprived of my spouse too, O scion of Raghu, I ranged the whole earth with its forests and oceans for fear of him. (27)

verses.text:
ऋष्यमूकं गिरिवरं भार्याहरणदुःखितः।
प्रविष्टोऽस्मि दुराधर्षं वालिनः कारणान्तरे॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Distressed by the usurpation of my consort, I have retired to Ṛṣyamūka, the foremost of mountains, which is difficult of access for Vālī due to another reason (the imprecation uttered by Sage Mataṅga). (28)

verses.text:
एतत्ते सर्वमाख्यातं वैरानुकथनं महत्।
अनागसा मया प्राप्तं व्यसनं पश्य राघव॥ २९॥
verses.m: “In this way the whole momentous story of my hostility with Vālī has been narrated to you by me. See for yourself, O scion of Raghu, the misfortune met with by me, innocent though I am. (29)

verses.text:
वालिनश्च भयात् तस्य सर्वलोकभयापह।
कर्तुमर्हसि मे वीर प्रसादं तस्य निग्रहात्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Nay, you ought to bring immunity to me, situated as I am, from the threat of Vālī through his subjugation, O gallant prince, the dispeller of the fear of all the worlds !” (30)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः स तेजस्वी धर्मज्ञो धर्मसंहितम्।
वचनं वक्तुमारेभे सुग्रीवं प्रहसन्निव॥ ३१॥
verses.m: Requested as aforesaid, the glorious Śrī Rāma, who knew what is right, proceeded to address the following words, conformable to righteousness, to Sugrīva as though laughing heartily : (31)

verses.text:
अमोघाः सूर्यसंकाशा निशिता मे शरा इमे।
तस्मिन् वालिनि दुर्वृत्ते पतिष्यन्ति रुषान्विताः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Full of wrath these unfailing sharp arrows of mine, brilliant as the sun, will descend on that Vālī of immoral conduct. (32)

verses.text:
यावत् तं नहि पश्येयं तव भार्यापहारिणम्।
तावत् स जीवेत् पापात्मा वाली चारित्रदूषकः॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “The aforesaid Vālī, whose mind is set on sin and who has transgressed morality, will survive only till I do not behold that usurper of your spouse. (33)

verses.text:
आत्मानुमानात् पश्यामि मग्नस्त्वं शोकसागरे।
त्वामहं तारयिष्यामि बाढं प्राप्स्यसि पुष्कलम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Through inference based on my own example I can see that you are plunged in an ocean of grief. I shall accordingly help you to cross it and you will surely be able to regain all that you have lost, viz., your consort and sovereignty, too.” (34)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा हर्षपौरुषवर्धनम्।
सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतः सुमहद्वाक्यमब्रवीत्॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Supremely rejoiced to hear the aforesaid assurance of Śrī Rāma, which intensified his joy and courage, Sugrīva gave a most momentous reply. (35)

verses.text:
रामस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा हर्षपौरुषवर्धनम्।
सुग्रीवः पूजयांचक्रे राघवं प्रशशंस च॥ १॥
verses.m: Hearing the assurance of Śrī Rāma, that enhanced his joy and courage, Sugrīva welcomed it and applauded him in the following words : (1)

verses.text:
असंशयं प्रज्वलितैस्तीक्ष्णैर्मर्मातिगैः शरैः।
त्वं दहेः कुपितो लोकान् युगान्त इव भास्करः॥ २॥
verses.m: “Like the sun at the end of creation, you can doubtless consume, when provoked, all the worlds with your fiery and pointed arrows that are capable of piercing the vital parts. (2)

verses.text:
वालिनः पौरुषं यत्तद् यच्च वीर्यं धृतिश्च या।
तन्ममैकमनाः श्रुत्वा विधत्स्व यदनन्तरम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Hearing from my lips with a concentrated mind of the prowess as well as of the valour and fortitude that exist in Vālī, do what should be done next. (3)

verses.text:
समुद्रात् पश्चिमात् पूर्वं दक्षिणादपि चोत्तरम्।
क्रामत्यनुदिते सूर्ये वाली व्यपगतक्लमः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Getting up at the close of night Vālī strides from the western to the eastern and (moving to the south) from the southern to the northern ocean too, fatigue having altogether departed from him. (4)

verses.text:
अग्राण्यारुह्य शैलानां शिखराणि महान्त्यपि।
ऊर्ध्वमुत्पात्य तरसा प्रतिगृह्णाति वीर्यवान्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Climbing up the tops of mountains, and tossing up even gigantic peaks with force, the mighty Vālī catches them up.(5)

verses.text:
बहवः सारवन्तश्च वनेषु विविधा द्रुमाः।
वालिना तरसा भग्ना बलं प्रथयताऽऽत्मनः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Nay, numerous solid trees of every description in the forests were forcibly snapped by Vālī while demonstrating his might. (6)

verses.text:
महिषो दुन्दुभिर्नाम कैलासशिखरप्रभः।
बलं नागसहस्रस्य धारयामास वीर्यवान्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “A mighty demon appearing in the form of a buffalo, Dundubhi by name, who shone like the peak of Kailāsa, bore the strength of a thousand elephants. (7)

verses.text:
स वीर्योत्सेकदुष्टात्मा वरदानेन मोहितः।
जगाम स महाकायः समुद्रं सरितां पतिम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Blinded by a boon, that gigantic buffalo, whose mind had been perverted by pride of strength, approached Ocean, the lord of rivers. (8)

verses.text:
ऊर्मिमन्तमतिक्रम्य सागरं रत्नसंचयम्।
मम युद्धं प्रयच्छेति तमुवाच महार्णवम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Disdaining the turbulent sea, the storehouse of jewels, he said to the celebrated Ocean, ‘Give battle to me !’ (9)

verses.text:
ततः समुद्रो धर्मात्मा समुत्थाय महाबलः।
अब्रवीद् वचनं राजन्नसुरं कालचोदितम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: Duly rising (as a mark of respect), the very mighty Ocean, whose mind was set on righteousness, then replied as follows to the demon, who was impelled by the Time-Spirit : (10)

verses.text:
समर्थो नास्मि ते दातुं युद्धं युद्धविशारद।
श्रूयतां त्वभिधास्यामि यस्ते युद्धं प्रदास्यति॥ ११॥
verses.m: “ ‘I am not competent to give battle to you, O demon skilled in warfare! Listen, I will presently name him who will give battle to you. (11)

verses.text:
शैलराजो महारण्ये तपस्विशरणं परम्।
शंकरश्वशुरो नाम्ना हिमवानिति विश्रुतः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘There exists in a large forest the lord of mountains, Himavān by name, the supreme resort of ascetics and the far-famed father-in-law of Lord Śiva. (12)

verses.text:
महाप्रस्रवणोपेतो बहुकन्दरनिर्झरः।
स समर्थस्तव प्रीतिमतुलां कर्तुमर्हति॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Adorned with big waterfalls and comprising numerous caves and cascades, he is powerful and ought to render incomparable satisfaction to you through his skill in warfare. (13)

verses.text:
तं भीतमिति विज्ञाय समुद्रमसुरोत्तमः।
हिमवद्वनमागम्य शरश्चापादिव च्युतः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Concluding Ocean to be afraid of himself, Dundubhi (the foremost of demons) sped to the forest of Himavān like an arrow shot from a bow. (14)

verses.text:
ततस्तस्य गिरेः श्वेता गजेन्द्रप्रतिमाः शिलाः।
चिक्षेप बहुधा भूमौ दुन्दुभिर्विननाद च॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Then he hurled to the ground in a large number white cliffs of that mountain, resembling lordly elephants, and loudly roared. (15)

verses.text:
ततः श्वेताम्बुदाकारः सौम्यः प्रीतिकराकृतिः।
हिमवानब्रवीद् वाक्यं स्व एव शिखरे स्थितः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Remaining established on his own summit, the gentle Himavān, who looked like a white cloud and wore a pleasing aspect, spoke as follows : (16)

verses.text:
क्लेष्टुमर्हसि मां न त्वं दुन्दुभे धर्मवत्सल।
रणकर्मस्वकुशलस्तपस्विशरणो ह्यहम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘You ought not to pester me, O Dundubhi, who are fond of righteousness. I am not adept in warfare, the resort as I am of ascetics.’ (17)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा गिरिराजस्य धीमतः।
उवाच दुन्दुभिर्वाक्यं क्रोधात् संरक्तलोचनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid reply of the wise king of mountains, Dundubhi spoke as follows, his eyes turned crimson through anger : (18)

verses.text:
यदि युद्धेऽसमर्थस्त्वं मद्भयाद् वा निरुद्यमः।
तमाचक्ष्व प्रदद्यान्मे यो हि युद्धं युयुत्सतः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘If you are incapable of an encounter (with me) or are inactive through fear of me, name him who may actually give battle to me in earnest, eager as I am to fight.’(19)

verses.text:
हिमवानब्रवीद् वाक्यं श्रुत्वा वाक्यविशारदः।
अनुक्तपूर्वं धर्मात्मा क्रोधात् तमसुरोत्तमम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Hearing this, Himavān, who was an adept in expression and whose mind was set on virtue, angrily spoke as follows to Dundubhi the foremost of demons, to whom the name of a rival had not been mentioned before : (20)

verses.text:
वाली नाम महाप्राज्ञ शक्रपुत्रः प्रतापवान्।
अध्यास्ते वानरः श्रीमान् किष्किन्धामतुलप्रभाम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “ ‘A glorious and mighty monkey, Vālī by name, son of Indra (the ruler of gods), dwells in Kiṣkindhā, which is unequalled in splendour, O highly intelligent demon ! (21)

verses.text:
स समर्थो महाप्राज्ञस्तव युद्धविशारदः।
द्वन्द्वयुद्धं स दातुं ते नमुचेरिव वासवः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Highly intelligent and skilled in warfare, the aforesaid Vālī is capable of giving battle to you as Indra did to Namuci in the past. (22)

verses.text:
तं शीघ्रमभिगच्छ त्वं यदि युद्धमिहेच्छसि।
स हि दुर्मर्षणो नित्यं शूरः समरकर्मणि॥ २३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Approach him quickly if you seek an encounter with some rival on this earth; for he does not easily brook opposition and is ever valiant in warfare.” (23)

verses.text:
श्रुत्वा हिमवतो वाक्यं कोपाविष्टः स दुन्दुभिः।
जगाम तां पुरीं तस्य किष्किन्धां वालिनस्तदा॥ २४॥
धारयन् माहिषं रूपं तीक्ष्णशृङ्गो भयावहः।
प्रावृषीव महामेघस्तोयपूर्णो नभस्तले॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Seized with wrath to hear the words of Himavān, nay, retaining the form of a buffalo and looking like a huge cloud surcharged with water in the vault of heavens during the rains, the said Dundubhi, who was endowed with pointed horns and inspired terror, forthwith sought Kiṣkindhā, the well-known capital of the celebrated Vālī. (24-25)

verses.text:
ततस्तु द्वारमागम्य किष्किन्धाया महाबलः।
ननर्द कम्पयन् भूमिं दुन्दुभिर्दुन्दुभिर्यथा॥ २६॥
समीपजान् द्रुमान् भञ्जन् वसुधां दारयन् खुरैः।
विषाणेनोल्लिखन् दर्पात् तद्द्वारं द्विरदो यथा॥ २७॥
verses.m: “Reaching the gate of Kiṣkindhā, Dundubhi for his part, who was possessed of great might, thundered even as a large kettledrum would when beaten, causing the earth to shake, snapping the trees that had taken root in the neighbourhood, nay, rending the earth with its hoofs and arrogantly damaging the gate of Kiṣkindhā with its horns, as an elephant would with its tusk. (26-27)

verses.text:
अन्तःपुरगतो वाली श्रुत्वा शब्दममर्षणः।
निष्पपात सह स्त्रीभिस्ताराभिरिव चन्द्रमा॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Hearing the roar, Vālī, who was in the gynaeceum, and who was intolerant by nature, rushed forth with his wives even as the moon would appear in the horizon with hosts of stars. (28)

verses.text:
मितं व्यक्ताक्षरपदं तमुवाच स दुन्दुभिम्।
हरीणामीश्वरो वाली सर्वेषां वनचारिणाम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Vālī, the ruler of monkeys as well as of all the other denizens of the forest, spoke to the aforesaid Dundubhi in the following few words uttered with distinct accents : (29)

verses.text:
किमर्थं नगरद्वारमिदं रुद्ध्वा विनर्दसे।
दुन्दुभे विदितो मेऽसि रक्ष प्राणान् महाबल॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Why do you utter loud threats blocking this gate of the city, O Dundubhi? You are already known to me; (please) save your life (if you can), O demon possessed of extraordinary might !’ (30)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा वानरेन्द्रस्य धीमतः।
उवाच दुन्दुभिर्वाक्यं क्रोधात् संरक्तलोचनः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid challenge of the wise Vālī, the ruler of monkeys, Dundubhi replied as follows, his eyes turned crimson with anger : (31)

verses.text:
न त्वं स्त्रीसंनिधौ वीर वचनं वक्तुमर्हसि।
मम युद्धं प्रयच्छाद्य ततो ज्ञास्यामि ते बलम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “ ‘You ought not to throw out a challenge in the presence of ladies, O gallant monkey ! Give battle to me today, then only shall I come to know your might. (32)

verses.text:
अथवा धारयिष्यामि क्रोधमद्य निशामिमाम्।
गृह्यतामुदयः स्वैरं कामभोगेषु वानर॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “ ‘Or, I shall restrain my anger today; let your passion for the enjoyment of sensuous pleasures be freely indulged in for this night, O monkey ! (33)

verses.text:
दीयतां सम्प्रदानं च परिष्वज्य च वानरान्।
सर्वशाखामृगेन्द्रस्त्वं संसादय सुहृज्जनम्॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “ ‘Let loving presents be given to the monkeys after embracing them. Take you leave of your dear and near ones, the ruler as you are of all monkeys. (34)

verses.text:
सुदृष्टां कुरु किष्किन्धां कुरुष्वात्मसमं पुरे।
क्रीडस्व च समं स्त्रीभिरहं ते दर्पशासनः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Let Kiṣkindhā be carefully seen for the last time, since you are not going to see it any more; place a replica of yours in the person of your son in charge of the city to look after it when you are no more and revel finally in the company of your wives till sunrise; for I am going to tame your arrogance soon. (35)

verses.text:
यो हि मत्तं प्रमत्तं वा भग्नं वा रहितं कृशम्।
हन्यात् स भ्रूणहा लोके त्वद्विधं मदमोहितम्॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “ ‘He who kills one who is drunk, is unwary, has broken a limb or has been deprived of his weapons, is emaciated of body or is blinded by passion like you is indeed as despicable as a foeticide.’ (36)

verses.text:
स प्रहस्याब्रवीन्मन्दं क्रोधात् तमसुरेश्वरम्।
विसृज्य ताः स्त्रियः सर्वास्ताराप्रभृतिकास्तदा॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Laughing heartily and dismissing all those ladies led by Tārā, Vālī now angrily replied as follows to the silly lord of demons : (37)

verses.text:
मत्तोऽयमिति मा मंस्था यद्यभीतोऽसि संयुगे।
मदोऽयं सम्प्रहारेऽस्मिन् वीरपानं समर्थ्यताम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Do not be misled to think that I am drunk, if you are not afraid of engaging in a contest with me. Let this inebriety of mine be construed as a state of drunkenness resorted to by a hero on the occasion of this duel with you.’ (38)

verses.text:
तमेवमुक्त्वा संक्रुद्धो मालामुत्क्षिप्य काञ्चनीम्।
पित्रा दत्तां महेन्द्रेण युद्धाय व्यवतिष्ठत॥ ३९॥
verses.m: “Replying to him thus and throwing about his neck a chain of gold gifted to him by his father, the mighty Indra, Vālī stood prepared for an encounter with the demon, highly enraged. (39)

verses.text:
विषाणयोर्गृहीत्वा तं दुन्दुभिं गिरिसंनिभम्।
आविध्यत तथा वाली विनदन् कपिकुञ्जरः॥ ४०॥
verses.m: “Seizing by the horns the aforesaid Dundubhi, who looked like a mountain, Vālī, an elephant among monkeys, forthwith began to revolve him, uttering a loud deep hoarse sound. (40)

verses.text:
बलाद् व्यापादयांचक्रे ननर्द च महास्वनम्।
श्रोत्राभ्यामथ रक्तं तु तस्य सुस्राव पात्यतः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: “Vālī then threw him down and uttered a loud cry. While he was being thrown down, blood immediately flowed from his ears. (41)

verses.text:
तयोस्तु क्रोधसंरम्भात् परस्परजयैषिणोः।
युद्धं समभवद् घोरं दुन्दुभेर्वालिनस्तथा॥ ४२॥
verses.m: “A terrible struggle then raged between the two combatants, Dundubhi and Vālī, who were keen to conquer each other in the vehemence of their wrath. (42)

verses.text:
अयुध्यत तदा वाली शक्रतुल्यपराक्रमः।
मुष्टिभिर्जानुभिः पद्भिः शिलाभिः पादपैस्तथा॥ ४३॥
verses.m: “Vālī, who was equal to Indra, the ruler of gods, in prowess, then struck with fists, knees, feet, rocks and trees. (43)

verses.text:
परस्परं घ्नतोस्तत्र वानरासुरयोस्तदा।
आसीद्धीनोऽसुरो युद्धे शक्रसूनुर्व्यवर्धत॥ ४४॥
verses.m: “While the monkey and the demon were striking one another on that spot at that time, the demon began to lose ground in the contest, while Vālī (Indra’s son) gained the upper hand. (44)

verses.text:
तं तु दुन्दुभिमुद्यम्य धरण्यामभ्यपातयत्।
युद्धे प्राणहरे तस्मिन्निष्पिष्टो दुन्दुभिस्तदा॥ ४५॥
verses.m: “Lifting Dundubhi, Vālī for his part dashed him to the ground with the result that Dundubhi was instantly crushed in that deadly contest. (45)

verses.text:
स्रोतोभ्यो बहु रक्तं तु तस्य सुस्राव पात्यतः।
पपात च महाबाहुः क्षितौ पञ्चत्वमागतः॥ ४६॥
verses.m: “While he was being thrown down, profuse blood flowed from the openings in his body (viz., his eyes, ears, nostrils, mouth and so on) and the mighty-armed demon dropped dead to the ground. (46)

verses.text:
तं तोलयित्वा बाहुभ्यां गतसत्त्वमचेतनम्।
चिक्षेप वेगवान् वाली वेगेनैकेन योजनम्॥ ४७॥
verses.m: “Lifting up with his arms Dundubhi, who was now lifeless and as such unconscious, the impetuous Vālī hurled him with a single effort to a distance of four miles. (47)

verses.text:
तस्य वेगप्रविद्धस्य वक्त्रात् क्षतजबिन्दवः।
प्रपेतुर्मारुतोत्क्षिप्ता मतङ्गस्याश्रमं प्रति॥ ४८॥
verses.m: “Propelled by the wind, drops of blood from the mouth of the demon, when he was hurled with impetuosity, fell on the side of Mataṅga’s hermitage. (48)

verses.text:
तान् दृष्ट्वा पतितांस्तत्र मुनिः शोणितविप्रुषः।
क्रुद्धस्तस्य महाभाग चिन्तयामास को न्वयम्॥ ४९॥
verses.m: “Enraged to behold those drops of blood fallen in the precincts of his hermitage, O highly blessed prince, the sage contemplated as to who on earth was responsible for scattering the blood. (49)

verses.text:
येनाहं सहसा स्पृष्टः शोणितेन दुरात्मना।
कोऽयं दुरात्मा दुर्बुद्धिरकृतात्मा च बालिशः॥ ५०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Who is the evil-minded, perverse, wanton and stupid fellow by whom I have been spattered with blood all at once?’ he said to himself. (50)

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा स विनिष्क्रम्य ददृशे मुनिसत्तमः।
महिषं पर्वताकारं गतासुं पतितं भुवि॥ ५१॥
verses.m: “Saying so and coming out in the open, the aforesaid jewel among ascetics beheld a buffalo, looking like a mountain, fallen dead on the ground. (51)

verses.text:
स तु विज्ञाय तपसा वानरेण कृतं हि तत्।
उत्ससर्ज महाशापं क्षेप्तारं वानरं प्रति॥ ५२॥
verses.m: “Definitely coming to know by virtue of his askesis that it was surely the work of a monkey, he pronounced the following terrible imprecation on the monkey who had hurled the carcass. (52)

verses.text:
इह तेनाप्रवेष्टव्यं प्रविष्टस्य वधो भवेत्।
वनं मत्संश्रयं येन दूषितं रुधिरस्रवैः॥ ५३॥
verses.m: “ ‘The monkey by whom the forest which is my abode has been desecrated with drops of blood ought not to set foot into this forest; his death will instantly follow if he steps into it. (53)

verses.text:
क्षिपता पादपाश्चेमे सम्भग्नाश्चासुरीं तनुम्।
समन्तादाश्रमं पूर्णं योजनं मामकं यदि॥ ५४॥
आगमिष्यति दुर्बुद्धिर्व्यक्तं स न भविष्यति।
ये चास्य सचिवाः केचित् संश्रिता मामकं वनम्॥ ५५॥
न च तैरिह वस्तव्यं श्रुत्वा यान्तु यथासुखम्।
तेऽपि वा यदि तिष्ठन्ति शपिष्ये तानपि ध्रुवम्॥ ५६॥
वनेऽस्मिन् मामके नित्यं पुत्रवत् परिरक्षिते।
पत्राङ्कुरविनाशाय फलमूलाभवाय च॥ ५७॥
verses.m: “ ‘If the perverted fellow by whom these trees have been smashed while throwing away the corpse of a demon sets his foot within a radius of full four miles of my hermitage will surely no longer survive. Nor should his ministers, whosoever have encamped in my forest tarry here any longer. Let them on hearing this malediction conveniently depart. If, however, they too remain in this forest of mine—which has been nurtured by me like my own offspring—for the destruction of its leaves and shoots as well as for the extinction of its fruits and roots, I shall assuredly curse them too. (54—57)

verses.text:
दिवसश्चाद्य मर्यादा यं द्रष्टा श्वोऽस्मि वानरम्।
बहुवर्षसहस्राणि स वै शैलो भविष्यति॥ ५८॥
verses.m: “ ‘This day (on which I pronounced this execration) is the deadline for their sojourn in this forest. The monkey whom I shall see here tomorrow will surely be changed into a rock and continue in that state for many thousands of years.’ (58)

verses.text:
ततस्ते वानराः श्रुत्वा गिरं मुनिसमीरिताम्।
निश्चक्रमुर्वनात् तस्मात् तान् दृष्ट्वा वालिरब्रवीत्॥ ५९॥
verses.m: “Hearing the malediction uttered by the sage, the aforesaid monkeys thereupon went away from that forest. Seeing them, Vālī said to them : (59)

verses.text:
किं भवन्तः समस्ताश्च मतङ्गवनवासिनः।
मत्समीपमनुप्राप्ता अपि स्वस्ति वनौकसाम्॥ ६०॥
verses.m: “ ‘Wherefore have you and all the denizens of Mataṅgavana (the grove occupied by Sage Mataṅga) sought my presence? I hope all is well with the denizens of the said forest.’ (60)

verses.text:
ततस्ते कारणं सर्वं तथा शापं च वालिनः।
शशंसुर्वानराः सर्वे वालिने हेममालिने॥ ६१॥
verses.m: “Thereupon all those monkeys reported to Vālī, who was adorned with a chain of gold, the whole reason of their sudden departure from the forest and referred to the malediction pronounced on Vālī. (61)

verses.text:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा तदा वाली वचनं वानरेरितम्।
स महर्षिं समासाद्य याचते स्म कृताञ्जलिः॥ ६२॥
verses.m: “Hearing the aforesaid explanation given by the monkeys, and duly approaching the eminent sage, the aforesaid Vālī with joined palms craved his indulgence. (62)

verses.text:
महर्षिस्तमनादृत्य प्रविवेशाश्रमं प्रति।
शापधारणभीतस्तु वाली विह्वलतां गतः॥ ६३॥
verses.m: “Disregarding him, however, the eminent sage entered deep into the hermitage, while Vālī, who was afraid of receiving the curse, was reduced to a state of utter confusion. (63)

verses.text:
ततः शापभयाद् भीतो ऋष्यमूकं महागिरिम्।
प्रवेष्टुं नेच्छति हरिर्द्रष्टुं वापि नरेश्वर॥ ६४॥
verses.m: “Stricken with fear of the curse, the monkey, Vālī, no longer seeks to enter the boundary of the great Ṛṣyamūka hill or even to look at it, O lord of human beings ! (64)

verses.text:
तस्याप्रवेशं ज्ञात्वाहमिदं राम महावनम्।
विचरामि सहामात्यो विषादेन विवर्जितः॥ ६५॥
verses.m: “Knowing that he cannot penetrate into it, O Rāma, I roam about in this large forest with my ministers, entirely free from anxiety as I am. (65)

verses.text:
एषोऽस्थिनिचयस्तस्य दुन्दुभेः सम्प्रकाशते।
वीर्योत्सेकान्निरस्तस्य गिरिकूटनिभो महान्॥ ६६॥
verses.m: “Here is the colossal heap, shining most conspicuously like a mountain-top, of the bones of Dundubhi, who was thrown with pride of virility. (66)

verses.text:
इमे च विपुलाः सालाः सप्त शाखावलम्बिनः।
यत्रैकं घटते वाली निष्पत्रयितुमोजसा॥ ६७॥
verses.m: “These are the seven gigantic sal trees, hanging low with their boughs, each of which Vālī can denude of its leaves by shaking it with his might. (67)

verses.text:
एतदस्यासमं वीर्यं मया राम प्रकाशितम्।
कथं तं वालिनं हन्तुं समरे शक्ष्यसे नृप॥ ६८॥
verses.m: “Such is the matchless strength of Vālī revealed by me, O Rāma ! How will you be able to kill that Vālī in a combat, O protector of men?” (68)

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवाणं सुग्रीवं प्रहसँल्लक्ष्मणोऽब्रवीत्।
कस्मिन् कर्मणि निर्वृत्ते श्रद्दध्या वालिनो वधम्॥ ६९॥
verses.m: To Sugrīva, who was speaking as aforesaid, Lakṣmaṇa, heartily laughing, said, “On what feat being accomplished should you believe that Vālī can be disposed of by Śrī Rāma?” (69)

verses.text:
तमुवाचाथ सुग्रीवः सप्त सालानिमान् पुरा।
एवमेकैकशो वाली विव्याधाथ स चासकृत्॥ ७०॥
verses.m: To him Sugrīva forthwith replied, “In the past Vālī pierced these seven sal trees one after another and he did so more than once even later. (70)

verses.text:
रामो निर्दारयेदेषां बाणेनैकेन च द्रुमम्।
वालिनं निहतं मन्ये दृष्ट्वा रामस्य विक्रमम्॥ ७१॥
verses.m: “If Śrī Rāma too should be able to split one of these trees with a single arrow, I shall consider Vālī killed on witnessing Śrī Rāma’s prowess. (71)

verses.text:
हतस्य महिषस्यास्थि पादेनैकेन लक्ष्मण।
उद्यम्य प्रक्षिपेच्चापि तरसा द्वे धनुःशते॥ ७२॥
verses.m: “I shall deem him killed even if lifting with his single foot the bones of the buffalo made short work of by Vālī, Śrī Rāma should be able to throw them by his might to a distance of two hundred bows’ (or eight hundred arms’) length, O Lakṣmaṇa !” (72)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवो रामं रक्तान्तलोचनम्।
ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं काकुत्स्थं पुनरेव वचोऽब्रवीत्॥ ७३॥
verses.m: Saying so, and contemplating awhile on Śrī Rāma, Sugrīva, for his part, the corners of whose eyes were red, spoke once more as follows to Śrī Rāma (a scion of Kakutstha) : (73)

verses.text:
शूरश्च शूरमानी च प्रख्यातबलपौरुषः।
बलवान् वानरो वाली संयुगेष्वपराजितः॥ ७४॥
verses.m: “The powerful monkey, Vālī, is valiant and accounts himself valiant and is widely known for his strength and manliness. He has never been worsted in conflicts. (74)

verses.text:
दृश्यन्ते चास्य कर्माणि दुष्कराणि सुरैरपि।
यानि संचिन्त्य भीतोऽहमृष्यमूकमुपाश्रितः॥ ७५॥
verses.m: “His exploits are seen to be such as are difficult to accomplish even for gods and pondering them I have taken shelter on Mount Ṛṣyamūka, afraid as I am. (75)

verses.text:
तमजय्यमधृष्यं च वानरेन्द्रममर्षणम्।
विचिन्तयन्न मुञ्चामि ऋष्यमूकममुं त्वहम्॥ ७६॥
verses.m: “Thinking with apprehension of that lord of monkeys, who is invincible, nay, unassailable and intolerant, I, for my part, do not leave this Ṛṣyamūka mountain.(76)

verses.text:
उद्विग्नः शङ्कितश्चाहं विचरामि महावने।
अनुरक्तैः सहामात्यैर्हनुमत्प्रमुखैर्वरैः॥ ७७॥
verses.m: “Perturbed and full of apprehension I roam about in the extensive forest with my devoted and excellent ministers headed by Hanumān. (77)

verses.text:
उपलब्धं च मे श्लाघ्यं सन्मित्रं मित्रवत्सल।
त्वामहं पुरुषव्याघ्र हिमवन्तमिवाश्रितः॥ ७८॥
verses.m: “Nay, a praiseworthy and noble ally has been found by me in you, O prince, fond of your friends ! I have taken refuge in you as one would resort to the Himālaya mountain, O tiger among men ! (78)

verses.text:
किं तु तस्य बलज्ञोऽहं दुर्भ्रातुर्बलशालिनः।
अप्रत्यक्षं तु मे वीर्यं समरे तव राघव॥ ७९॥
verses.m: “I am, however, aware of the strength of my mighty and vile brother; while your prowess in battle is not before my eyes, O scion of Raghu ! (79)

verses.text:
न खल्वहं त्वां तुलये नावमन्ये न भीषये।
कर्मभिस्तस्य भीमैश्च कातर्यं जनितं मम॥ ८०॥
verses.m: “Assuredly, I neither test you, nor belittle you, nor do I frighten you. Nay, pusillanimity has been engendered in me by his terrible deeds. (80)

verses.text:
कामं राघव ते वाणी प्रमाणं धैर्यमाकृतिः।
सूचयन्ति परं तेजो भस्मच्छन्नमिवानलम्॥ ८१॥
verses.m: “Your (unfaltering) speech, which is trustworthy, as well as your confidence and divine look abundantly indicate your supreme strength, which is analogous to a fire covered with ashes, O scion of Raghu !” (81)

verses.text:
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
स्मितपूर्वमथो रामः प्रत्युवाच हरिं प्रति॥ ८२॥
verses.m: Hearing the aforesaid submission of that high-minded Sugrīva, Śrī Rāma then smilingly replied as follows to the monkey, Sugrīva : (82)

verses.text:
यदि न प्रत्ययोऽस्मासु विक्रमे तव वानर।
प्रत्ययं समरे श्लाघ्यमहमुत्पादयामि ते॥ ८३॥
verses.m: “If you have no faith in the prowess inhering in us, O monkey, I shall presently inspire in you confidence which is laudable in a combat.” (83)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा तु सुग्रीवं सान्त्वयँल्लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
राघवो दुन्दुभेः कायं पादाङ्गुष्ठेन लीलया॥ ८४॥
तोलयित्वा महाबाहुश्चिक्षेप दशयोजनम्।
असुरस्य तनुं शुष्कां पादाङ्गुष्ठेन वीर्यवान्॥ ८५॥
verses.m: Saying so and lifting in sport the carcass of Dundubhi with his toe, the mighty-armed and powerful Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa, for his part hurled the dried up skeleton of the demon to a distance of ten Yojanas (eighty-miles), thereby reassuring Sugrīva. (84-85)

verses.text:
क्षिप्तं दृष्ट्वा ततः कायं सुग्रीवः पुनरब्रवीत्।
लक्ष्मणस्याग्रतो रामं तपन्तमिव भास्करम्।
हरीणामग्रतो वीरमिदं वचनमर्थवत्॥ ८६॥
verses.m: Beholding the skeleton cast away by Śrī Rāma, Sugrīva then addressed once more to the heroic Śrī Rāma, scorching as the sun, in the presence of Lakṣmaṇa as well as of the other monkeys the following significant words : (86)

verses.text:
आर्द्रः समांसः प्रत्यग्रः क्षिप्तः कायः पुरा सखे।
परिश्रान्तेन मत्तेन भ्रात्रा मे वालिना तदा॥ ८७॥
verses.m: “The carcass was thrown in the past, O my friend, while it was saturated with blood, full of flesh and fresh, having been shortly before killed by my elder brother, Vālī, at a time when he was exhausted and drunk. (87)

verses.text:
लघुः सम्प्रति निर्मांसस्तृणभूतश्च राघव।
क्षिप्त एवं प्रहर्षेण भवता रघुनन्दन॥ ८८॥
verses.m: “Having been stripped of its flesh, it is now light and converted into mere straw, as compared to its former weight, O scion of Raghu, and has been hurled by you with such extreme joy, O delight of Raghu ! (88)

verses.text:
नात्र शक्यं बलं ज्ञातुं तव वा तस्य वाधिकम्।
आर्द्रं शुष्कमिति ह्येतत् सुमहद् राघवान्तरम्॥ ८९॥
verses.m: “It is not possible under the circumstances to ascertain whose strength is greater—yours or his; for whether a carcass is saturated with blood or dried up makes a very great difference, O scion of Raghu ! (89)

verses.text:
स एव संशयस्तात तव तस्य च यद्बलम्।
सालमेकं विनिर्भिद्य भवेद् व्यक्तिर्बलाबले॥ ९०॥
verses.m: “The same doubt still lingers in my mind about the strength which inheres in you as well as in Vālī, O dear friend ! Certainly in the matter of your relative strength or weakness will be arrived at by your thoroughly piercing a single sal tree (of the seven trees shown to you). (90)

verses.text:
कृत्वैतत् कार्मुकं सज्यं हस्तिहस्तमिवाततम्।
आकर्णपूर्णमायम्य विसृजस्व महाशरम्॥ ९१॥
verses.m: “Stringing this bow, which is like another trunk of an elephant, and stretching it at full length up to your ear, discharge a big arrow. (91)

verses.text:
इमं हि सालं प्रहितस्त्वया शरो
न संशयोऽत्रास्ति विदारयिष्यति।
अलं विमर्शेन मम प्रियं ध्रुवं
कुरुष्व राजन् प्रतिशापितो मया॥ ९२॥
verses.m: “Shot by you, the arrow will surely split up the yonder sal tree : there is no doubt about it. Reflect no more and, adjured by me, O king, oblige me unhesitatingly. (92)

verses.text:
यथा हि तेजःसु वरः सदा रवि-
र्यथा हि शैलो हिमवान् महाद्रिषु।
यथा चतुष्पात्सु च केसरी वर-
स्तथा नराणामसि विक्रमे वरः॥ ९३॥
verses.m: “Even as the sun is always the foremost of all luminaries, even as the Himālaya mountain is the foremost of all large mountains and even as a lion is the foremost of all quadrupeds, so are you the foremost of all human beings in prowess.” (93)

verses.text:
एतच्च वचनं श्रुत्वा सुग्रीवस्य सुभाषितम्।
प्रत्ययार्थं महातेजा रामो जग्राह कार्मुकम्॥ १॥
verses.m: Nay, hearing this well-worded submission of Sugrīva, Śrī Rāma, who was invested with exceptional glory, took up his bow to inspire confidence in the former. (1)

verses.text:
स गृहीत्वा धनुर्घोरं शरमेकं च मानदः।
सालमुद्दिश्य चिक्षेप पूरयन् स रवैर्दिशः॥ २॥
verses.m: Taking up the dreadful bow and an arrow and aiming it at the sal tree (pointed out by Sugrīva), the celebrated Śrī Rāma, the bestower of honour on others, discharged it filling the quarters with the twang of the bow. (2)

verses.text:
स विसृष्टो बलवता बाणः स्वर्णपरिष्कृतः।
भित्त्वा सालान् गिरिप्रस्थं सप्तभूमिं विवेश ह॥ ३॥
verses.m: Piercing all the seven sal trees (though it was aimed at only one of them), as well as the plateau on which they stood, as also the six subterranean regions, the aforesaid arrow, which was shot by the mighty prince and was decked with gold, entered Pātāla (the seventh subterranean region); so the tradition goes. (3)

verses.text:
सायकस्तु मुहूर्तेन सालान् भित्त्वा महाजवः।
निष्पत्य च पुनस्तूणं तमेव प्रविवेश ह॥ ४॥
verses.m: Having pierced the sal trees (as well as the plateau and the bowels of the earth) in the course of less than an hour and forcing its way out, the arrow for its part, which was possessed of great velocity, quickly entered once more, they say, the same quiver from which it had emerged. (4)

verses.text:
तान् दृष्ट्वा सप्त निर्भिन्नान् सालान् वानरपुङ्गवः।
रामस्य शरवेगेन विस्मयं परमं गतः॥ ५॥
verses.m: Sugrīva (the foremost of monkeys) was seized with great wonder to see (with his own eyes) those seven sal trees thoroughly pierced by the impetuosity of Śrī Rāma’s arrow. (5)

verses.text:
स मूर्ध्ना न्यपतद् भूमौ प्रलम्बीकृतभूषणः।
सुग्रीवः परमप्रीतो राघवाय कृताञ्जलिः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Supremely pleased, Sugrīva with joined palms fell flat on the ground as a token of respect towards Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), with his head touching the ground and his ornaments also hanging loose in the process of bending low. (6)

verses.text:
इदं चोवाच धर्मज्ञं कर्मणा तेन हर्षितः।
रामं सर्वास्त्रविदुषां श्रेष्ठं शूरमवस्थितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: Nay, delighted with that feat of Śrī Rāma, he spoke as follows to the valiant Śrī Rāma, the foremost of those adept in the use of all types of missiles, who knew what is right and stood before him : (7)

verses.text:
सेन्द्रानपि सुरान् सर्वांस्त्वं बाणैः पुरुषर्षभ।
समर्थः समरे हन्तुं किं पुनर्वालिनं प्रभो॥ ८॥
verses.m: “You are able to kill with your arrows in an encounter all the gods including even Indra, their ruler, O jewel among men, much more so, Vālī, my lord ! (8)

verses.text:
येन सप्त महासाला गिरिर्भूमिश्च दारिताः।
बाणेनैकेन काकुत्स्थ स्थाता ते को रणाग्रतः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Who can stand in the van of a battle before you, by whom seven big sal trees as well as the mountain on which the trees stood and the earth supporting it have been pierced with a single arrow, O scion of Kakutstha? (9)

verses.text:
अद्य मे विगतः शोकः प्रीतिरद्य परा मम।
सुहृदं त्वां समासाद्य महेन्द्रवरुणोपमम्॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Now that I have duly met in the form of an ally you, who are a compeer of the mighty Indra (the ruler of gods) and Varuṇa (the god of waters), my grief has totally disappeared and my joy is supreme today. (10)

verses.text:
तमद्यैव प्रियार्थं मे वैरिणं भ्रातृरूपिणम्।
वालिनं जहि काकुत्स्थ मया बद्धोऽयमञ्जलिः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “For my pleasure, O scion of Kākutstha, pray, make short work of Vālī, my enemy in the guise of a brother, this very day: so have these palms been joined by me.” (11)

verses.text:
ततो रामः परिष्वज्य सुग्रीवं प्रियदर्शनम्।
प्रत्युवाच महाप्राज्ञो लक्ष्मणानुगतं वचः॥ १२॥
verses.m: Embracing Sugrīva of pleasing aspect, Śrī Rāma, who was exceptionally wise, thereupon replied as follows to Sugrīva, who was dear as Lakṣmaṇa to him : (12)

verses.text:
अस्माद्गच्छाम किष्किन्धां क्षिप्रं गच्छ त्वमग्रतः।
गत्वा चाह्वय सुग्रीव वालिनं भ्रातृगन्धिनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Let us proceed, O Sugrīva, to Kiṣkindhā from this mountain; depart you ahead without delay and, going there, challenge to a duel Vālī, who bears the name of a brother !” (13)

verses.text:
सर्वे ते त्वरितं गत्वा किष्किन्धां वालिनः पुरीम्।
वृक्षैरात्मानमावृत्य ह्यतिष्ठन् गहने वने॥ १४॥
verses.m: Reaching with hasty steps Kiṣkindhā, the capital of Vālī, and hiding themselves behind trees, they all halted in a dense forest. (14)

verses.text:
सुग्रीवोऽप्यनदद् घोरं वालिनो ह्वानकारणात्।
गाढं परिहितो वेगान्नादैर्भिन्दन्निवाम्बरम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: Tightly girded about his loins, even Sugrīva roared frightfully by way of a challenge to Vālī, rending the air, as it were, by his shouts uttered with vehemence. (15)

verses.text:
तं श्रुत्वा निनदं भ्रातुः क्रुद्धो वाली महाबलः।
निष्पपात सुसंरब्धो भास्करोऽस्ततटादिव॥ १६॥
verses.m: Enraged to hear that roar of his (younger) brother and highly excited, Vālī, who was possessed of extraordinary might, rushed forth as impetuously as the sun would slide from the edge of the western mountain (behind which the sun is supposed to set). (16)

verses.text:
ततः सुतुमुलं युद्धं वालिसुग्रीवयोरभूत्।
गगने ग्रहयोर्घोरं बुधाङ्गारकयोरिव॥ १७॥
verses.m: Then ensued a most tumultuous and terrible combat between Vālī and Sugrīva, resembling a clash between Mercury and Mars in the heavens. (17)

verses.text:
तलैरशनिकल्पैश्च वज्रकल्पैश्च मुष्टिभिः।
जघ्नतुः समरेऽन्योन्यं भ्रातरौ क्रोधमूर्च्छितौ॥ १८॥
verses.m: Blinded with anger, the two brothers struck each other in the course of their encounter with their palms and soles, which fell like lightning, and fists, which descended like the thunderbolt. (18)

verses.text:
ततो रामो धनुष्पाणिस्तावुभौ समुदैक्षत।
अन्योन्यसदृशौ वीरावुभौ देवाविवाश्विनौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: Bow in hand, Śrī Rāma thereupon keenly watched both the aforesaid heroes, who both closely resembled each other like the two Aświns (the twin-gods presiding over the star, Gemini). (19)

verses.text:
यन्नावगच्छत् सुग्रीवं वालिनं वापि राघवः।
ततो न कृतवान् बुद्धिं मोक्तुमन्तकरं शरम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: Since Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) could not make out Sugrīva or Vālī because of their close resemblance, he, therefore, could not make up his mind to discharge his deadly arrow (lest it should hit Sugrīva and dispose him of). (20)

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे भग्नः सुग्रीवस्तेन वालिना।
अपश्यन् राघवं नाथमृष्यमूकं प्रदुद्रुवे॥ २१॥
verses.m: Discomfited by the aforesaid Vālī and not perceiving Śrī Rāma as his protector, Sugrīva in the meantime ran for life towards Ṛṣyamūka. (21)

verses.text:
क्लान्तो रुधिरसिक्ताङ्गः प्रहारैर्जर्जरीकृतः।
वालिनाभिद्रुतः क्रोधात् प्रविवेश महावनम्॥ २२॥
verses.m: Exhausted and battered with the blows of Vālī, his whole body bathed in blood, and chased in anger by Vālī, he entered the large forest (occupied by Sage Mataṅga). (22)

verses.text:
तं प्रविष्टं वनं दृष्ट्वा वाली शापभयात् ततः।
मुक्तो ह्यसि त्वमित्युक्त्वा स निवृत्तो महाबलः॥ २३॥
verses.m: Seeing him having penetrated into the forest and saying “Indeed you are spared,” the aforesaid Vālī, even though possessed of extraordinary might, desisted from the pursuit due to fear of the curse. (23)

verses.text:
राघवोऽपि सह भ्रात्रा सह चैव हनूमता।
तदेव वनमागच्छत् सुग्रीवो यत्र वानरः॥ २४॥
verses.m: Alongwith his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, as well as Hanumān, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) too returned to the same forest where the monkey chief Sugrīva was. (24)

verses.text:
तं समीक्ष्यागतं रामं सुग्रीवः सहलक्ष्मणम्।
ह्रीमान् दीनमुवाचेदं वसुधामवलोकयन्॥ २५॥
verses.m: Discerning Śrī Rāma returned with Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva piteously spoke to him as follows, looking at the ground, full of shame at his discomfiture, as he was : (25)

verses.text:
आह्वयस्वेति मामुक्त्वा दर्शयित्वा च विक्रमम्।
वैरिणा घातयित्वा च किमिदानीं त्वया कृतम्॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Having demonstrated your prowess and saying to me ‘Challenge Vālī to a duel’, what have you done now by getting me smitten by the enemy? (26)

verses.text:
तामेव वेलां वक्तव्यं त्वया राघव तत्त्वतः।
वालिनं न निहन्मीति ततो नाहमितो व्रजे॥ २७॥
verses.m: “In all faith it should have been pointed out by you that very moment : ‘I am not going to kill Vālī’. Then I would not have moved from this place.” (27)

verses.text:
तस्य चैवं ब्रुवाणस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः।
करुणं दीनया वाचा राघवः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ २८॥
verses.m: To that high-minded Sugrīva, who was piteously speaking as aforesaid in doleful accents, Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu) replied again : (28)

verses.text:
सुग्रीव श्रूयतां तात क्रोधश्च व्यपनीयताम्।
कारणं येन बाणोऽयं स मया न विसर्जितः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Sugrīva, dear brother, let anger be banished from your mind and the reason why this deadly arrow was not discharged by me be heard. (29)

verses.text:
अलंकारेण वेषेण प्रमाणेन गतेन च।
त्वं च सुग्रीव वाली च सदृशौ स्थः परस्परम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “You, O Sugrīva, and Vālī resemble each other in personal embellishment, costume, stature and gait too. (30)

verses.text:
स्वरेण वर्चसा चैव प्रेक्षितेन च वानर।
विक्रमेण च वाक्यैश्च व्यक्तिं वां नोपलक्षये॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “I did not perceive any distinction between you two—in voice as well as in splendour, in look and in prowess as well as in speech.(31)

verses.text:
ततोऽहं रूपसादृश्यान्मोहितो वानरोत्तम।
नोत्सृजामि महावेगं शरं शत्रुनिबर्हणम्॥ ३२॥
जीवितान्तकरं घोरं सादृश्यात् तु विशङ्कितः।
मूलघातो न नौ स्याद्धि द्वयोरिति कृतो मया॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Puzzled as I was by the likeness of your features, O jewel among the monkeys, I, therefore, did not let fly the deadly and terrible arrow possessed of great velocity and capable of destroying the enemy. Seized as I was with apprehension, due to your close resemblance, lest the very root of us both should be destroyed by me by killing you unwittingly, this omission was deliberately committed by me. (32-33)

verses.text:
त्वयि वीर विपन्ने हि अज्ञानाल्लाघवान्मया।
मौढ्यं च मम बाल्यं च ख्यापितं स्यात् कपीश्वर॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “In the event of your being killed by me through ignorance or frivolity, my stupidity and puerility would have been surely exposed, O gallant ruler of monkeys ! (34)

verses.text:
दत्ताभयवधो नाम पातकं महदद्भुतम्।
अहं च लक्ष्मणश्चैव सीता च वरवर्णिनी॥ ३५॥
त्वदधीना वयं सर्वे वनेऽस्मिन् शरणं भवान्।
तस्माद् युध्यस्व भूयस्त्वं मा माशङ्कीश्च वानर॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Killing one to whom protection has been vouchsafed is professedly a great and astounding sin. Moreover, myself and Lakṣmaṇa too as well as Sītā of excellent complexion—we all depend on you. You are our refuge in this forest. Therefore, engage you in a combat with Vālī once more. Pray, do not, O do not fall a prey to misgiving, O monkey chief ! (35-36)

verses.text:
एतन्मुहूर्ते तु मया पश्य वालिनमाहवे।
निरस्तमिषुणैकेन चेष्टमानं महीतले॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “Within this hour behold Vālī struck down by me in course of the very combat with you with a single arrow and writhing on the ground. (37)

verses.text:
अभिज्ञानं कुरुष्व त्वमात्मनो वानरेश्वर।
येन त्वामभिजानीयां द्वन्द्वयुद्धमुपागतम्॥ ३८॥
verses.m: “Wear some distinguishing mark on your person, O lord of monkeys, by means of which I might recognize you when actually come to grips with Vālī. (38)

verses.text:
गजपुष्पीमिमां फुल्लामुत्पाट्य शुभलक्षणाम्।
कुरु लक्ष्मण कण्ठेऽस्य सुग्रीवस्य महात्मनः॥ ३९॥
verses.m: Turning to Lakṣmaṇa, he continued : “Uprooting this creeper, named Gajapuṣpī, which is in blossom and is propitious in character, fasten it, O Lakṣmaṇa, about the neck of the high-souled Sugrīva.” (39)

verses.text:
ततो गिरितटे जातामुत्पाट्य कुसुमायुताम्।
लक्ष्मणो गजपुष्पीं तां तस्य कण्ठे व्यसर्जयत्॥ ४०॥
verses.m: Plucking Gajapuṣpī creeper, adorned with flowers and growing on the side of the mountain, Lakṣmaṇa then fastened it about the neck of Sugrīva. (40)

verses.text:
स तया शुशुभे श्रीमाल्ँलतया कण्ठसक्तया।
मालयेव बलाकानां ससंध्य इव तोयदः॥ ४१॥
verses.m: With that creeper fastened to his neck, the glorious Sugrīva shone like a cloud accompanied by twilight, and encircled by a string of herons. (41)

verses.text:
विभ्राजमानो वपुषा रामवाक्यसमाहितः।
जगाम सह रामेण किष्किन्धां पुनराप सः॥ ४२॥
verses.m: Shining brightly with his body and reassured by Śrī Rāma’s words, Sugrīva left with Śrī Rāma and reached Kiṣkindhā once more. (42)

verses.text:
ऋष्यमूकात् स धर्मात्मा किष्किन्धां लक्ष्मणाग्रजः।
जगाम सह सुग्रीवो वालिविक्रमपालिताम्॥ १॥
समुद्यम्य महच्चापं रामः काञ्चनभूषितम्।
शरांश्चादित्यसंकाशान् गृहीत्वा रणसाधकान्॥ २॥
verses.m: Duly lifting up his great bow, decked with gold, and taking his arrows, which shone brightly like the sun and were so effective in battle, and accompanied by Sugrīva, Śrī Rāma (the eldest brother of Lakṣmaṇa), whose mind was set on virtue, proceeded from Ṛṣyamūka to Kiṣkindhā, which stood protected by Vālī’s valour. (1-2)

verses.text:
अग्रतस्तु ययौ तस्य राघवस्य महात्मनः।
सुग्रीवः संहतग्रीवो लक्ष्मणश्च महाबलः॥ ३॥
verses.m: In front of the high-souled Śrī Rāma, a scion of Raghu, strode Sugrīva who had a strongly built neck, as well as Lakṣmaṇa, who was possessed of extraordinary might. (3)

verses.text:
पृष्ठतो हनुमान् वीरो नलो नीलश्च वीर्यवान्।
तारश्चैव महातेजा हरियूथपयूथपः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Behind him came the valiant Hanumān, Nala and the powerful Nīla and Tāra, who was endowed with exceptional energy and was a commander of commanders of monkey hordes. (4)

verses.text:
ते वीक्षमाणा वृक्षांश्च पुष्पभारावलम्बिनः।
प्रसन्नाम्बुवहाश्चैव सरितः सागरंगमाः॥ ५॥
कन्दराणि च शैलांश्च निर्दराणि गुहास्तथा।
शिखराणि च मुख्यानि दरीश्च प्रियदर्शनाः॥ ६॥
वैदूर्यविमलैस्तोयैः पद्मैश्चाकोशकुड्मलैः।
शोभितान् सजलान् मार्गे तटाकांश्चावलोकयन्॥ ७॥
कारण्डैः सारसैर्हंसैर्वञ्जुलैर्जलकुक्कुटैः।
चक्रवाकैस्तथा चान्यैः शकुनैः प्रतिनादितान्॥ ८॥
मृदुशष्पाङ्कुराहारान्निर्भयान् वनगोचरान्।
चरतः सर्वतः पश्यन् स्थलीषु हरिणान् स्थितान्॥ ९॥
तटाकवैरिणश्चापि शुक्लदन्तविभूषितान्।
घोरानेकचरान् वन्यान् द्विरदान् कूलघातिनः॥ १०॥
मत्तान् गिरितटोत्कृष्टान् पर्वतानिव जङ्गमान्।
वानरान् द्विरदप्रख्यान् महीरेणुसमुक्षितान्॥ ११॥
वने वनचरांश्चान्यान् खेचरांश्च विहंगमान्।
पश्यन्तस्त्वरिता जग्मुः सुग्रीववशवर्तिनः॥ १२॥
