verses.m: “The monkeys have fallen into danger through the death of King Daśaratha, the destruction of Jaṭāyu and the abduction of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory).(14)

verses.text:
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्वासमरण्ये सह सीतया।
राघवस्य च बाणेन वालिनश्च तथा वधः॥ १५॥
रामकोपादशेषाणां रक्षसां च तथा वधम्।
कैकेय्या वरदानेन इदं च विकृतं कृतम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Know the sojourn of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmana in the forest with Sītā, and even so the destruction of Vālī encompassed by an arrow of Śrī Rāma (a scion of Raghu), and similarly the prospective extermination of all the ogres through the wrath of Śrī Rāma—all this evil to have been brought about by the boon granted by Daśaratha in favour of Kaikeyī.” (15-16)

verses.text:
तदसुखमनुकीर्तितं वचो
भुवि पतितांश्च निरीक्ष्य वानरान्।
भृशचकितमतिर्महामतिः
कृपणमुदाहृतवान् स गृध्रराजः॥ १७॥
verses.m: Greatly bewildered in mind to hear the aforesaid doleful cries uttered by the monkeys, and to perceive them tumbled down on the ground, the highly intelligent Sampāti, the king of vultures, spoke as follows in a piteous tone. (17)

verses.text:
तत् तु श्रुत्वा तथा वाक्यमङ्गदस्य मुखोद्गतम्।
अब्रवीद् वचनं गृध्रस्तीक्ष्णतुण्डो महास्वनः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Nay, hearing the speech that had escaped from the lips of Aṅgada as above, the sharp-beaked vulture, Sampāti, spoke as follows, making a loud noise : (18)

verses.text:
कोऽयं गिरा घोषयति प्राणैः प्रियतरस्य मे।
जटायुषो वधं भ्रातुः कम्पयन्निव मे मनः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Who is the being which proclaims in so many distinct words the death of my brother, Jaṭāyu, who was dearer to me than life itself, causing my heart to tremble as it were (with this heart-rending news)? (19)

verses.text:
कथमासीज्जनस्थाने युद्धं राक्षसगृध्रयोः।
नामधेयमिदं भ्रातुश्चिरस्याद्य मया श्रुतम्॥ २०॥
verses.m: “How did an encounter take place between an ogre and the vulture in Janasthāna? This name of my younger brother has been heard of by me after a long time today. (20)

verses.text:
इच्छेयं गिरिदुर्गाच्च भवद्भिरवतारितुम्।
यवीयसो गुणज्ञस्य श्लाघनीयस्य विक्रमैः॥ २१॥
अतिदीर्घस्य कालस्य परितुष्टोऽस्मि कीर्तनात्।
तदिच्छेयमहं श्रोतुं विनाशं वानरर्षभाः॥ २२॥
भ्रातुर्जटायुषस्तस्य जनस्थाननिवासिनः।
तस्यैव च मम भ्रातुः सखा दशरथः कथम्॥ २३॥
यस्य रामः प्रियः पुत्रो ज्येष्ठो गुरुजनप्रियः।
सूर्यांशुदग्धपक्षत्वान्न शक्नोमि विसर्पितुम्।
इच्छेयं पर्वतादस्मादवतर्तुमरिंदमाः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Nay, with your help I wish to bring myself down from the mountain citadel on which I am perched. I am highly gratified with the praises, heard after a very long time, of my younger brother, Jaṭāyu, who appreciated the virtues of others and was deserving of praise because of his exploits. Therefore, O leaders of monkeys, I long to hear about the destruction of my younger brother, Jaṭāyu, who lived in Janasthāna. Again, how did King Daśaratha, a friend of the selfsame brother of mine—whose beloved eldest son is Śrī Rāma, the favourite of his elders—meet his end? My wings having been scorched by the rays of the sun, I cannot fly about. All the same, I wish to descend from this eminence, O tamers of your foes.” (21—24)

verses.text:
शोकाद् भ्रष्टस्वरमपि श्रुत्वा वानरयूथपाः।
श्रद्दधुर्नैव तद्वाक्यं कर्मणा तस्य शङ्किताः॥ १॥
verses.m: Even after hearing the words of Sampāti, whose voice had turned hoarse due to grief caused by the news of his brother’s death, the monkey generals did not put faith in his words, seized as they were with suspicion caused by his contemplated action of eating up the monkeys. (1)

verses.text:
ते प्रायमुपविष्टास्तु दृष्ट्वा गृध्रं प्लवंगमाः।
चक्रुर्बुद्धिं तदा रौद्रां सर्वान् नो भक्षयिष्यति॥ २॥
verses.m: Seeing the vulture, the said monkeys, for their part, who had sat down to starve themselves to death, entertained the horrid idea that he would eat them all up. (2)

verses.text:
सर्वथा प्रायमासीनान् यदि नो भक्षयिष्यति।
कृतकृत्या भविष्यामः क्षिप्रं सिद्धिमितो गताः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “If he eats up us, who have sat down to fast till death, we shall have thoroughly accomplished our purpose, having attained speedy success (in the form of death) through this act of his.” (3)

verses.text:
एतां बुद्धिं ततश्चक्रुः सर्वे ते हरियूथपाः।
अवतार्य गिरेः शृङ्गाद् गृध्रमाहाङ्गदस्तदा॥ ४॥
verses.m: All those monkey leaders subsequently arrived at this latter conclusion. Having helped the vulture to descend from the mountain-peak, Aṅgada then spoke to the vulture as follows : (4)

verses.text:
बभूवर्क्षरजो नाम वानरेन्द्रः प्रतापवान्।
ममार्यः पार्थिवः पक्षिन् धार्मिकौ तस्य चात्मजौ॥ ५॥
सुग्रीवश्चैव वाली च पुत्रौ घनबलावुभौ।
लोके विश्रुतकर्माभूद् राजा वाली पिता मम॥ ६॥
verses.m: “There was a glorious lord of monkeys, King Ṛkṣrāja by name, my grandfather, O bird ! And he had two pious sons, Vālī and Sugrīva, sprung from his own loins, both possessed of great strength. My father, King Vālī, was well-known for his exploits in the world. (5-6)

verses.text:
राजा कृत्स्नस्य जगत इक्ष्वाकूणां महारथः।
रामो दाशरथिः श्रीमान् प्रविष्टो दण्डकावनम्॥ ७॥
लक्ष्मणेन सह भ्रात्रा वैदेह्या सह भार्यया।
पितुर्निदेशनिरतो धर्मं पन्थानमाश्रितः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “The sovereign of the whole earth and a great chariot warrior born in the line of the Ikṣwākus, and son of the late King Daśaratha, the glorious Rāma, who was wholly intent upon carrying out the command of his father and had taken to the path of virtue, entered the forest of Daṇḍaka with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, and consort, Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory). (7-8)

verses.text:
तस्य भार्या जनस्थानाद् रावणेन हृता बलात्।
रामस्य तु पितुर्मित्रं जटायुर्नाम गृध्रराट्॥ ९॥
ददर्श सीतां वैदेहीं ह्रियमाणां विहायसा।
रावणं विरथं कृत्वा स्थापयित्वा च मैथिलीम्।
परिश्रान्तश्च वृद्धश्च रावणेन हतो रणे॥ १०॥
verses.m: “His consort, Sītā, was forcibly borne away from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa. The king of vultures, Jaṭāyu by name, for his part, who was a friend of Śrī Rāmā’s father (Emperor Daśaratha), observed Sītā, a princess of the Videha territory, being borne away in an aerial car through the airspace. Having deprived Rāvaṇa of his aerial car by shattering it and placed Sītā (a princess of Mithilā) on the ground, Jaṭāyu, who had been completely exhausted and was aged too, was slain by Rāvaṇa in combat.(9-10)

verses.text:
एवं गृध्रो हतस्तेन रावणेन बलीयसा।
संस्कृतश्चापि रामेण जगाम गतिमुत्तमाम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “In this way the vulture, Jaṭāyu, was killed by the said Rāvaṇa, who was superior in might, and, having been cremated by Śrī Rāma, attained the highest destiny. (11)

verses.text:
ततो मम पितृव्येण सुग्रीवेण महात्मना।
चकार राघवः सख्यं सोऽवधीत् पितरं मम॥ १२॥
verses.m: “Then the celebrated Śrī Rāma contracted an alliance with my uncle, the high-souled Sugrīva, and killed my father (as a token of his friendship). (12)

verses.text:
मम पित्रा निरुद्धो हि सुग्रीवः सचिवैः सह।
निहत्य वालिनं रामस्ततस्तमभिषेचयत्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Since Sugrīva had been banished with his ministers by my father, Śrī Rāma forthwith installed him on the throne after killing Vālī. (13)

verses.text:
स राज्ये स्थापितस्तेन सुग्रीवो वानरेश्वरः।
राजा वानरमुख्यानां तेन प्रस्थापिता वयम्॥ १४॥
एवं रामप्रयुक्तास्तु मार्गमाणास्ततस्ततः।
वैदेहीं नाधिगच्छामो रात्रौ सूर्यप्रभामिव॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Installed on the throne as the lord of monkeys by Śrī Rāma, the aforesaid Sugrīva is now the ruler of all the monkey chiefs. Dispatched by him and directed by Śrī Rāma, and looking about here and there in this way, we could not find Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) any more than one would perceive the splendour of the sun at night. (14-15)

verses.text:
ते वयं दण्डकारण्यं विचिं त्य सुसमाहिताः।
अज्ञानात् तु प्रविष्टाः स्म धरण्या विवृतं बिलम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Having explored the Daṇḍaka forest most carefully, we, however, penetrated deeply through ignorance into a gaping hole in the ground. (16)

verses.text:
मयस्य मायाविहितं तद् बिलं च विचिन्वताम्।
व्यतीतस्तत्र नो मासो यो राज्ञा समयः कृतः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Nay, even as we were scouring that cavern constructed by the demon Maya by dint of his wonderful architectural skill, the period of one month appointed by the king, Sugrīva, as the time-limit for the search, slipped past us. (17)

verses.text:
ते वयं कपिराजस्य सर्वे वचनकारिणः।
कृतां संस्थामतिक्रान्ता भयात् प्रायमुपासिताः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “Having exceeded the time-limit fixed by the king, we all, who were engaged in carrying out the command of Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys), have sat down through fear to starve ourselves to death. (18)

verses.text:
क्रुद्धे तस्मिंस्तु काकुत्स्थे सुग्रीवे च सलक्ष्मणे।
गतानामपि सर्वेषां तत्र नो नास्ति जीवितम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “In the event of Śrī Rāma, a scion of Kākutstha, as well as Sugrīva with Lakṣmaṇa being angry, there is no hope of survival for us all even if we return to Kiṣkindhā.” (19)

verses.text:
इत्युक्तः करुणं वाक्यं वानरैस्त्यक्तजीवितैः।
सबाष्पो वानरान् गृध्रः प्रत्युवाच महास्वनः॥ १॥
verses.m: Spoken to in these pitiful words by the monkeys, who had given up all hope of their life, the vulture, full of tears, replied as follows to the monkeys in a loud voice : (1)

verses.text:
यवीयान् स मम भ्राता जटायुर्नाम वानराः।
यमाख्यात हतं युद्धे रावणेन बलीयसा॥ २॥
verses.m: “He was my younger brother, Jaṭāyu by name, O monkeys, whom you have spoken of as killed in an encounter by Rāvaṇa, who was superior in strength to him. (2)

verses.text:
वृद्धभावादपक्षत्वाच्छृण्वंस्तदपि मर्षये।
नहि मे शक्तिरस्त्यद्य भ्रातुर्वैरविमोक्षणे॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Due to old age and loss of my wings, I forbear even on hearing of it; for I have no more strength left in me to requite his mortal enmity towards my brother. (3)

verses.text:
पुरा वृत्रवधे वृत्ते स चाहं च जयैषिणौ।
आदित्यमुपयातौ स्वो ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्॥ ४॥
आवृत्याकाशमार्गेण जवेन स्वर्गतौ भृशम्।
मध्यं प्राप्ते तु सूर्ये तु जटायुरवसीदति॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Seeking to conquer Indra in the olden days, when the death of the demon Vṛtra had taken place at the hands of Indra, Jaṭāyu and myself too soared with inordinate speed through the airspace to heaven. Turning back from heaven after conquering him, we flew up still higher and drew near the sun encircled by its aureole of rays and illumining heaven. When, however, the sun reached the meridian, Jaṭāyu for his part began to grow faint. (4-5)

verses.text:
तमहं भ्रातरं दृष्ट्वा सूर्यरश्मिभिरर्दितम्।
पक्षाभ्यां छादयामास स्नेहात् परमविह्वलम्॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Seeing my aforesaid brother tormented by the sun’s rays and greatly unnerved, I covered him with my wings out of affection. (6)

verses.text:
निर्दग्धपत्रः पतितो विन्ध्येऽहं वानरर्षभाः।
अहमस्मिन् वसन् भ्रातुः प्रवृत्तिं नोपलक्षये॥ ७॥
verses.m: “My wings having been fully burnt, I dropped down on the Vindhyan range, O leaders of monkeys! Living on this mountain, as I did, I got no news of my brother,” (7)

verses.text:
जटायुषस्त्वेवमुक्तो भ्रात्रा सम्पातिना तदा।
युवराजो महाप्रज्ञः प्रत्युवाचाङ्गदस्तदा॥ ८॥
verses.m: Told thus by Sampāti, the brother of Jaṭāyu on that occassion, the highly intelligent Aṅgada, the Prince Regent of Kiṣkindhā, for his part, then replied as follows : (8)

verses.text:
जटायुषो यदि भ्राता श्रुतं ते गदितं मया।
आख्याहि यदि जानासि निलयं तस्य रक्षसः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “If you are the brother of Jaṭāyu and if you have listened to what has been narrated by me, please say if you know the abode of that ogre. (9)

verses.text:
अदीर्घदर्शिनं तं वै रावणं राक्षसाधमम्।
अन्तिके यदि वा दूरे यदि जानासि शंस नः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “If you actually know that short-sighted Rāvaṇa, the vilest of ogres, to be living near or far, please tell us.” (10)

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीन्महातेजा भ्राता ज्येष्ठो जटायुषः।
आत्मानुरूपं वचनं वानरान् सम्प्रहर्षयन्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Sampāti, the elder brother of Jaṭāyu, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, thereupon spoke the following words becoming of himself, bringing supreme delight to the monkeys thereby : (11)

verses.text:
निर्दग्धपक्षो गृध्रोऽहं गतवीर्यः प्लवङ्गमाः।
वाङ्मात्रेण तु रामस्य करिष्ये साह्यमुत्तमम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “A vulture whose wings have been entirely burnt and whose virility has departed for good, O monkeys, I would render foremost service to Śrī Rāma through you, who are engaged in his service, at least through my speech only. (12)

verses.text:
जानामि वारुणाँल्लोकान् विष्णोस्त्रैविक्रमानपि।
देवासुरविमर्दांश्च ह्यमृतस्य विमन्थनम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I have knowledge of the worlds presided over by Varuṇa (the god of water) as also those measured in three strides by Lord Viṣṇu (descended in the form of the Divine Dwarf and then assuming inordinate proportions). I am equally aware of the conflicts that took place between the gods and the demons and also how nectar was churned out of the ocean of milk. (13)

verses.text:
रामस्य यदिदं कार्यं कर्तव्यं प्रथमं मया।
जरया च हृतं तेजः प्राणाश्च शिथिला मम॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Even though my energy has been snatched away by old age and my vitality is ebbing, this errand of Śrī Rāma, which you have mentioned, must be accomplished by me first. (14)

verses.text:
तरुणी रूपसम्पन्ना सर्वाभरणभूषिता।
ह्रियमाणा मया दृष्टा रावणेन दुरात्मना॥ १५॥
क्रोशन्ती रामरामेति लक्ष्मणेति च भामिनी।
भूषणान्यपविध्यन्ती गात्राणि च विधुन्वती॥ १६॥
verses.m: “A Lovely young lady richly endowed with comeliness and adorned with all kinds of jewels was seen by me the other day crying out ‘Rāma !’, ‘O Rāma !’ ‘O Lakṣmaṇa, nay, dropping down her ornaments and tossing her limbs in her attempt to extricate herself while being borne away by the evil-minded Rāvaṇa. (15-16)

verses.text:
सूर्यप्रभेव शैलाग्रे तस्याः कौशेयमुत्तमम्।
असिते राक्षसे भाति यथा वा तडिदम्बुदे॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Her exquisite silken robe shone against the dark-complexioned ogre as the splendour of the sun against a mountain-peak or as a flash of lightning in the sky. (17)

verses.text:
तां तु सीतामहं मन्ये रामस्य परिकीर्तनात्।
श्रूयतां मे कथयतो निलयं तस्य रक्षसः॥ १८॥
verses.m: “From the fact that she was uttering the name of Rāma again and again, I believe her to have been Sītā without doubt. Now hear from me, as I speak, about the abode of that ogre. (18)

verses.text:
पुत्रो विश्रवसः साक्षाद् भ्राता वैश्रवणस्य च।
अध्यास्ते नगरीं लङ्कां रावणो नाम राक्षसः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “The son of Sage Viśravā himself and a (half-) brother of Kubera (son of Viśravā), the ogre, Rāvaṇa by name, lives in the city of Laṅkā. (19)

verses.text:
इतो द्वीपे समुद्रस्य सम्पूर्णे शतयोजने।
तस्मिँल्लङ्का पुरी रम्या निर्मिता विश्वकर्मणा॥ २०॥
जाम्बूनदमयैर्द्वारैश्चित्रैः काञ्चनवेदिकैः।
प्रासादैर्हेमवर्णैश्च महद्भिः सुसमाकृता॥ २१॥
प्राकारेणार्कवर्णेन महता च समन्विता।
तस्यां वसति वैदेही दीना कौशेयवासिनी॥ २२॥
रावणान्तःपुरे रुद्धा राक्षसीभिः सुरक्षिता।
जनकस्यात्मजां राज्ञस्तस्यां द्रक्ष्यथ मैथिलीम्॥ २३॥
verses.m: “On a well-known island in the sea, situated at a distance of full one hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles) from this shore, lies the lovely city of Laṅkā, constructed by Viśwakarmā (the architect of gods), abounding in wonderful gates of Jāmbūnada (gold found on the banks of the Jammu river) and stately mansions of golden hue with terraces of gold and enclosed by a massive fortification wall bright as the sun. “In that city lives the agonized Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory), clad in silk, confined in the gynaeceum of Rāvaṇa and strongly guarded by ogresses. There you will be able to see Sītā (a princess of Mithilā), daughter of King Janaka. (20—23)

verses.text:
लङ्कायामथ गुप्तायां सागरेण समन्ततः।
सम्प्राप्य सागरस्यान्तं सम्पूर्णं शतयोजनम्॥ २४॥
आसाद्य दक्षिणं तीरं ततो द्रक्ष्यथ रावणम्।
तत्रैव त्वरिताः क्षिप्रं विक्रमध्वं प्लवङ्गमाः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Duly reaching the end of the sea, which lies at a distance of a full hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles), and arriving at its southern coast you will be able to see after that Rāvaṇa in Laṅkā, protected by the sea on all sides. Reaching there expeditiously show your valour soon, O monkeys ! (24-25)

verses.text:
ज्ञानेन खलु पश्यामि दृष्ट्वा प्रत्यागमिष्यथ।
आद्यः पन्थाः कुलिङ्गानां ये चान्ये धान्यजीविनः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “I perceive through intuition that you will indeed be able to return after seeing Sītā. The first shortest flight in point of height is that of sparrows and other birds who live on grain. (26)

verses.text:
द्वितीयो बलिभोजानां ये च वृक्षफलाशनाः।
भासास्तृतीयं गच्छन्ति क्रौञ्चाश्च कुररैः सह॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The second, in order of height, is that of birds such as crows living on fragments of food left at a meal and those such as parrots that subsist on the fruits of trees. Bhāsas and herons as well as ospreys take a flight which is third in order of height. (27)

verses.text:
श्येनाश्चतुर्थं गच्छन्ति गृध्रा गच्छन्ति पञ्चमम्।
बलवीर्योपपन्नानां रूपयौवनशालिनाम्॥ २८॥
षष्ठस्तु पन्था हंसानां वैनतेयगतिः परा।
वैनतेयाच्च नो जन्म सर्वेषां वानरर्षभाः॥ २९॥
verses.m: “Hawks take a flight which is fourth in order of height; while vultures take a flight which is fifth in order of height. The sixth in order of height is the flight of swans endowed with strength and virility and graced with comeliness and youth; while the flight of Garuḍa (son of Vinatā) is the highest. We all vultures claim our descent from Aruṇa, the younger son of Vinatā, O leaders of monkeys ! (28-29)

verses.text:
गर्हितं तु कृतं कर्म येन स्म पिशिताशिनः।
प्रतिकार्यं च मे तस्य वैरं भ्रातृकृतं भवेत्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “The enmity shown towards my brother, Jaṭāyu, by that ogre (lit., one who feeds on raw flesh), by whom the execrable act in the shape of Sītā’s abduction was actually perpetrated, remains to be repaid by me, which will be automatically done through your agency. (30)

verses.text:
इहस्थोऽहं प्रपश्यामि रावणं जानकीं तथा।
अस्माकमपि सौपर्णं दिव्यं चक्षुर्बलं तथा॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Standing here I vividly perceive Rāvaṇa and Sītā (daughter of Janaka). We also possess the supersensuous vision of Garuḍa of charming wings. (31)

verses.text:
तस्मादाहारवीर्येण निसर्गेण च वानराः।
आयोजनशतात् साग्राद् वयं पश्याम नित्यशः॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Therefore, through the potency of our food and by virtue of our nature (as descendants of Vinatā) we can always see to a distance of more than one hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles), O monkeys ! (32)

verses.text:
अस्माकं विहिता वृत्तिर्निसर्गेण च दूरतः।
विहिता वृक्षमूले तु वृत्तिश्चरणयोधिनाम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Moreover, our sustenance has been ordained by Nature with food seen at a distance, while that of cocks (lit., birds contending with their claws) has been ordained with food obtained at the foot of a tree. (33)

verses.text:
उपायो दृश्यतां कश्चिल्लङ्घने लवणाम्भसः।
अभिगम्य तु वैदेहीं समृद्धार्था गमिष्यथ॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Some means may be found out to cross the sea (of brackish waters). Having met Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) you will surely return to Kiṣkindhā, fully accomplished of purpose. (34)

verses.text:
समुद्रं नेतुमिच्छामि भवद्भिर्वरुणालयम्।
प्रदास्याम्युदकं भ्रातुः स्वर्गतस्य महात्मनः॥ ३५॥
verses.m: “I wish myself to be taken by you to the sea, the abode of Varuṇa (the god of water). I will duly offer water to the spirit of my high-souled younger brother, Jaṭāyu, who has ascended to heaven.” (35)

verses.text:
ततो नीत्वा तु तं देशं तीरे नदनदीपतेः।
निर्दग्धपक्षं सम्पातिं वानराः सुमहौजसः॥ ३६॥
तं पुनः प्रापयित्वा च तं देशं पतगेश्वरम्।
बभूवुर्वानरा हृष्टाः प्रवृत्तिमुपलभ्य ते॥ ३७॥
verses.m: Actually taking Sampāti, whose wings had been completely burnt, to the aforesaid region lying on the shore of the ocean (the lord of rivers and streams), and then, after he had offered water to the spirit of his younger brother, taking the said king of birds back to the same place where he lived, the aforesaid monkeys, who were endowed with extraordinary energy, felt rejoiced to receive the information regarding Rāvaṇa and Sītā. (36-37)

verses.text:
ततस्तदमृतास्वादं गृध्रराजेन भाषितम्।
निशम्य वदता हृष्टास्ते वचः प्लवगर्षभाः॥ १॥
verses.m: The aforesaid leaders of monkeys were delighted to hear the words, sweet as nectar, uttered by the king of vultures, even as he spoke to them. (1)

verses.text:
जाम्बवान् वानरश्रेष्ठः सह सर्वैः प्लवङ्गमैः।
भूतलात् सहसोत्थाय गृध्रराजानमब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Rising from the ground all at once alongwith all the monkeys, Jāmbavān, the foremost of all monkeys and bears, spoke as follows to Sampāti, the king of vultures : (2)

verses.text:
क्व सीता केन वा दृष्टा को वा हरति मैथिलीम्।
तदाख्यातु भवान् सर्वं गतिर्भव वनौकसाम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Where is Sītā and by whom was she seen? And who abducted the princess of Mithilā? Pray, relate all that and prove to be an asylum for the monkeys and bears (lit., dwellers in the woods). (3)

verses.text:
को दाशरथिबाणानां वज्रवेगनिपातिनाम्।
स्वयं लक्ष्मणमुक्तानां न चिन्तयति विक्रमम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Who is it that does not mind the might of the arrows of Śrī Rāma (son of Daśaratha), which rush with the speed of lightning, as well as of those discharged by Lakṣmaṇa himself?” (4)

verses.text:
स हरीन् प्रतिसम्मुक्तान् सीताश्रुतिसमाहितान्।
पुनराश्वासयन् प्रीत इदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ५॥
verses.m: Consoling once more the monkeys, who had now totally given up the vow of starving themselves to death and were all attention to hear more about Sītā, Sampāti joyously made the following reply : (5)

verses.text:
श्रूयतामिह वैदेह्या यथा मे हरणं श्रुतम्।
येन चापि ममाख्यातं यत्र चायतलोचना॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Hear how the abduction of Sītā (a princess of the Videha territory) was heard of by me here and also by whom the story was related to me, and where the large-eyed lady is. (6)

verses.text:
अहमस्मिन् गिरौ दुर्गे बहुयोजनमायते।
चिरान्निपतितो वृद्धः क्षीणप्राणपराक्रमः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Long ago I fell on this mountain, which is difficult of access and is many Yojanas in extent. I am now old and find my vitality and prowess, too, depleted. (7)

verses.text:
तं मामेवंगतं पुत्रः सुपार्श्वो नाम नामतः।
आहारेण यथाकालं बिभर्ति पततां वरः॥ ८॥
verses.m: “My own son, well-known by the name of Supārśwa, the foremost of birds, nourished me with food at regular hours when I was reduced to this plight. (8)

verses.text:
तीक्ष्णकामास्तु गन्धर्वास्तीक्ष्णकोपा भुजङ्गमाः।
मृगाणां तु भयं तीक्ष्णं ततस्तीक्ष्णक्षुधा वयम्॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Ardent is the longing of Gandharvas (celestial musicians) for women and violent is the anger of serpents. Intense is the fear of antelopes, while we, birds, are noted more than the latter for our keen appetite. (9)

verses.text:
स कदाचित् क्षुधार्तस्य ममाहाराभिकांक्षिणः।
गतसूर्येऽहनि प्राप्तो मम पुत्रो ह्यनामिषः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “One day, my aforesaid son came to me actually without any flesh at an hour of the day when the sun had actually set; while I was tormented with hunger and was ardently longing for food. (10)

verses.text:
स मयाऽऽहारसंरोधात् पीडितः प्रीतिवर्धनः।
अनुमान्य यथातत्त्वमिदं वचनमब्रवीत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Honouring me when stung by me with harsh words for withholding food from me, Supārśwa, who heightened my joy on meeting me, made the following reply, which was in consonance with facts : (11)

verses.text:
अहं तात यथाकालमामिषार्थी खमाप्लुतः।
महेन्द्रस्य गिरेर्द्वारमावृत्य सुसमाश्रितः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “ ‘Having flown into the air in quest of flesh in time I stationed myself blocking the approach to the Mahendra mountain, O dear father ! (12)

verses.text:
तत्र सत्त्वसहस्राणां सागरान्तरचारिणाम्।
पन्थानमेकोऽध्यवसं संनिरोद्धुमवाङ्मुखः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “ ‘I stayed there alone, head downwards, with a view to obstructing completely the passage of thousands of creatures living in the sea. (13)

verses.text:
तत्र कश्चिन्मया दृष्टः सूर्योदयसमप्रभाम्।
स्त्रियमादाय गच्छन् वै भिन्नाञ्जनचयोपमः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “ ‘On that occasion was seen by me someone looking like a mass of collyrium, actually carrying a lady bright as the dawn. (14)

verses.text:
सोऽहमभ्यवहारार्थं तौ दृष्ट्वा कृतनिश्चयः।
तेन साम्ना विनीतेन पन्थानमनुयाचितः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “ ‘Seeing them, I resolved to seize them for your food. By him, however, I was asked for a passage in gentle words and in a submissive demeanour. (15)

verses.text:
नहि सामोपपन्नानां प्रहर्ता विद्यते भुवि।
नीचेष्वपि जनः कश्चित् किमङ्ग बत मद्विधः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “ ‘Indeed there is no creature on earth, even among the vile, who would strike those armed with conciliatory words; how, then, can a creature like myself do so, O dear father? (16)

verses.text:
स यातस्तेजसा व्योम संक्षिपन्निव वेगितः।
अथाहं खेचरैर्भूतैरभिगम्य सभाजितः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “ ‘He hurriedly passed on enveloping the sky as it were with splendour. Thereupon I was met and felicitated by living beings coursing in the air. (17)

verses.text:
दिष्ट्या जीवति सीतेति ह्यब्रुवन् मां महर्षयः।
कथंचित् सकलत्रोऽसौ गतस्ते स्वस्त्यसंशयम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Eminent sages actually said to me : By good luck Sītā is still alive; again it is undoubtedly well for you that the fellow somehow left with that lady without doing any harm to you. (18)

verses.text:
एवमुक्तस्ततोऽहं तैः सिद्धैः परमशोभनैः।
स च मे रावणो राजा रक्षसां प्रतिवेदितः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘After he had left I was spoken to as aforesaid by those highly glorious Siddhas. Nay, the fellow was further pointed out to have been no other than Rāvaṇa, the king of ogres. (19)

verses.text:
पश्यन् दाशरथेर्भार्यां रामस्य जनकात्मजाम्।
भ्रष्टाभरणकौशेयां शोकवेगपराजिताम्॥ २०॥
रामलक्ष्मणयोर्नाम क्रोशन्तीं मुक्तमूर्धजाम्।
एष कालात्ययस्तात इति वाक्यविदां वरः॥ २१॥
एतदर्थं समग्रं मे सुपार्श्वः प्रत्यवेदयत्।
तच्छ्रुत्वापि हि मे बुद्धिर्नासीत् काचित् पराक्रमे॥ २२॥
अपक्षो हि कथं पक्षी कर्म किंचित् समारभेत्।
यत् तु शक्यं मया कर्तुं वाग्बुद्धिगुणवर्तिना॥ २३॥
श्रूयतां तत्र वक्ष्यामि भवतां पौरुषाश्रयम्।
वाङ् मतिभ्यां हि सर्वेषां करिष्यामि प्रियं हि वः॥ २४॥
verses.m: “ ‘I remained looking on the consort of Śrī Rāma, son of Daśaratha, and daughter of Janaka, whose jewels had dropped from her person and whose silk covering had slipped from over her head, nay, who had been overcome with vehemence of grief and who was calling loudly the names of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, her hair dishevelled. This is how the time passed, O dear father !’ So did Supārśwa, the foremost of masters of expression, convey all this information to me. Even after actually hearing it the idea of showing valour did not occur to me at all. Indeed how can a bird shorn of its wings undertake to do anything? I, however, shall tell you something which can be done in that behalf by me, used as I am to helping others with my speech and understanding, but the execution of which depends entirely on your prowess. Surely, I will do with my word and intellect that which is really agreeable to you. (20—24)

verses.text:
यद्धि दाशरथेः कार्यं मम तन्नात्र संशयः।
तद् भवन्तो मतिश्रेष्ठा बलवन्तो मनस्विनः॥ २५॥
प्रहिताः कपिराजेन देवैरपि दुरासदाः।
रामलक्ष्मणबाणाश्च विहिताः कङ्कपत्रिणः॥ २६॥
त्रयाणामपि लोकानां पर्याप्तास्त्राणनिग्रहे।
कामं खलु दशग्रीवस्तेजोबलसमन्वितः।
भवतां तु समर्थानां न किंचिदपि दुष्करम्॥ २७॥
verses.m: “For that which is the concern of Śrī Rāma (a son of Daśaratha) is equally my concern: there is no doubt about it. You are pre-eminent in point of intelligence, mighty, high-minded and difficult to assail even for gods. Hence you have been dispatched here by Sugrīva (the ruler of monkeys). The shafts of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, which have been evolved by the creator himself and are furnished with the plumes of a buzzard, are adequate to protect or subdue all the three worlds. Granted that Rāvaṇa (the ten-headed monster) is, truly speaking, fully endowed with energy and bodily strength; nothing whatsoever is, however, difficult to accomplish for you, powerful as you are. (25—27)

verses.text:
तदलं कालसङ्गेन क्रियतां बुद्धिनिश्चयः।
नहि कर्मसु सज्जन्ते बुद्धिमन्तो भवद्विधाः॥ २८॥
verses.m: “Therefore, there should be no more loss of time; let your mind be made up soon to do your best to find out Sītā. For, intelligent people like you do not lag behind in their undertakings.” (28)

verses.text:
ततः कृतोदकं स्नातं तं गृध्रं हरियूथपाः।
उपविष्टा गिरौ रम्ये परिवार्य समन्ततः॥ १॥
verses.m: The monkey chiefs now sat on the lovely mountain encompassing on all sides the vulture, Sampāti, who had offered water to the spirit of his deceased brother and taken his bath. (1)

verses.text:
तमङ्गदमुपासीनं तैः सर्वैर्हरिभिर्वृतम्।
जनितप्रत्ययो हर्षात् सम्पातिः पुनरब्रवीत्॥ २॥
verses.m: Having inspired confidence in the monkeys, Sampāti joyously spoke once more to the celebrated Aṅgada, who was sitting close by, surrounded by all those monkeys : (2)

verses.text:
कृत्वा निःशब्दमेकाग्राः शृण्वन्तु हरयो मम।
तथ्यं संकीर्तयिष्यामि यथा जानामि मैथिलीम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Let all the monkeys listen to me attentively, observing complete silence. I will narrate in detail the truth as to how I came to know of Sītā, the princess of Mithilā. (3)

verses.text:
अस्य विन्ध्यस्य शिखरे पतितोऽस्मि पुरानघ।
सूर्यतापपरीताङ्गो निर्दग्धः सूर्यरश्मिभिः॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Scorched by the rays of the sun, all my limbs overpowered by the sun’s heat, I fell in the former days on a summit of this Vindhyan range, O sinless ones ! (4)

verses.text:
लब्धसंज्ञस्तु षड्रात्राद् विवशो विह्वलन्निव।
वीक्षमाणो दिशः सर्वा नाभिजानामि किंचन॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Having regained consciousness after six nights, I for my part stood looking all-round, powerless and fainting as it were, but could not distinguish anything. (5)

verses.text:
ततस्तु सागराञ्शैलान् नदीः सर्वाः सरांसि च।
वनानि च प्रदेशांश्च निरीक्ष्य मतिरागता॥ ६॥
verses.m: “Then on scanning the seas and rocks, all the rivers and lakes, woods and the parts of the country, however, memory returned to me. (6)

verses.text:
हृष्टपक्षिगणाकीर्णः कन्दरोदरकूटवान्।
दक्षिणस्योदधेस्तीरे विन्ध्योऽयमिति निश्चितः॥ ७॥
verses.m: “It was eventually concluded to be no other than the Vindhya mountain on the shore of the southern sea—a mountain which is crowded with flocks of joyous birds and contains caves in its flanks and a number of peaks. (7)•

verses.text:
आसीच्चात्राश्रमं पुण्यं सुरैरपि सुपूजितम्।
ऋषिर्निशाकरो नाम यस्मिन्नुग्रतपाऽभवत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Again, here there was a holy hermitage, highly adored even by gods, in which dwelt a Ṛṣi (a seer of Vedic Mantras) named Niśākara, noted for his rigorous austerities. (8)

verses.text:
अष्टौ वर्षसहस्राणि तेनास्मिन्नृषिणा गिरौ।
वसतो मम धर्मज्ञे स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Even after Sage Niśākara, who knew what is right, had ascended to heaven, eight thousand years slipped past me as I lived on this mountain without this Ṛṣi. (9)

verses.text:
अवतीर्य च विन्ध्याग्रात् कृच्छ्रेण विषमाच्छनैः।
तीक्ष्णदर्भां वसुमतीं दुःखेन पुनरागतः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Descending slowly and painfully from the rugged peak of the Vindhya mountain (on regaining consciousness after my fall from the sky) I then reached with difficulty a plain bristling with sharp-pointed blades of the sacred Kuśa grass. (10)

verses.text:
तमृषिं द्रष्टुकामोऽस्मि दुःखेनाभ्यागतो भृशम्।
जटायुषा मया चैव बहुशोऽधिगतो हि सः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Eager to see the aforesaid Ṛṣi I arrived there with great hardship; for he had been visited by Jaṭāyu and myself on many an occasion in the past. (11)

verses.text:
तस्याश्रमपदाभ्याशे ववुर्वाताः सुगन्धिनः।
वृक्षो नापुष्पितः कश्चिदफलो वा न दृश्यते॥ १२॥
verses.m: “In the neighbourhood of the site of that hermitage fragrant breezes blew. No tree without blossom or fruit could be seen there. (12)

verses.text:
उपेत्य चाश्रमं पुण्यं वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः।
द्रष्टुकामः प्रतीक्षे च भगवन्तं निशाकरम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nay, approaching the holy hermitage I took shelter at the foot of a tree and waited there, keen as I was to see the venerable Sage, Niśākara. (13)

verses.text:
अथ पश्यामि दूरस्थमृषिं ज्वलिततेजसम्।
कृताभिषेकं दुर्धर्षमुपावृत्तमुदङ् मुखम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Presently I beheld at a distance the sage of dazzling brilliance, who could not easily be disregarded, returning with his face turned towards the north having taken his bath in the sea. (14)

verses.text:
तमृक्षाः सृमरा व्याघ्राः सिंहा नानासरीसृपाः।
परिवार्योपगच्छन्ति दातारं प्राणिनो यथा॥ १५॥
verses.m: “Bears, Sṛmaras (a species of deer), tigers, lions and serpents of various kinds followed, surrounding him on all sides as supplicants would follow a donor. (15)

verses.text:
ततः प्राप्तमृषिं ज्ञात्वा तानि सत्त्वानि वै ययुः।
प्रविष्टे राजनि यथा सर्वं सामात्यकं बलम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Then finding the sage having reached the hermitage, the aforesaid animals left immediately for their dens, even as on a king retiring into his palace the whole army escorting him, alongwith the ministers, disperses. (16)

verses.text:
ऋषिस्तु दृष्ट्वा मां तुष्टः प्रविष्टश्चाश्रमं पुनः।
मुहूर्तमात्रान्निर्गम्य ततः कार्यमपृच्छत॥ १७॥
verses.m: “The Ṛṣi was pleased to behold me and retired into his hermitage. Coming out, however, once more after an hour or so, he then inquired of me the purpose of my visit. (17)

verses.text:
सौम्य वैकल्यतां दृष्ट्वा रोम्णां ते नावगम्यते।
अग्निदग्धाविमौ पक्षौ प्राणाश्चापि शरीरके॥ १८॥
verses.m: “He said: ‘Seeing the disappearance of your feathers I could not recognize you, O gentle one ! These wings of yours have also been burnt with fire and even so the vitality as well as the strength and prowess too in your frail frame stand well-nigh consumed. (18)

verses.text:
गृध्रौ द्वौ दृष्टपूर्वौ मे मातरिश्वसमौ जवे।
गृध्राणां चैव राजानौ भ्रातरौ कामरूपिणौ॥ १९॥
verses.m: “Two vultures, related as brothers to each other, the rulers of vultures, who vied with the wind in speed and were capable of changing form at will, were seen by me before. (19)

verses.text:
ज्येष्ठोऽवितस्त्वं सम्पाते जटायुरनुजस्तव।
मानुषं रूपमास्थाय गृह्णीतां चरणौ मम॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Assuming human forms, you, who stand recognized by me as the elder of the two, O Sampāti, and Jaṭāyu, your younger brother, used to clasp my feet as a token of respect. (20)

verses.text:
किं ते व्याधिसमुत्थानं पक्षयोः पतनं कथम्।
दण्डो वायं धृतः केन सर्वमाख्याहि पृच्छतः॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Is this a symptom of some disease appearing in your body? How is the falling off of your wings to be accounted for? Or by whom has this punishment been inflicted on you? Relate everything to me, who makes this inquiry of you.” (21)

verses.text:
ततस्तद् दारुणं कर्म दुष्करं सहसा कृतम्।
आचचक्षे मुनेः सर्वं सूर्यानुगमनं तथा॥ १॥
verses.m: Thereupon Sampāti related in the following words to the sage Niśākara all about that impetuous act (in the form of discomfiting Indra), which was so hard to accomplish and had been rashly undertaken, as also about their wild goose chase after the sun : (1)

verses.text:
भगवन् व्रणयुक्तत्वाल्लज्जया चाकुलेन्द्रियः।
परिश्रान्तो न शक्नोमि वचनं परिभाषितुम्॥ २॥
verses.m: “Due to my being afflicted with wounds inflicted by the thunderbolt of Indra and my mind being confused through shame (at my humiliation and frustration that followed in the wake of my chasing the sun) and exhausted by my arduous journey to your hermitage, I cannot narrate my story at length. O venerable sage ! (2)

verses.text:
अहं चैव जटायुश्च संघर्षाद् गर्वमोहितौ।
आकाशं पतितौ दूराज्जिज्ञासन्तौ पराक्रमम्॥ ३॥
कैलासशिखरे बद्ध्वा मुनीनामग्रतः पणम्।
रविः स्यादनुयातव्यो यावदस्तं महागिरिम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Having taken a vow on a peak of Mount Kailāsa in the presence of hermits that the sun must be followed till it reached the huge Western Mountain (where the sun is supposed to set), Jaṭāyu, my younger brother, and myself too, who were anxious to test our relative strength, infatuated as we were with pride (occasioned by our having worsted Indra in an encounter), flew far into the sky in a spirit of emulation. (3-4)

verses.text:
अप्यावां युगपत् प्राप्तावपश्याव महीतले।
रथचक्रप्रमाणानि नगराणि पृथक् पृथक्॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Nay, having reached the sky together, we distinctly perceived cities on the earth’s surface, equal in size to the wheel of a chariot. (5)

verses.text:
क्वचिद् वादित्रघोषश्च क्वचिद् भूषणनिःस्वनः।
गायन्तीः स्माङ्गना बह्वीः पश्यावो रक्तवाससः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “In one region of the sky was heard the sound of musical instruments, while in another could be heard the jingling of ornaments. In a third region we found singing numerous young ladies clad in red. (6)

verses.text:
तूर्णमुत्पत्य चाकाशमादित्यपदमास्थितौ।
आवामालोकयावस्तद् वनं शाद्वलसंस्थितम्॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Nay, speedily rising above the region immediately below the path of the sun and having reached the path of the sun, we found the forest below looking like a grassy plot. (7)

verses.text:
उपलैरिव संछन्ना दृश्यते भूः शिलोच्चयैः।
आपगाभिश्च संवीता सूत्रैरिव वसुंधरा॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Thickly covered with mountains, the earth looked as though strewn with pebbles; nay, surrounded by rivers, the terrestrial globe appeared entwined with threads. (8)

verses.text:
हिमवांश्चैव विन्ध्यश्च मेरुश्च सुमहागिरिः।
भूतले सम्प्रकाशन्ते नागा इव जलाशये॥ ९॥
verses.m: “The Himalayan range as well as the Vindhyan range and the huge mountain Meru too vividly appeared on the earth’s surface as so many elephants in a pond. (9)

verses.text:
तीव्रः स्वेदश्च खेदश्च भयं चासीत् तदावयोः।
समाविशत मोहश्च ततो मूर्च्छा च दारुणा॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Intense perspiration and fatigue as well as fear presently came upon us. Nay, confusion and then violent unconsciousness too overcame us. (10)

verses.text:
न च दिग् ज्ञायते याम्या न चाग्नेयी न वारुणी।
युगान्ते नियतो लोको हतो दग्ध इवाग्निना॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Neither the southern quarter presided over by Yama, the god of retribution, nor the south-eastern corner presided over by the god of fire nor again the western quarter presided over by Varuṇa (the god of water) could be distinguished between. The world, which is governed by laws of nature and could not perish before the appointed time, seemed to have been consumed by fire as at the time of universal destruction (lit., the end of a Kalpa or cycle). (11)

verses.text:
मनश्च मे हतं भूयश्चक्षुः प्राप्य तु संश्रयम्।
यत्नेन महता ह्यस्मिन् मनः संधाय चक्षुषी॥ १२॥
यत्नेन महता भूयो भास्करः प्रतिलोकितः।
तुल्य पृथ्वीप्रमाणेन भास्करः प्रतिभाति नौ॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Nay, falling back upon the sense of vision as its medium, my mind for its part got lost (due to the failure of my vision). Fixing once more my mind and eyes on the sun with great effort, of course, the sun could at least be seen with great effort. The sun appeared to us to be equal in size to the earth. (12-13)

verses.text:
जटायुर्मामनापृच्छ्य निपपात महीं ततः।
तं दृष्ट्वा तूर्णमाकाशादात्मानं मुक्तवानहम्॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Without taking leave of me, Jaṭāyu then descended to the earth. Seeing him descend, I too speedily let myself fall from the sky. (14)

verses.text:
पक्षाभ्यां च मया गुप्तो जटायुर्न प्रदह्यत।
प्रमादात् तत्र निर्दग्धः पतन् वायुपथादहम्॥ १५॥
आशङ्के तं निपतितं जनस्थाने जटायुषम्।
अहं तु पतितो विन्ध्ये दग्धपक्षो जडीकृतः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Having been protected by me with my wings, Jaṭāyu was not burnt; I, however; got my wings badly burnt at that time due to my recklessness. While falling down from the sky I suspected Jaṭāyu to have dropped somewhere in Janasthāna; while I fell down unconscious on the Vindhyan range, my wings having been burnt. (15-16)

verses.text:
राज्याच्च हीनो भ्रात्रा च पक्षाभ्यां विक्रमेण च।
सर्वथा मर्तुमेवेच्छन् पतिष्ये शिखराद् गिरेः॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Deprived of my rulership of the feathered kingdom and my brother, and shorn of my wings and prowess, and, therefore, seeking death alone under all circumstances, I will fall down from a mountain-peak.” (17)

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठमरुदं भृशदुःखितः।
अथ ध्यात्वा मुहूर्तं च भगवानिदमब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: “Having submitted to Niśākara, the foremost of sages, as above, I fell asobbing, sore distressed as I was. Reflecting a while, the venerable sage, however, spoke as follows : (1)

verses.text:
पक्षौ च ते प्रपक्षौ च पुनरन्यौ भविष्यतः।
चक्षुषी चैव प्राणाश्च विक्रमश्च बलं च ते॥ २॥
verses.m: “ ‘You will get back other pair of wings as well as vision and renewed vitality as also valour and strength too. (2)

verses.text:
पुराणे सुमहत्कार्यं भविष्यं हि मया श्रुतम्।
दृष्टं मे तपसा चैव श्रुत्वा च विदितं मम॥ ३॥
verses.m: “ ‘It has actually been heard by me (predicted) in the old traditional history that a very remarkable event is going to take place in future. It has not only been learnt by me through hearsay but also foreseen by me by virtue of my asceticism. (3)

verses.text:
राजा दशरथो नाम कश्चिदिक्ष्वाकुवर्धनः।
तस्य पुत्रो महातेजा रामो नाम भविष्यति॥ ४॥
verses.m: “There will be a certain king, Daśaratha by name, the promoter of Ikṣwāku’s race. A son, Rāma by name, endowed with extraordinary energy, will be born to him. (4)

verses.text:
अरण्यं च सह भ्रात्रा लक्ष्मणेन गमिष्यति।
तस्मिन्नर्थे नियुक्तः सन् पित्रा सत्यपराक्रमः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “Called upon by his father to do so, Śrī Rāma of unfailing prowess will proceed to the forest with his younger brother, Lakṣmaṇa, and his consort, Sītā. (5)

verses.text:
नैर्ऋतो रावणो नाम तस्य भार्यां हरिष्यति।
राक्षसेन्द्रो जनस्थाने अवध्यः सुरदानवैः॥ ६॥
verses.m: “ ‘An ogre (lit., One born in the line of Nirṛti, the deity presiding over the south-east), Rāvaṇa by name, the ruler of ogres, incapable of being slain by gods and demons alike, will carry off his consort, Sītā, in Janasthāna. (6)

verses.text:
सा च कामैः प्रलोभ्यन्ती भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैश्च मैथिली।
न भोक्ष्यति महाभागा दुःखमग्ना यशस्विनी॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Plunged in sorrow, the illustrious and highly blessed Sītā, a princess of Mithilā, however, will not partake of anything, even though tempted with offers of dishes—worth coveting—requiring mastication and those which can be easily gulped. (7)

verses.text:
परमान्नं च वैदेह्या ज्ञात्वा दास्यति वासवः।
यदन्नममृतप्रख्यं सुराणामपि दुर्लभम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: “Learning of this, Indra (the ruler of gods) will offer (through his messenger Mātali, a dish of) milk boiled with rice and sugar, a dish which will be like ambrosia and difficult to get even for gods. (8)

verses.text:
तदन्नं मैथिली प्राप्य विज्ञायेन्द्रादिदं त्विति।
अग्रमुद्धृत्य रामाय भूतले निर्वपिष्यति॥ ९॥
यदि जीवति मे भर्ता लक्ष्मणो वापि देवरः।
देवत्वं गच्छतोर्वापि तयोरन्नमिदं त्विति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “Receiving that dish and taking out the foremost part of it on coming to know for certain that it has come from Indra, Sītā (a princess of Mithilā) for her part will pour it on the ground as an offering to Śrī Rāma, saying: ‘If my husband or even Lakṣmaṇa, my brother-in-law, is alive, or even if they have attained the celestial state, let this food actually reach them.’ (9-10)

verses.text:
एष्यन्ति प्रेषितास्तत्र रामदूताः प्लवङ्गमाः।
आख्येया राममहिषी त्वया तेभ्यो विहङ्गम॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Dispatched as messengers of Śrī Rāma, monkeys will arrive on that spot. To them, O bird, the information about Sītā (the consort of Śrī Rāma) should be communicated by you. (11)

verses.text:
सर्वथा तु न गन्तव्यमीदृशः क्व गमिष्यसि।
देशकालौ प्रतीक्षस्व पक्षौ त्वं प्रतिपत्स्यसे॥ १२॥
verses.m: “On no account, however, should you venture out. Where can you go in this state? Wait for a suitable place and time, you will recover your wings. (12)

verses.text:
उत्सहेयमहं कर्तुमद्यैव त्वां सपक्षकम्।
इहस्थस्त्वं हि लोकानां हितं कार्यं करिष्यसि॥ १३॥
verses.m: “I can furnish you with wings this very day. (But in that case you will fly away to some other place). Continuing here, however, you will do a friendly act of service to mankind by enabling Śrī Rāma to trace out Sītā and kill Rāvaṇa, a sworn enemy of mankind. (13)

verses.text:
त्वयापि खलु तत् कार्यं तयोश्च नृपपुत्रयोः।
ब्राह्मणानां गुरूणां च मुनीनां वासवस्य च॥ १४॥
verses.m: “Indeed it is your duty too to render the aforesaid service to those two princes (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa), to the Brāhmaṇas as well as to your teachers (viz., ourselves) and other hermits as also to Indra, inasmuch as the interests of all these, including yourself, will be served by it. (14)

verses.text:
इच्छाम्यहमपि द्रष्टुं भ्रातरौ रामलक्ष्मणौ।
नेच्छे चिरं धारयितुं प्राणांस्त्यक्ष्ये कलेवरम्।
महर्षिस्त्वब्रवीदेवं दृष्टतत्त्वार्थदर्शनः॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I too long to see the two brothers, Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa; yet I do not wish to preserve my life for a long time and will cast off my body.” Thus spoke the great Ṛṣi Niśākara, who had for his part realized the substance forming the Reality (viz., Brahma) and mastered the Veda (which enables one to realize It). (15)

verses.text:
एतैरन्यैश्च बहुभिर्वाक्यैर्वाक्यविशारदः।
मां प्रशस्याभ्यनुज्ञाप्य प्रविष्टः स स्वमालयम्॥ १॥
verses.m: “Having extolled me in the forgoing and many other such words and taking leave of me, the sage, who was a master of expression, retired into his abode. (1)

verses.text:
कन्दरात् तु विसर्पित्वा पर्वतस्य शनैः शनैः।
अहं विन्ध्यं समारुह्य भवतः प्रतिपालये॥ २॥
verses.m: “Crawling from the mountain-cave and climbing up the Vindhyan range, I have been waiting for you all. (2)

verses.text:
अद्य त्वेतस्य कालस्य वर्षं साग्रशतं गतम्।
देशकालप्रतीक्षोऽस्मि हृदि कृत्वा मुनेर्वचः॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Since then more than eight thousand* years have elapsed till this day. Bearing in mind the sage’s words I have been waiting for the predicted place and time. (3)

verses.text:
महाप्रस्थानमासाद्य स्वर्गते तु निशाकरे।
मां निर्दहति संतापो वितर्कैर्बहुभिर्वृतम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “Sage Niśākara for his part having ascended to heaven on reaching the end of his life, agony has been consuming me, beset as I am with numerous doubts. (4)

verses.text:
उदितां मरणे बुद्धिं मुनिवाक्यैर्निवर्तये।
बुद्धिर्या तेन मे दत्ता प्राणानां रक्षणे मम॥ ५॥
सा मेऽपनयते दुःखं दीप्तेवाग्निशिखा तमः।
बुध्यता च मया वीर्यं रावणस्य दुरात्मनः॥ ६॥
पुत्रः संतर्जितो वाग्भिर्न त्राता मैथिली कथम्।
तस्या विलपितं श्रुत्वा तौ च सीतावियोजितौ॥ ७॥
न मे दशरथस्नेहात् पुत्रेणोत्पादितं प्रियम्।
तस्य त्वेवं ब्रुवाणस्य संहतैर्वानरैः सह॥ ८॥
उत्पेततुस्तदा पक्षौ समक्षं वनचारिणाम्।
स दृष्ट्वा स्वां तनुं पक्षैरुद्गतैररुणच्छदैः॥ ९॥
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे वानरांश्चेदमब्रवीत्।
निशाकरस्य राजर्षेः प्रसादादमितौजसः॥ १०॥
आदित्यरश्मिनिर्दग्धौ पक्षौ पुनरुपस्थितौ।
यौवने वर्तमानस्य ममासीद् यः पराक्रमः॥ ११॥
तमेवाद्यावगच्छामि बलं पौरुषमेव च।
सर्वथा क्रियतां यत्नः सीतामधिगमिष्यथ॥ १२॥
verses.m: “I have been setting aside the thought of suicide, which now and then appeared in me, by recalling the words of the sage. The determination he inspired in me to preserve my life takes away my agony even as a blazing flame of fire would dispel darkness. Nay, knowing as I did the virility of the evil-minded Rāvaṇa, my son was twitted by me in the following words : ‘Wherefore did you not rescue Sītā (the princess of Mithilā)?’ (I feel distressed to note that even) on hearing the wails of Sītā and on coming to know of the two princes (Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa) having been deprived of Sītā, that which would have conduced to my pleasure viz., an all out attempt to rescue her, was not done by my son, even though he was capable of doing it, which he ought to have done looking to my love for the late Emperor Daśaratha.” Even while Sampāti was speaking as aforesaid with the monkeys collected together, a pair of wings presently appeared on his sides in the presence of those dwellers of the forest. He experienced an ecstasy of delight, which was unequalled, on seeing his body covered by two newly grown wings with ruddy feathers, and spoke to the monkeys as follows : “By the grace of the royal sage Niśākara, who was possessed of immense spiritual power, my pair of wings, which had been completely burnt by the rays of the sun, have newly appeared. I find in me today the same prowess, strength and virility which existed in me when I was passing through my youth. Let an all out effort be made to trace out Sītā; you will surely be able to discover Sītā. (5—12)

verses.text:
पक्षलाभो ममायं वः सिद्धिप्रत्ययकारकः।
इत्युक्त्वा तान् हरीन् सर्वान् सम्पातिः पतगोत्तमः॥ १३॥
उत्पपात गिरेः शृङ्गाज्जिज्ञासुः खगमो गतिम्।
तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रतिसंहृष्टमानसाः।
बभूवुर्हरिशार्दूला विक्रमाभ्युदयोन्मुखाः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “This recovery of wings on my part is a pledge of your success.” Having spoken as aforesaid to all those monkeys, Sampāti, the foremost of birds, flew from the mountain-peak, keen as he was to see for himself once again how a bird flew. Highly pleased in mind in their turn to hear the foregoing words of Sampāti, those tigers among the monkeys became hopeful of their success, which depended on their valour. (13-14)

verses.text:
अथ पवनसमानविक्रमाः
प्लवगवराः प्रतिलब्धपौरुषाः।
अभिजिदभिमुखां दिशं ययु-
र्जनकसुतापरिमार्गणोन्मुखाः॥ १५॥
verses.m: Having regained their virility, which had been lost as a result of their frustration, the aforesaid leaders of monkeys, who were endowed with a speed equal to that of the wind, headed towards the southern quarter in which the constellation known by the name of Abhijit (a name associated by astrologers with triumph) appears foremost, keen as they were to trace out Sītā (daughter of King Janaka). (15)

verses.text:
आख्याता गृध्रराजेन समुत्प्लुत्य प्लवङ्गमाः।
संगताः प्रीतिसंयुक्ता विनेदुः सिंहविक्रमाः॥ १॥
verses.m: Leaping at full height in a body when enlightened by the king of vultures on the whereabouts of Sītā, the monkeys, who were all endowed with the prowess of a lion, thundered with joy. (1)

verses.text:
सम्पातेर्वचनं श्रुत्वा हरयो रावणक्षयम्।
हृष्टाः सागरमाजग्मुः सीतादर्शनकांक्षिणः॥ २॥
verses.m: Rejoiced to hear the words of Sampāti, the monkeys sought the ocean, constituting a passage to the abode of Rāvaṇa, keen as they were to discover Sītā. (2)

verses.text:
अभिगम्य तु तं देशं ददृशुर्भीमविक्रमाः।
कृत्स्नं लोकस्य महतः प्रतिबिम्बमवस्थितम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Approaching the aforesaid region (viz., the seashore), the monkeys, who were possessed of terrific prowess, beheld the ocean, in which there stood a full image of the vast steller region. (3)

verses.text:
दक्षिणस्य समुद्रस्य समासाद्योत्तरां दिशम्।
संनिवेशं ततश्चक्रुर्हरिवीरा महाबलाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: Duly reaching the northern end of the South Sea (the Indian Ocean), the monkey heroes, who were possessed of extraordinary might, halted there. (4)

verses.text:
प्रसुप्तमिव चान्यत्र क्रीडन्तमिव चान्यतः।
क्वचित् पर्वतमात्रैश्च जलराशिभिरावृतम्॥ ५॥
संकुलं दानवेन्द्रैश्च पातालतलवासिभिः।
रोमहर्षकरं दृष्ट्वा विषेदुः कपिकुञ्जराः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Those elephants among the monkeys felt despondent on seeing the ocean, which lay fast asleep as it were at one place, was sporting as it were at another and was covered at a third place with volumes of water as high as mountains, nay, which was thickly inhabited by the rulers of demons living in the depths of Pātāla (the seventh or nethermost subterranean region) and made one’s hair stand on end. (5-6)

verses.text:
आकाशमिव दुष्पारं सागरं प्रेक्ष्य वानराः।
विषेदुः सहिताः सर्वे कथं कार्यमिति ब्रुवन्॥ ७॥
verses.m: The monkeys felt dejected on perceiving the ocean, which was difficult to cross like the sky, and all exclaimed with one voice : “How will our purpose be achieved?” (7)

verses.text:
विषण्णां वाहिनीं दृष्ट्वा सागरस्य निरीक्षणात्।
आश्वासयामास हरीन् भयार्तान् हरिसत्तमः॥ ८॥
verses.m: Seeing the whole band of his followers despondent at the sight of the ocean, Aṅgada, the foremost of the monkeys, consoled as follows the monkeys, stricken as they were with fear : (8)

verses.text:
न विषादे मनः कार्यं विषादो दोषवत्तरः।
विषादो हन्ति पुरुषं बालं क्रुद्ध इवोरगः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Your mind should not be allowed to be swayed by despondency; for despondency is very harmful. The latter destroys a man as an angry serpent would kill an infant. (9)

verses.text:
यो विषादं प्रसहते विक्रमे समुपस्थिते।
तेजसा तस्य हीनस्य पुरुषार्थो न सिद्ध्यति॥ १०॥
verses.m: “The endeavour of a man, lacking in spirit, who falls a prey to despondency when an occasion for valour duly presents itself, does not bear fruit.” (10)

verses.text:
तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायामङ्गदो वानरैः सह।
हरिवृद्धैः समागम्य पुनर्मन्त्रममन्त्रयत्॥ ११॥
verses.m: Meeting the older among the monkeys when that night had passed, Aṅgada took counsel with them once more. (11)

verses.text:
सा वानराणां ध्वजिनी परिवार्याङ्गदं बभौ।
वासवं परिवार्येव मरुतां वाहिनी स्थिता॥ १२॥
verses.m: Surrounding Aṅgada on all sides, that monkey force shone like an army of gods standing round Indra. (12)

verses.text:
कोऽन्यस्तां वानरीं सेनां शक्तः स्तम्भयितुं भवेत्।
अन्यत्र वालितनयादन्यत्र च हनूमतः॥ १३॥
verses.m: Barring Aṅgada (the son of Vālī) and barring Hanūmān, who else would be able to hold that army of monkeys in check? (13)

verses.text:
ततस्तान् हरिवृद्धांश्च तच्च सैन्यमरिंदमः।
अनुमान्याङ्गदः श्रीमान् वाक्यमर्थवदब्रवीत्॥ १४॥
verses.m: Showing respect to those elderly monkeys as also to that army of monkeys, the glorious Aṅgada, the tamer of his foes, presently addressed to them the following significant words : (14)

verses.text:
क इदानीं महातेजा लङ्घयिष्यति सागरम्।
कः करिष्यति सुग्रीवं सत्यसंधमरिंदमम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “What monkey of extraordinary energy will take a leap across the sea at this juncture? Who will enable Sugrīva, the subduer of his foes, to prove himself to be true to his promise of wresting Sītā from the clutches of Rāvaṇa? (15)

verses.text:
को वीरो योजनशतं लङ्घयेत प्लवङ्गमः।
इमांश्च यूथपान् सर्वान् मोचयेत् को महाभयात्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “What heroic monkey can leap to a distance of a hundred Yojanas (or eight hundred miles)? Again, who will deliver all these leaders of monkey hordes from the great fear viz., that of incurring the wrath of Sugrīva? (16)

verses.text:
कस्य प्रसादाद् दारांश्च पुत्रांश्चैव गृहाणि च।
इतो निवृत्ताः पश्येम सिद्धार्थाः सुखिनो वयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “By whose good-will shall we be able to see, when returned accomplished of purpose and happy from this place, our wife as well as our sons and home? (17)

verses.text:
कस्य प्रसादाद् रामं च लक्ष्मणं च महाबलम्।
अभिगच्छेम संहृष्टाः सुग्रीवं च वनौकसम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “By whose grace shall we be able to meet Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, who are possessed of extraordinary might, and the monkey Sugrīva, and feel transported with joy? (18)

verses.text:
यदि कश्चित् समर्थो वः सागरप्लवने हरिः।
स ददात्विह नः शीघ्रं पुण्यामभयदक्षिणाम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “If any monkey among you is capable of leaping across the sea, let him quickly vouchsafe to us on this spot a holy boon in the shape of a vow to that effect, thereby ridding us of fear.” (19)

verses.text:
अङ्गदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा न कश्चित् किंचिदब्रवीत्।
स्तिमितेवाभवत् सर्वा सा तत्र हरिवाहिनी॥ २०॥
verses.m: Hearing the question of Aṅgada nobody said anything. The entire Vānara force stood motionless, as it were. (20)

verses.text:
पुनरेवाङ्गदः प्राह तान् हरीन् हरिसत्तमः।
सर्वे बलवतां श्रेष्ठा भवन्तो दृढविक्रमाः।
व्यपदेशकुले जाताः पूजिताश्चाप्यभीक्ष्णशः॥ २१॥
verses.m: Once more did Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys speak as follows to the aforesaid monkeys : “You are all pre-eminent among the mighty and endowed with unbending prowess. Born in a family free from all stigma, you have also been honoured time and again for your valour by the royal court. (21)

verses.text:
नहि वो गमने सङ्गः कदाचित् कस्यचिद् भवेत्।
ब्रुवध्वं यस्य या शक्तिः प्लवने प्लवगर्षभाः॥ २२॥
verses.m: “No obstruction is ever possible in the movement of any of you. Therefore, speak out, O leaders of monkeys, who can leap how far?” (22)

verses.text:
अथाङ्गदवचः श्रुत्वा ते सर्वे वानरर्षभाः।
स्वं स्वं गतौ समुत्साहमूचुस्तत्र यथाक्रमम्॥ १॥
गजो गवाक्षो गवयः शरभो गन्धमादनः।
मैन्दश्च द्विविदश्चैव सुषेणो जाम्बवांस्तथा॥ २॥
verses.m: Hearing the speech of Aṅgada all the aforesaid leaders of monkeys—Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha, Gandhamādana, Mainda and even so Dwivida, Suṣeṇa and Jāmbavān proclaimed in due succession each his own leaping capacity on that spot. (1-2)

verses.text:
आबभाषे गजस्तत्र प्लवेयं दशयोजनम्।
गवाक्षो योजनान्याह गमिष्यामीति विंशतिम्॥ ३॥
verses.m: Of them, Gaja said, “I can leap as far as ten Yojanas (or eighty miles);” while Gavākṣa said, “I shall be able to leap to a distance of twenty Yojanas (or one hundred and sixty miles).” (3)

verses.text:
शरभो वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह।
त्रिंशतं तु गमिष्यामि योजनानां प्लवङ्गमाः॥ ४॥
verses.m: The monkey Śarabha, they say, said to those monkeys on that occassion, “I shall cover in one leap thirty Yojanas (or two hundred and forty miles), O monkeys !” (4)

verses.text:
ऋषभो वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह।
चत्वारिंशद् गमिष्यामि योजनानां न संशयः॥ ५॥
verses.m: The monkey Ṛṣabha, it is said, spoke to the monkeys on that spot as follows : “I shall cover in one leap forty Yojanas (or three hundred and twenty miles); there is no doubt about it.” (5)

verses.text:
वानरांस्तु महातेजा अब्रवीद् गन्धमादनः।
योजनानां गमिष्यामि पञ्चाशत्तु न संशयः॥ ६॥
verses.m: Gandhamādana for his part, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, spoke, they say, to the monkeys as follows : “I for my part shall cover in a leap fifty Yojanas (or four hundred miles): there is no doubt about it.” (6)

verses.text:
मैन्दस्तु वानरस्तत्र वानरांस्तानुवाच ह।
योजनानां परं षष्टिमहं प्लवितुमुत्सहे॥ ७॥
verses.m: The monkey Mainda for his part, they say, said to the monkeys on that spot, “I can leap at the utmost sixty Yojanas (or four hundred and eighty miles).” (7)

verses.text:
ततस्तत्र महातेजा द्विविदः प्रत्यभाषत।
गमिष्यामि न संदेहः सप्ततिं योजनान्यहम्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Dwivida, who was endowed with extraordinary energy, then said on that occassion, “I shall cover seventy Yojanas (or five hundred and sixty miles): there is no doubt about it.” (8)

verses.text:
सुषेणस्तु महातेजाः सत्त्ववान् कपिसत्तमः।
अशीतिं प्रतिजानेऽहं योजनानां पराक्रमे॥ ९॥
verses.m: The foremost of monkeys, Suṣeṇa, for his part, who was endowed with extraordinary energy and full of courage, said, “I solemnly declare that I can leap eighty Yojanas (or six hundred and forty miles).” (9)

verses.text:
तेषां कथयतां तत्र सर्वांस्ताननुमान्य च।
ततो वृद्धतमस्तेषां जाम्बवान् प्रत्यभाषत॥ १०॥
verses.m: Showing respect to them all, while they were speaking on that spot, Jāmbavān, the oldest of them all, then submitted as follows : (10)

verses.text:
पूर्वमस्माकमप्यासीत् कश्चिद् गतिपराक्रमः।
ते वयं वयसः पारमनुप्राप्ताः स्म साम्प्रतम्॥ ११॥
verses.m: “Formerly we too had some leaping capacity. Now, of course, we have reached the fag-end of our life. (11)

verses.text:
किं तु नैवं गते शक्यमिदं कार्यमुपेक्षितुम्।
यदर्थं कपिराजश्च रामश्च कृतनिश्चयौ॥ १२॥
साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं या गतिस्तां निबोधत।
नवतिं योजनानां तु गमिष्यामि न संशयः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Even in such circumstances, however, the work in hand, which Sugrīva (the king of monkeys) and Śrī Rāma too are determined to carry through, can on no account be neglected. Please hear of the leaping capacity which now exists in me: I shall certainly cover in one leap ninety Yojanas (or seven hundred and twenty miles): there is no doubt about it.” (12-13)

verses.text:
तांश्च सर्वान् हरिश्रेष्ठाञ्जाम्बवानिदमब्रवीत्।
न खल्वेतावदेवासीद् गमने मे पराक्रमः॥ १४॥
verses.m: Nay, Jāmbavān spoke as follows to all those jewels among the monkeys : “Surely, I did not have only this much leaping capacity in the past. (14)

verses.text:
मया वैरोचने यज्ञे प्रभविष्णुः सनातनः।
प्रदक्षिणीकृतः पूर्वं क्रममाणस्त्रिविक्रमम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “At the well-known sacrifice performed by King Bali (the son of Virocana) in the former days, the all-pervading and immortal Lord Trivikrama (who measured the whole universe in three strides) was gone round clockwise by me while taking His strides over the universe. (15)

verses.text:
स इदानीमहं वृद्धः प्लवने मन्दविक्रमः।
यौवने च तदासीन्मे बलमप्रतिमं परम्॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Having grown old I, whose surpassing strength in youth was unequalled, have now become tardy of movement in leaping. (16)

verses.text:
सम्प्रत्येतावदेवाद्य शक्यं मे गमने स्वतः।
नैतावता च संसिद्धिः कार्यस्यास्य भविष्यति॥ १७॥
verses.m: “This much only is my capacity in leaping unaided today and at this moment. The success of this undertaking of ours is, however, out of the question with this much capacity.” (17)

verses.text:
अथोत्तरमुदारार्थमब्रवीदङ्गदस्तदा।
अनुमान्य तदा प्राज्ञो जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः॥ १८॥
verses.m: Showing respect to Jāmbavān at that moment, the wise Aṅgada, the mighty monkey, forthwith made on that occasion the following reply, which bore a noble import : (18)

verses.text:
अहमेतद् गमिष्यामि योजनानां शतं महत्।
निवर्तने तु मे शक्तिः स्यान्न वेति न निश्चितम्॥ १९॥
verses.m: “I shall surely cover these hundred long Yojanas (or eight hundred miles), but it is not certain whether I shall be able to return or not.” (19)

verses.text:
तमुवाच हरिश्रेष्ठं जाम्बवान् वाक्यकोविदः।
ज्ञायते गमने शक्तिस्तव हर्यृक्षसत्तम॥ २०॥
verses.m: To Aṅgada, the foremost of monkeys, Jāmbavān, who was a master of expression, submitted as follows : “Your power of movement is known to us, O jewel among the monkeys and bears ! (20)

verses.text:
कामं शतसहस्रं वा नह्येष विधिरुच्यते।
योजनानां भवाञ्शक्तो गन्तुं प्रतिनिवर्तितुम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: “Nay, you may easily be able to leap a hundred or (even) a thousand Yojanas and come back. Surely, however, this is not said to be the rule. (21)

verses.text:
नहि प्रेषयिता तात स्वामी प्रेष्यः कथंचन।
भवतायं जनः सर्वः प्रेष्यः प्लवगसत्तम॥ २२॥
verses.m: “A master, O dear Aṅgada, who sends or directs an expedition, can under no circumstance be worthy of being directed or sent on an expedition. On the other hand, we all deserve to be directed or sent on an errand by you, O jewel among the monkeys ! (22)

verses.text:
भवान् कलत्रमस्माकं स्वामिभावे व्यवस्थितः।
स्वामी कलत्रं सैन्यस्य गतिरेषा परंतप॥ २३॥
verses.m: “You deserve to be protected by us even like the mistress of a household, installed as you are in the position of our master. The ruler of an army deserves to be protected (like the mistress of a household): such is the rule, O scourge of your foes ! (23)

verses.text:
अपि वै तस्य कार्यस्य भवान् मूलमरिंदम।
तस्मात् कलत्रवत् तात प्रतिपाल्यः सदा भवान्॥ २४॥
verses.m: “Moreover you are the very basis of the work in hand to us viz., the discovery of Sītā, O tamer of your foes ! Hence, O dear child, you deserve to be protected by us like a housewife at all times. (24)

verses.text:
मूलमर्थस्य संरक्ष्यमेष कार्यविदां नयः।
मूले हि सति सिध्यन्ति गुणाः सर्वे फलोदयाः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “The root of a thing must be carefully preserved: this is the maxim of those knowing their business. Only so long as the root is there all excellences (which are only of secondary importance) bear fruit. (25)

verses.text:
तद् भवानस्य कार्यस्य साधनं सत्यविक्रम।
बुद्धिविक्रमसम्पन्नो हेतुरत्र परंतप॥ २६॥
verses.m: “Therefore you are the means of accomplishing this work, O prince of unfailing prowess, and a key to it, richly endowed as you are with wisdom and valour, O scourge of your foes ! (26)

verses.text:
गुरुश्च गुरुपुत्रश्च त्वं हि नः कपिसत्तम।
भवन्तमाश्रित्य वयं समर्था ह्यर्थसाधने॥ २७॥
verses.m: “You are our superior and the son of our superior. Banking on you we shall really be able to accomplish our end, O jewel among the monkeys !” (27)

verses.text:
उक्तवाक्यं महाप्राज्ञं जाम्बवन्तं महाकपिः।
प्रत्युवाचोत्तरं वाक्यं वालिसूनुरथाङ्गदः॥ २८॥
verses.m: To the highly intelligent Jāmbavān, who had spoken as above, the great monkey, Aṅgada, the son of Vālī, now addressed the following reply : (28)

verses.text:
यदि नाहं गमिष्यामि नान्यो वानरपुङ्गवः।
पुनः खल्विदमस्माभिः कार्यं प्रायोपवेशनम्॥ २९॥
verses.m: “If I do not stir nor does any other leader of the monkeys, fasting till death must surely be undertaken by us again. (29)

verses.text:
नह्यकृत्वा हरिपतेः संदेशं तस्य धीमतः।
तत्रापि गत्वा प्राणानां न पश्ये परिरक्षणम्॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Having failed to carry out the instructions of that wise ruler of monkeys, I do not see any hope of preserving our life even after going there. (30)

verses.text:
स हि प्रसादे चात्यर्थकोपे च हरिरीश्वरः।
अतीत्य तस्य संदेशं विनाशो गमने भवेत्॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “That monkey, Sugrīva, has certainly the absolute power to show clemency or give vent to his extreme anger towards us. Death is bound to follow if we depart for Kiṣkindhā without carrying out his instructions. (31)

verses.text:
तत्तथा ह्यस्य कार्यस्य न भवत्यन्यथा गतिः।
तद् भवानेव दृष्टार्थः संचिन्तयितुमर्हति॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “Therefore, you alone, who have perceived the truth of everything, should devise some means to see that this purpose of ours in the shape of discovery of Sītā does not actually get frustrated.” (32)

verses.text:
सोऽङ्गदेन तदा वीरः प्रत्युक्तः प्लवगर्षभः।
जाम्बवानुत्तमं वाक्यं प्रोवाचेदं ततोऽङ्गदम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: In response to these words of Aṅgada at that juncture, the celebrated and heroic Jāmbavān, a jewel among the monkeys and bears, now addressed the following excellent rejoinder to Aṅgada : (33)

verses.text:
तस्य ते वीर कार्यस्य न किंचित् परिहास्यते।
एष संचोदयाम्येनं यः कार्यं साधयिष्यति॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “Not an iota of your aforementioned purpose will be balked, O gallant prince ! I now make an appeal to one who will surely accomplish our purpose.” (34)

verses.text:
ततः प्रतीतं प्लवतां वरिष्ठ-
मेकान्तमाश्रित्य सुखोपविष्टम्।
संचोदयामास हरिप्रवीरो
हरिप्रवीरं हनुमन्तमेव॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Thereupon Jāmbavān, a prominent hero among the monkeys and bears, made an appeal to none else than the celebrated Hanumān, another prominent hero of the monkey race, the foremost of monkeys, who was sitting at ease apart. (35)

verses.text:
अनेकशतसाहस्रीं विषण्णां हरिवाहिनीम्।
जाम्बवान् समुदीक्ष्यैवं हनूमन्तमथाब्रवीत्॥ १॥
verses.m: Perceiving the monkey force, which was many lakhs strong, despondent, Jāmbavān presently spoke to Hanumān as follows :(1)

verses.text:
वीर वानरलोकस्य सर्वशास्त्रविदां वर।
तूष्णीमेकान्तमाश्रित्य हनूमन् किं न जल्पसि॥ २॥
verses.m: “Sitting quietly apart, O hero of the Vānara kingdom, O jewel among those well-versed in all the scriptures, why don’t you speak, O Hanumān ! (2)

verses.text:
हनूमन्हरिराजस्य सुग्रीवस्य समो ह्यसि।
रामलक्ष्मणयोश्चापि तेजसा च बलेन च॥ ३॥
verses.m: “Indeed you are a compeer, O Hanumān, of Sugrīva, the ruler of all monkeys, nay, even of Śrī Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa in point of valour and might. (3)

verses.text:
अरिष्टनेमिनः पुत्रो वैनतेयो महाबलः।
गरुत्मानिव विख्यात उत्तमः सर्वपक्षिणाम्॥ ४॥
verses.m: “You are as widely known as Garuḍa, son of Ariṣṭanemi (Sage Kaśyapa) through Vinatā, and the foremost of all winged creatures, who is possessed of extraordinary strength. (4)

verses.text:
बहुशो हि मया दृष्टः सागरे स महाबलः।
भुजङ्गानुद्धरन् पक्षी महाबाहुर्महाबलः॥ ५॥
verses.m: “That bird, Garuḍa, of mighty arms and possessed of extraordinary strength and courage has actually been seen by me on many an occasion picking up huge serpents at sea. (5)

verses.text:
पक्षयोर्यद् बलं तस्य भुजवीर्यबलं तव।
विक्रमश्चापि वेगश्च न ते तेनापहीयते॥ ६॥
verses.m: “The strength which inheres in his wings and the power and strength of your arms are equal. Your prowess and energy too are in no way inferior to his (Garuḍa’s). (6)

verses.text:
बलं बुद्धिश्च तेजश्च सत्त्वं च हरिपुङ्गव।
विशिष्टं सर्वभूतेषु किमात्मानं न सज्जसे॥ ७॥
verses.m: “Your strength and wisdom, energy and courage too, O bull among the monkeys, distinguish you from all other created beings. Why then do you not make yourself ready for the adventure? (7)

verses.text:
अप्सराऽप्सरसां श्रेष्ठा विख्याता पुञ्जिकस्थला।
अञ्जनेति परिख्याता पत्नी केसरिणो हरेः॥ ८॥
विख्याता त्रिषु लोकेषु रूपेणाप्रतिमा भुवि।
अभिशापादभूत् तात कपित्वे कामरूपिणी॥ ९॥
दुहिता वानरेन्द्रस्य कुञ्जरस्य महात्मनः।
मानुषं विग्रहं कृत्वा रूपयौवनशालिनी॥ १०॥
विचित्रमाल्याभरणा कदाचित् क्षौमधारिणी।
अचरत् पर्वतस्याग्रे प्रावृडम्बुदसंनिभे॥ ११॥
verses.m: “There was a celestial nymph, the foremost of all celestial nymphs and widely known by the name of Puñjikasthalā. Due to a curse pronounced by a Ṛṣi, she was reborn as a daughter of the high-souled Kuñjara, a monkey chief, and became widely known as Añjanā. She came to be the wife of a monkey, Kesarī by name. She was celebrated in all the three worlds and was unparalleled on earth in beauty. Though living in the form of a monkey she could change her form at will. Having assumed a human form, Añjanā, who looked charming due to her comeliness and youth, was decked with wonderful ornaments of flowers and was clad in silk, was once roving on a mountain-peak, which looked like a rainy cloud. (8—11)

verses.text:
तस्या वस्त्रं विशालाक्ष्याः पीतं रक्तदशं शुभम्।
स्थितायाः पर्वतस्याग्रे मारुतोऽपाहरच्छनैः॥ १२॥
verses.m: “The wind-god gently removed the charming red-bordered yellow covering of that large-eyed belle standing on the mountain-top. (12)

verses.text:
स ददर्श ततस्तस्या वृत्तावूरू सुसंहतौ।
स्तनौ च पीनौ सहितौ सुजातं चारु चाननम्॥ १३॥
verses.m: “He thereupon perceived her rounded and closely united thighs and well-knit swelling breasts as well as her shapely and lovely countenance. (13)

verses.text:
तां बलादायतश्रोणीं तनुमध्यां यशस्विनीम्।
दृष्ट्वैव शुभसर्वाङ्गीं पवनः काममोहितः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “The wind-god got infatuated through love in spite of himself the moment he saw that glorious woman with broad hips, slender of waist and charming of every limb. (14)

verses.text:
स तां भुजाभ्यां दीर्घाभ्यां पर्यष्वजत मारुतः।
मन्मथाविष्टसर्वाङ्गो गतात्मा तामनिन्दिताम्॥ १५॥
verses.m: “The wind-god, whose mind was set on her and all whose limbs were possessed by love, pressed to his bosom that irreproachable girl with his long arms. (15)

verses.text:
सा तु तत्रैव सम्भ्रान्ता सुव्रता वाक्यमब्रवीत्।
एकपत्नीव्रतमिदं को नाशयितुमिच्छति॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Utterly confused, that lady of noble vows, for her part, spoke that very moment as follows : ‘Who seeks to violate this vow of mine of fidelity to a single husband?’ (16)

verses.text:
अञ्जनाया वचः श्रुत्वा मारुतः प्रत्यभाषत।
न त्वां हिंसामि सुश्रोणि मा भूत् ते मनसो भयम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “Hearing the question of Añjanā, the wind-god replied, ‘I am not going to violate you, O lady of charming limbs ! Let there be no fear in your mind. (17)

verses.text:
मनसास्मि गतो यत् त्वां परिष्वज्य यशस्विनि।
वीर्यवान् बुद्धिसम्पन्नस्तव पुत्रो भविष्यति॥ १८॥
verses.m: “ ‘Since after embracing you I have entered your being with my mind, O illustrious lady, a son who is powerful and richly endowed with intelligence will be born to you. (18)

verses.text:
महासत्त्वो महातेजा महाबलपराक्रमः।
लङ्घने प्लवने चैव भविष्यति मया समः॥ १९॥
verses.m: “ ‘Full of extraordinary courage, extraordinary energy and extraordinary strength and prowess, he will prove to be my equal in jumping and leaping.’ (19)

verses.text:
एवमुक्ता ततस्तुष्टा जननी ते महाकपे।
गुहायां त्वां महाबाहो प्रजज्ञे प्लवगर्षभ॥ २०॥
verses.m: “Satisfied when spoken to in these words, your mother, O great and mighty-armed monkey, gave birth to you in a cave, O jewel among the monkeys! (20)

verses.text:
अभ्युत्थितं ततः सूर्यं बालो दृष्ट्वा महावने।
फलं चेति जिघृक्षुस्त्वमुत्प्लुत्याभ्युत्पतो दिवम्॥ २१॥
verses.m: Seeing the sun just risen in an extensive forest while you were still a child, and bounding with intent to have it, taking it to be a fruit, you rose to the sky. (21)

verses.text:
शतानि त्रीणि गत्वाथ योजनानां महाकपे।
तेजसा तस्य निर्धूतो न विषादं गतस्ततः॥ २२॥
verses.m: Having sprung to an altitude of over three thousand Yojanas* (or twenty-four thousand miles), O great monkey, you were repulsed by the brilliance of the sun but did not meet with despondency on that account. (22)

verses.text:
त्वामप्युपगतं तूर्णमन्तरिक्षं महाकपे।
क्षिप्तमिन्द्रेण ते वज्रं कोपाविष्टेन तेजसा॥ २३॥
तदा शैलाग्रशिखरे वामो हनुरभज्यत।
ततो हि नामधेयं ते हनुमानिति कीर्तितम्॥ २४॥
verses.m: Seeing you risen to the sky in no time even on being repulsed, O great monkey, Indra hurled his thunderbolt with violence at you, possessed as he was with anger, dashing you against the foremost summit of a mountain, with the result that the left side of your chin got immediately fractured. From that time onward your name became current as Hanumān (one with a broken or defective chin). (23-24)

verses.text:
ततस्त्वां निहतं दृष्ट्वा वायुर्गन्धवहः स्वयम्।
त्रैलोक्यं भृशसंक्रुद्धो न ववौ वै प्रभञ्जनः॥ २५॥
verses.m: “Seeing you badly hurt, the wind-god, the wafer of odour, himself felt extremely enraged and the wind now ceased to visit the three worlds. (25)

verses.text:
सम्भ्रान्ताश्च सुराः सर्वे त्रैलोक्ये क्षुभिते सति।
प्रसादयन्ति संक्रुद्धं मारुतं भुवनेश्वराः॥ २६॥
verses.m: “All the three worlds being agitated for want of air, all the gods felt perplexed. The rulers of the worlds, Brahmā and others, proceeded to pacify the infuriated wind-god. (26)

verses.text:
प्रसादिते च पवने ब्रह्मा तुभ्यं वरं ददौ।
अशस्त्रवध्यतां तात समरे सत्यविक्रम॥ २७॥
verses.m: “The wind-god being placated, Brahmā granted in your favour a boon in the form of invulnerability in combat, O dear child of unfailing prowess ! (27)

verses.text:
वज्रस्य च निपातेन विरुजं त्वां समीक्ष्य च।
सहस्रनेत्रः प्रीतात्मा ददौ ते वरमुत्तमम्॥ २८॥
स्वच्छन्दतश्च मरणं तव स्यादिति वै प्रभो।
स त्वं केसरिणः पुत्रः क्षेत्रजो भीमविक्रमः॥ २९॥
मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तेजसा चापि तत्समः।
त्वं हि वायुसुतो वत्स प्लवने चापि तत्समः॥ ३०॥
verses.m: “Pleased at heart to observe you free from anguish despite the impact of the thunderbolt and notwithstanding your being dashed against a mountain-peak, Indra (the thousand-eyed god) too conferred another excellent boon on you to the effect that death will come to you only when you wish to die, O powerful monkey ! In this way you are, on the one hand, the son of Kesarī, begotten through his wife, and by another, are endowed with terrible prowess. Again, sprung as you are from the loins of the wind-god, you are his equal in energy. Indeed, being a son of the wind-god, you are his equal even in leaping. (28—30)

verses.text:
वयमद्य गतप्राणा भवानस्मासु साम्प्रतम्।
दाक्ष्यविक्रमसम्पन्नः कपिराज इवापरः॥ ३१॥
verses.m: “Our vitality has now all but gone. You alone amongst us are endowed with skill and prowess and are another Sugrīva, the ruler of monkeys, as it were. (31)

verses.text:
त्रिविक्रमे मया तात सशैलवनकानना।
त्रिःसप्तकृत्वः पृथिवी परिक्रान्ता प्रदक्षिणम्॥ ३२॥
verses.m: “During the descent of the Lord as Trivikrama (who measured the entire universe in three strides), O dear child, the entire globe with its mountains, forests and woodlands was gone round clockwise by me as many as one and twenty times. (32)

verses.text:
तथा चौषधयोऽस्माभिः संचिता देवशासनात्।
निर्मथ्यममृतं याभिस्तदानीं नो महद्बलम्॥ ३३॥
verses.m: “Nay, that time, in obedience to the command of the gods, the herbs with the help of which nectar was to be churned out of the ocean of milk were gathered by me single-handed, since at that time extraordinary strength existed in me. (33)

verses.text:
स इदानीमहं वृद्धः परिहीनपराक्रमः।
साम्प्रतं कालमस्माकं भवान् सर्वगुणान्वितः॥ ३४॥
verses.m: “I am now old and destitute of prowess. You alone amongst us are endowed with all virtues at the present moment. (34)

verses.text:
तद् विजृम्भस्व विक्रान्त प्लवतामुत्तमो ह्यसि।
त्वद्वीर्यं द्रष्टुकामा हि सर्वा वानरवाहिनी॥ ३५॥
verses.m: Therefore exhibit your immense strength, O hero, since you are the foremost of monkeys. Indeed the entire Vānara force is keen to witness your virility. (35)

verses.text:
उत्तिष्ठ हरिशार्दूल लङ्घयस्व महार्णवम्।
परा हि सर्वभूतानां हनुमन् या गतिस्तव॥ ३६॥
verses.m: “Get up, O tiger among the monkeys, and leap over the vast sea; for the leaping capacity that exists in you, O Hanumān, is greater than that of all other created beings. (36)

verses.text:
विषण्णा हरयः सर्वे हनुमन् किमुपेक्षसे।
विक्रमस्व महावेग विष्णुस्त्रीन् विक्रमानिव॥ ३७॥
verses.m: “All the monkeys have grown despondent, O Hanumān ! How do you ignore them? Show your courage, O monkey of extraordinary speed, as did Lord Viṣṇu in His descent as Trivikrama take three strides in order to measure the universe.” (37)

verses.text:
ततः कपीनामृषभेण चोदितः
प्रतीतवेगः पवनात्मजः कपिः।
प्रहर्षयंस्तां हरिवीरवाहिनीं
चकार रूपं महदात्मनस्तदा॥ ३८॥
verses.m: Encouraged by Jāmbavān, the foremost of monkeys and bears, and convinced of his capacity for vigorous action, the monkey chief, Hanumān, son of the wind-god, now expanded his form that very moment, thereby bringing excessive joy to that army of monkey heroes. (38)

verses.text:
तं दृष्ट्वा जृम्भमाणं ते क्रमितुं शतयोजनम्।
वेगेनापूर्यमाणं च सहसा वानरोत्तमम्॥ १॥
सहसा शोकमुत्सृज्य प्रहर्षेण समन्विताः।
विनेदुस्तुष्टुवुश्चापि हनूमन्तं महाबलम्॥ २॥
verses.m: Shaking off grief all at once on seeing Hanumān, the foremost of monkeys, expanding his form with a view to leaping over a hundred Yojanas, and being filled with dash, the monkeys full of excessive joy, thundered and also glorified Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary might. (1-2)

verses.text:
प्रहृष्टा विस्मिताश्चापि ते वीक्षन्ते समन्ततः।
त्रिविक्रमं कृतोत्साहं नारायणमिव प्रजाः॥ ३॥
verses.m: Standing around him highly rejoiced and amazed too, they gazed on him even as all created beings looked on Lord Nārāyaṇa (Viṣṇu) when he had made a resolve to measure the entire cosmos in His descent as Trivikrama. (3)

verses.text:
संस्तूयमानो हनुमान् व्यवर्धत महाबलः।
समाविद्ध्य च लाङ्गूलं हर्षाद् बलमुपेयिवान्॥ ४॥
verses.m: Hanumān, who was endowed with extraordinary strength, grew considerably in size even while he was being acclaimed and, whirling his tail with delight, recollected his native strength. (4)

verses.text:
तस्य संस्तूयमानस्य वृद्धैर्वानरपुङ्गवैः।
तेजसाऽऽपूर्यमाणस्य रूपमासीदनुत्तमम्॥ ५॥
verses.m: While he was being duly acclaimed by the foremost of monkeys, who were all senior in age, and while he was getting recharged with energy, his form looked surpassingly excellent. (5)

verses.text:
यथा विजृम्भते सिंहो विवृते गिरिगह्वरे।
मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रस्तथा सम्प्रति जृम्भते॥ ६॥
verses.m: Even as a lion stretches his limbs in a commodious mountain-cave, Hanumān (sprung from the loins of the wind-god) now yawned and expanded his form likewise. (6)

verses.text:
अशोभत मुखं तस्य जृम्भमाणस्य धीमतः।
अम्बरीषोपमं दीप्तं विधूम इव पावकः॥ ७॥
verses.m: While Hanumān, the wise one, was yawning, his mouth looked bright like a lighted oven or a smokeless fire. (7)

verses.text:
हरीणामुत्थितो मध्यात् सम्प्रहृष्टतनूरुहः।
अभिवाद्य हरीन् वृद्धान् हनूमानिदमब्रवीत्॥ ८॥
verses.m: Risen from the midst of monkeys, his hair standing on end through excessive joy, and greeting the older monkeys, Hanumān spoke as follows : (8)

verses.text:
आरुजन् पर्वताग्राणि हुताशनसखोऽनिलः।
बलवानप्रमेयश्च वायुराकाशगोचरः॥ ९॥
verses.m: “Circulating in space in the form of the wind and shattering mountain-peaks, the wind-god, a friend of fire, is mighty and beyond measure. (9)

verses.text:
तस्याहं शीघ्रवेगस्य शीघ्रगस्य महात्मनः।
मारुतस्यौरसः पुत्रः प्लवनेनास्मि तत्समः॥ १०॥
verses.m: “I claim my descent from the loins of that high-souled wind-god of rapid speed and swift movement, and am his equal in leaping. (10)

verses.text:
उत्सहेयं हि विस्तीर्णमालिखन्तमिवाम्बरम्।
मेरुं गिरिमसङ्गेन परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः॥ ११॥
verses.m: “I can actually circumambulate a thousand times without pause the extensive Mount Meru, which stands scratching the firmament, as it were. (11)

verses.text:
बाहुवेगप्रणुन्नेन सागरेणाहमुत्सहे।
समाप्लावयितुं लोकं सपर्वतनदीह्रदम्॥ १२॥
verses.m: “With the ocean pushed away by the might of my arms, I can fully deluge the world including its mountains, rivers and lakes. (12)

verses.text:
ममोरुजङ्घावेगेन भविष्यति समुत्थितः।
समुत्थितमहाग्राहः समुद्रो वरुणालयः॥ १३॥
verses.m: “Stirred by the force of my thighs and shanks, the ocean, which is the abode of Varuṇa, will begin to overflow, bringing its huge alligators to the surface. (13)

verses.text:
पन्नगाशनमाकाशे पतन्तं पक्षिसेवितम्।
वैनतेयमहं शक्तः परिगन्तुं सहस्रशः॥ १४॥
verses.m: “I am capable of going clockwise a thousand times round Garuḍa (son of Vinatā), who feeds on serpents and is waited upon by birds (whose ruler he is), while he is coursing through the sky. (14)

verses.text:
उदयात् प्रस्थितं वापि ज्वलन्तं रश्मिमालिनम्।
अनस्तमितमादित्यमहं गन्तुं समुत्सहे॥ १५॥
verses.m: “I am fully capable of overtaking the blazing sun with its aureole of rays set out from the eastern mountain before it disappears behind the western mountain. (15)

verses.text:
ततो भूमिमसंस्पृष्ट्वा पुनरागन्तुमुत्सहे।
प्रवेगेनैव महता भीमेन प्लवगर्षभाः॥ १६॥
verses.m: “Then I can even come back to the earth and return to the sun before it sets with the same high and terrific rapid speed without standing on the earth for respite, O jewels among the monkeys ! (16)

verses.text:
उत्सहेयमतिक्रान्तुं सर्वानाकाशगोचरान्।
सागरान् शोषयिष्यामि दारयिष्यामि मेदिनीम्॥ १७॥
verses.m: “I can leave behind in a race all the luminaries coursing in the heavens and can dry up the oceans and rend the earth. (17)

verses.text:
पर्वतांश्चूर्णयिष्यामि प्लवमानः प्लवङ्गमः।
हरिष्याम्युरुवेगेन प्लवमानो महार्णवम्॥ १८॥
verses.m: “I can crush mountains while jumping on them, a monkey (lit., one who goes leaping) as I am. Nay, leaping with great speed I can reach the end of an ocean to say nothing of the sea dividing the Indian shore from Laṅkā. (18)

verses.text:
लतानां विविधं पुष्पं पादपानां च सर्वशः।
अनुयास्यति मामद्य प्लवमानं विहायसा॥ १९॥
